sec15-card-sec15-F039.memory_hook: Watch signals, give wide blind-spot room
sec15-card-sec15-F039.expected_back: Watch truck turn signals and allow enough space for the truck to maneuver without moving into its blind spots.

sec17-card-sec17-F001.front: Which five vehicle items should you inspect at least once a month for safety maintenance?
sec17-card-sec17-F001.memory_hook: Monthly tread, pressure, lights, wipers, fluids
sec17-card-sec17-F001.expected_back: The handbook recommends checking tire tread, tire pressure, brake lights, wipers and fluids at least monthly as part of vehicle safety maintenance.

sec17-card-sec17-F002.front: How do you perform the penny tread test, and what result shows the tires need replacement?
sec17-card-sec17-F002.memory_hook: Full Lincoln head visible means replace
sec17-card-sec17-F002.expected_back: To check tread with a penny, insert Lincoln's head into the deepest-looking tread groove; if the entire head is visible, the handbook says the tires are too worn to drive on and need replacement.

sec17-card-sec17-F003.front: How should you measure tire pressure, and where is the target pressure printed?
sec17-card-sec17-F003.memory_hook: Use a gauge against door-jamb specs
sec17-card-sec17-F003.expected_back: Use a tire-pressure gauge and compare its reading with the pressure specified on the door-jamb label rather than guessing by appearance.

sec17-card-sec17-F004.front: At what tire temperature should pressure be checked, and what if the reading is too high?
sec17-card-sec17-F004.memory_hook: Check cold tires, bleed excess air
sec17-card-sec17-F004.expected_back: Check tire pressure when the tires are cold, and release air if the reading exceeds the specified pressure.

sec17-card-sec17-F005.front: What two-person method does the handbook describe for checking brake lights?
sec17-card-sec17-F005.memory_hook: Helper watches rear while pressing pedal
sec17-card-sec17-F005.expected_back: To check brake lights, have another person watch behind the vehicle while the driver presses the brake pedal and confirm both lights operate.

sec17-card-sec17-F006.front: Which two parts commonly cause a dead brake light, and what if you cannot fix it yourself?
sec17-card-sec17-F006.memory_hook: Replace bulb or fuse, get pro
sec17-card-sec17-F006.expected_back: A brake light that does not work may require a bulb or fuse replacement; seek professional help if you do not know how to repair it.

sec17-card-sec17-F007.front: How often does the handbook advise replacing wiper blades across hot, cold, sunny, or dry climates?
sec17-card-sec17-F007.memory_hook: Yearly normally, twice yearly dry climates
sec17-card-sec17-F007.expected_back: Replace wiper blades periodically to preserve visibility; the handbook recommends at least annually in hot, sunny or cold climates and twice annually in dusty or dry climates.

sec17-card-sec17-F008.front: What simple cleaning step helps keep windshield wiper blades wiping cleanly?
sec17-card-sec17-F008.memory_hook: Wipe blades with rag or alcohol
sec17-card-sec17-F008.expected_back: Periodically wiping wiper blades with a rag or alcohol wipe helps maintain their performance.

sec17-card-sec17-F009.front: What four-step sequence gives an accurate engine-oil reading on the dipstick?
sec17-card-sec17-F009.memory_hook: Pull, wipe, fully reinsert, read film
sec17-card-sec17-F009.expected_back: To check engine oil, remove the dipstick, wipe it clean, fully reinsert it and pull it out again to read the oil film against its markings.

sec17-card-sec17-F010.front: When should you add engine oil, and where do you find the right oil-change schedule?
sec17-card-sec17-F010.memory_hook: Add below mark, follow owner's manual
sec17-card-sec17-F010.expected_back: Add oil when the dipstick reading is below the marked level, and use the vehicle manual to determine oil-change intervals.

sec17-card-sec17-F011.front: How do you inspect and top off engine coolant safely?
sec17-card-sec17-F011.memory_hook: Check reservoir mark, add manual's mix
sec17-card-sec17-F011.expected_back: Check the coolant reservoir level against its minimum fill mark and add the coolant-and-water mixture specified by the vehicle manual when needed.

sec17-card-sec17-F012.front: Why must you never open a radiator cap while the engine is hot?
sec17-card-sec17-F012.expected_back: Never open the radiator cap while the vehicle is hot; wait until the vehicle cools.

sec17-card-sec17-F013.front: What two roadside problems can result from hauling an uncovered or unsecured load?
sec17-card-sec17-F013.memory_hook: Creates roadside litter and road hazards
sec17-card-sec17-F013.expected_back: An uncovered or unsecured load can contribute to roadside litter and create a road hazard for other drivers.

sec17-card-sec17-F014.front: Is driving on Alaska roadways with an unsecured load legal?
sec17-card-sec17-F014.memory_hook: Driving with unsecured loads is illegal
sec17-card-sec17-F014.expected_back: Traveling on Alaska roads with an unsecured load is illegal.

sec17-card-sec17-F015.front: What maximum dollar fine and jail term can apply to littering in Alaska?
sec17-card-sec17-F015.memory_hook: Up to thousand dollars, ninety days
sec17-card-sec17-F015.expected_back: The handbook states that littering can bring a fine of up to one thousand dollars and as much as ninety days of imprisonment.

sec17-card-sec17-F016.front: Besides fines and jail, what cleanup duty may a court order for a littering offender?
sec17-card-sec17-F016.memory_hook: Court-ordered litter pickup in set areas
sec17-card-sec17-F016.expected_back: A court may also order a littering offender to collect litter for a specified period in a specified area.

sec18-card-sec18-F001.front: How does the Alaska handbook classify driving, and what does that place on every motorist?
sec18-card-sec18-F001.memory_hook: Driving is privilege, never unrestricted right
sec18-card-sec18-F001.expected_back: The handbook describes driving as a privilege rather than an unrestricted right, placing responsibility on each person who operates a vehicle.

sec18-card-sec18-F002.front: How do the handbook's closing safety reminders treat using a cell phone behind the wheel?
sec18-card-sec18-F002.memory_hook: Cell phones distract and trigger crashes
sec18-card-sec18-F002.expected_back: Using a cell phone while driving is among the distracting activities that can contribute to a crash, according to the handbook's closing safety reminders.

sec18-card-sec18-F003.front: Why do the closing safety reminders warn against eating, grooming, or other non-driving tasks?
sec18-card-sec18-F003.memory_hook: Eating and grooming steal driving focus
sec18-card-sec18-F003.expected_back: Eating or grooming while driving can divert a driver's attention and contribute to crashes, just as other activities unrelated to driving can.

sec18-card-sec18-F004.front: Why is playing a radio or music player extremely loudly flagged in the closing reminders?
sec18-card-sec18-F004.memory_hook: Blasting music distracts and risks crashes
sec18-card-sec18-F004.expected_back: Playing a radio or music player extremely loudly is identified as a driving distraction that can contribute to a collision.

sec18-card-sec18-F005.front: What severe danger comparison does research on the closing page draw regarding fatigued driving?
sec18-card-sec18-F005.expected_back: Fatigued driving can be as dangerous as driving after drinking, according to the research warning summarized in the handbook's closing page.

sec18-card-sec18-F006.front: How does the handbook classify speeding paired with frequent lane changes?
sec18-card-sec18-F006.memory_hook: Speeding and weaving signal aggressive driving
sec18-card-sec18-F006.expected_back: Speeding and frequent lane changes are identified as signs of aggressive driving rather than examples of responsible interaction with traffic.

sec18-card-sec18-F007.front: Under which dangerous behavior category does cutting in front of or cutting off other motorists fall?
sec18-card-sec18-F007.memory_hook: Cutting drivers off is aggressive behavior
sec18-card-sec18-F007.expected_back: Cutting in front of others or cutting other drivers off is included among the handbook's examples of aggressive behavior behind the wheel.

sec18-card-sec18-F008.front: How does the road-rage warning view forcing ahead of cars and treating traffic like a competition?
sec18-card-sec18-F008.memory_hook: Competitive pushing breeds aggressive road rage
sec18-card-sec18-F008.expected_back: Forcing a way ahead of other vehicles and treating traffic competitively are listed as aggressive-driving behaviors in the handbook's road-rage warning.

sec18-card-sec18-F009.front: What insurance coverage is mandatory in Alaska, and who may supply it?
sec18-card-sec18-F009.memory_hook: Owner or driver supplies liability insurance
sec18-card-sec18-F009.expected_back: Alaska requires liability insurance coverage supplied by either the vehicle owner or the driver; the closing safety page restates insurance as a mandatory responsibility.

sec18-card-sec18-F010.front: What two closing reminders does the handbook state about safety belts in Alaska?
sec18-card-sec18-F010.memory_hook: Safety belts are mandatory, save lives
sec18-card-sec18-F010.expected_back: The handbook's closing safety reminders say that safety belts are mandatory in Alaska and that wearing them helps save lives.

sec18-card-sec18-F011.front: Which five weather conditions are highlighted for making Alaska roads tough to drive on?
sec18-card-sec18-F011.memory_hook: Rain, sleet, snow, ice, and fog
sec18-card-sec18-F011.expected_back: Rain, sleet, snow, ice and fog can make Alaska roads difficult to drive on by producing poor road and weather conditions.

sec18-card-sec18-F012.front: What record, financial, and licensing consequences can follow disobeying Alaska traffic laws?
sec18-card-sec18-F012.memory_hook: Points, fines, penalties, even license loss
sec18-card-sec18-F012.expected_back: Disobeying traffic laws can add driving-record points, produce fines and other penalties, and even result in loss of the driver license.

sec18-card-sec18-F013.front: Why is obeying road rules essential beyond protecting just yourself?
sec18-card-sec18-F013.expected_back: Traffic-law violations endanger other road users as well as the driver, so obeying road rules is part of keeping everyone using the road safe.

sec09-card-sec09-F001.front: Why are walkers, cyclists, roadside workers, and mobility-device users considered vulnerable road users?
sec09-card-sec09-F001.expected_back: People walking, bicycling, working on foot near traffic or using mobility devices are vulnerable because a motor vehicle offers them no crash protection.

sec09-card-sec09-F002.front: How does higher vehicle speed affect a pedestrian's odds of surviving a car strike?
sec09-card-sec09-F002.expected_back: Higher collision speeds greatly reduce a pedestrian's chance of surviving a passenger-car impact.

sec09-card-sec09-F003.front: During which four lighting or weather conditions must you use extra care scanning for walkers and cyclists?
sec09-card-sec09-F003.expected_back: Look for pedestrians and bicyclists at all times, using extra care at dusk, dawn, night and in bad weather.

sec09-card-sec09-F004.front: How should you approach whenever turning across or entering a pedestrian crosswalk?
sec09-card-sec09-F004.expected_back: Slow and prepare to stop before turning into or entering a crosswalk.

sec09-card-sec09-F005.front: Besides yielding at a crosswalk, what visual connection should you seek with a pedestrian?
sec09-card-sec09-F005.expected_back: Yield to pedestrians in crosswalks and seek eye contact.

sec09-card-sec09-F006.front: Why should you stop well back behind a crosswalk rather than right on its paint?
sec09-card-sec09-F006.expected_back: Stop far enough behind a crosswalk that drivers in other vehicles can see crossing pedestrians.

sec09-card-sec09-F007.front: What must you obey where a separated bike or pedestrian pathway crosses a road entrance?
sec09-card-sec09-F007.expected_back: Obey a stop sign where a separated pathway crosses a road entrance.

sec09-card-sec09-F008.front: Why must you never overtake a vehicle stopped ahead at a crosswalk?
sec09-card-sec09-F008.expected_back: Do not pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk because it may hide a person crossing.

sec09-card-sec09-F009.front: Around which three places must you pay extra close attention to your speed?
sec09-card-sec09-F009.expected_back: Pay particular attention to speed limits near people in the street, schools and neighborhoods with children.

sec09-card-sec09-F010.front: Who must you specifically check for before putting your vehicle in reverse?
sec09-card-sec09-F010.expected_back: Check carefully for pedestrians before backing.

sec09-card-sec09-F011.front: Which three safety practices does the manual recommend for pedestrians crossing streets?
sec09-card-sec09-F011.expected_back: Pedestrians should use crosswalks, obey traffic controls and watch for turning vehicles before crossing.

sec09-card-sec09-F012.front: During which three signal displays should a pedestrian refrain from starting across the street?
sec09-card-sec09-F012.expected_back: A pedestrian should not begin crossing on a nearly expired green signal or a steady or flashing don't-walk indication.

sec09-card-sec09-F013.front: Which side of a highway must a pedestrian walk along when no sidewalk exists?
sec09-card-sec09-F013.expected_back: When walking along a highway, use the left side facing approaching vehicles.

sec09-card-sec09-F014.front: Which two pedestrian behaviors are prohibited on or along an Alaska highway?
sec09-card-sec09-F014.expected_back: The handbook prohibits soliciting rides or being intoxicated on or along a highway.

sec09-card-sec09-F015.front: How does wearing light-colored clothing help a pedestrian walking near a road after dark?
sec09-card-sec09-F015.expected_back: Light-colored clothing makes a pedestrian easier to see beside a road at night.

sec09-card-sec09-F016.front: Are bicyclists entitled to use the roadway, and which direction must they ride?
sec09-card-sec09-F016.expected_back: Bicycle riders are entitled to roadway use and follow motor traffic's direction of travel.

sec09-card-sec09-F017.front: Before which four curb maneuvers must you turn your head to check blind spots for cyclists?
sec09-card-sec09-F017.expected_back: Before turning, parallel parking, opening a door or leaving a curb, turn your head to check blind spots for bicyclists rather than relying only on mirrors.

sec09-card-sec09-F018.front: How do intersection right-of-way rules apply to bicyclists?
sec09-card-sec09-F018.expected_back: Apply right-of-way rules to bicyclists just as to other vehicles.

sec09-card-sec09-F019.front: Under what age does the Alaska manual warn that young cyclists lack the development to handle complex traffic safely?
sec09-card-sec09-F019.expected_back: Use extra care near young bicyclists; the manual cautions that children younger than nine lack the development needed to handle complex traffic safely.

sec09-card-sec09-F020.front: Must bicyclists obey traffic laws, and does Alaska add driver-license points for a cycling violation?
sec09-card-sec09-F020.expected_back: Bicyclists must obey traffic signs, signals and other traffic laws, although Alaska does not assess license points for bicycle traffic violations.

sec09-card-sec09-F021.front: What three core safety practices does the handbook recommend for bicycle riders?
sec09-card-sec09-F021.expected_back: Bicycle safety guidance recommends wearing a helmet, riding near the road's right edge and not carrying another person on the bicycle.

sec09-card-sec09-F022.front: Which three maneuvers should a bicyclist communicate with hand signals?
sec09-card-sec09-F022.expected_back: A bicyclist should signal turns, lane changes and stops by hand.

sec09-card-sec09-F023.front: How does a bicyclist signal a left turn and a stop using the left arm?
sec09-card-sec09-F023.expected_back: A bicyclist signals left by extending the left arm straight to the left and signals stopping by bending the extended left arm downward at the elbow.

sec09-card-sec09-F024.front: Which two arm gestures may a bicyclist use to signal a right turn?
sec09-card-sec09-F024.expected_back: A bicyclist may signal a right turn with the right arm straight to the right or the left arm extended and bent upward at the elbow.

sec09-card-sec09-F025.front: Where should cyclists watch for emerging cars, and what steering mistake must they avoid when glancing back?
sec09-card-sec09-F025.expected_back: Bicyclists should watch cars at driveways, cross streets and parking places and avoid swerving when checking behind.

sec09-card-sec09-F026.front: What right-of-way and equipment duties apply to bicyclists?
sec09-card-sec09-F026.expected_back: Bicyclists must yield to pedestrians and keep their bicycles in good condition.

sec09-card-sec09-F027.front: What blind-spot and passing trap must cyclists avoid beside turning motor vehicles?
sec09-card-sec09-F027.expected_back: Stay out of motor-vehicle blind spots and do not pass a turning vehicle on the side toward which it is turning.

sec09-card-sec09-F028.front: What should you establish before crossing in front of a stopped or waiting driver even when you hold right-of-way?
sec09-card-sec09-F028.expected_back: Before crossing in front of a driver, make eye contact even when you have priority.

sec09-card-sec09-F029.front: What advice does the Alaska manual give bicyclists who listen through earbuds?
sec09-card-sec09-F029.expected_back: The manual advises bicyclists using headphones to leave one earbud out so they can hear surrounding hazards.

sec09-card-sec09-F030.front: How do a motorcyclist's legal rights and responsibilities compare with those of other motorists?
sec09-card-sec09-F030.expected_back: Motorcyclists have the same roadway rights and responsibilities as other drivers.

sec09-card-sec09-F031.front: Why must drivers actively train their eyes to look for motorcycles?
sec09-card-sec09-F031.expected_back: A motorcycle's distance and speed can be difficult for another driver to judge, so consciously look for motorcycles.

sec09-card-sec09-F032.front: What double-check is required before turning left across an oncoming motorcycle's lane?
sec09-card-sec09-F032.expected_back: Before turning left across an oncoming motorcycle's path, look again and make sure its position and speed are understood.

sec09-card-sec09-F033.front: Why shouldn't you trust a motorcycle's flashing turn signal by itself before pulling out?
sec09-card-sec09-F033.expected_back: Do not assume a motorcycle's blinking turn signal means it will turn, because many motorcycle indicators do not cancel automatically.

sec09-card-sec09-F034.front: What recommended following cushion should you keep behind a motorcycle?
sec09-card-sec09-F034.expected_back: Allow a motorcycle the same recommended four-second following gap as other vehicles.

sec09-card-sec09-F035.front: May you pull alongside a motorcycle inside the same lane if the rider is hugging one side?
sec09-card-sec09-F035.expected_back: Motorcycles need the full lane; do not move into the lane beside a motorcycle even if it is traveling near one edge.

sec09-card-sec09-F036.front: Why do skilled motorcyclists purposely move left, center, or right within their lane?
sec09-card-sec09-F036.expected_back: A rider may change position within a lane to improve visibility or avoid an obstacle.

sec09-card-sec09-F037.front: How should you adjust following space behind a motorcycle on wet or slick roads, especially after dark?
sec09-card-sec09-F037.expected_back: Increase the following gap behind a motorcycle on a wet or slippery road and account for glare, especially at night.

sec09-card-sec09-F038.front: Where are crosswinds and truck air blasts especially likely to shove a motorcycle sideways?
sec09-card-sec09-F038.expected_back: Crosswinds and the wind blast from large trucks may push a motorcycle sideways, particularly on open highways and bridges.

sec09-card-sec09-F039.front: Which minor road-surface features can force a motorcyclist to adjust speed or swerve?
sec09-card-sec09-F039.expected_back: Gravel, debris, pavement seams, rain grooves, small animals or manhole covers may cause a rider to change speed or direction.

sec09-card-sec09-F040.front: What three moves might you see a motorcyclist make just before crossing railroad tracks?
sec09-card-sec09-F040.expected_back: A motorcyclist approaching railroad tracks may slow down, rise off the seat or change angle to cross the tracks more directly.

sec09-card-sec09-F041.front: How might a motorcyclist react on a metal or grated bridge deck, and how should you drive behind them?
sec09-card-sec09-F041.expected_back: On metal or grated bridges, a rider may slow and move toward the lane center or react suddenly to wobbling, so be prepared.

sec09-card-sec09-F042.front: What must you do when approaching the rear of a stopped school bus flashing red lights?
sec09-card-sec09-F042.expected_back: When approaching a stopped school bus from behind with flashing red lights, stop before reaching it and do not pass.

sec09-card-sec09-F043.front: When may a driver stopped behind a school bus begin moving again?
sec09-card-sec09-F043.expected_back: A driver behind the school bus must remain stopped until its stop sign retracts, red lights end and the bus moves again, or the bus driver signals permission to proceed.

sec09-card-sec09-F044.front: How must oncoming drivers respond when meeting a school bus flashing amber lights?
sec09-card-sec09-F044.expected_back: When meeting a school bus with flashing amber lights, slow down and stop when the bus stops, its red lights flash and its stop sign extends.

sec09-card-sec09-F045.front: When may an oncoming driver stopped opposite a school bus proceed cautiously?
sec09-card-sec09-F045.expected_back: A driver meeting the stopped bus must wait for its stop sign to retract and red lights to end before proceeding cautiously.

sec09-card-sec09-F046.front: On what roadway layout is oncoming traffic not required to stop for a school bus's red lights and stop arm in Alaska?
sec09-card-sec09-F046.expected_back: On separated roadways with at least two lanes in each direction, a driver approaching a school bus going the opposite way need not stop for its displayed stop arm and red lights.

sec09-card-sec09-F047.front: At or below what top travel speed must a vehicle display a slow-moving-vehicle emblem in Alaska?
sec09-card-sec09-F047.expected_back: The slow-moving-vehicle emblem is required on vehicles traveling at twenty-five miles per hour or less.

sec09-card-sec09-F048.front: Which part of the slow-moving-vehicle emblem catches drivers' eyes during daylight?
sec09-card-sec09-F048.expected_back: By day, the slow-moving-vehicle emblem's solid fluorescent orange triangle attracts attention from approaching drivers.

sec09-card-sec09-F049.front: Which part of the slow-moving-vehicle emblem lights up in your headlights at night?
sec09-card-sec09-F049.expected_back: At night, the emblem's reflective red triangular border identifies the slow-moving vehicle in headlights.

sec14-card-sec14-F001.front: Where should your wheels rest when parking beside an Alaska road outside city limits?
sec14-card-sec14-F001.expected_back: When parking beside a road outside city limits, place every wheel off the pavement if possible.

sec14-card-sec14-F002.front: When must a vehicle parked at night keep parking lights or low beams illuminated?
sec14-card-sec14-F002.memory_hook: Lights on within eight pavement feet
sec14-card-sec14-F002.expected_back: At night, leave parking lights or low beams on unless the parked vehicle is at least eight feet from the pavement edge.

sec14-card-sec14-F003.front: What street markings and controls commonly mark urban no-parking zones?
sec14-card-sec14-F003.memory_hook: Posted signs plus red, yellow curbs
sec14-card-sec14-F003.expected_back: Urban no-parking areas are commonly identified by signs or red or yellow curbs.

sec14-card-sec14-F004.front: Is double parking allowed on Alaska streets?

sec14-card-sec14-F005.front: What must you take with you whenever leaving a parked vehicle unattended?
sec14-card-sec14-F005.memory_hook: Take keys and fobs every time
sec14-card-sec14-F005.expected_back: Remove ignition keys or key fobs when leaving a parked vehicle unattended.

sec14-card-sec14-F006.front: Which way should you turn your front wheels when parking downhill versus uphill beside a curb?
sec14-card-sec14-F006.expected_back: For downhill parking, turn the front wheels toward the curb; for uphill parking, turn them away from it.

sec14-card-sec14-F007.front: How close to the near curb must your wheels sit when parallel parked?
sec14-card-sec14-F007.memory_hook: Parallel park within twelve curb inches
sec14-card-sec14-F007.expected_back: When parallel parked, the wheels must be within twelve inches of the near curb.

sec14-card-sec14-F008.front: What three actions are required before pulling out from a parked position?
sec14-card-sec14-F008.memory_hook: Look, signal, and yield pulling out
sec14-card-sec14-F008.expected_back: Before pulling out from a parked position, look, signal and yield to traffic.

sec14-card-sec14-F009.front: What minimum parking distances apply near a fire hydrant and near a stop sign?
sec14-card-sec14-F009.memory_hook: Fifteen feet hydrant, thirty stop sign
sec14-card-sec14-F009.expected_back: Do not park within fifteen feet of a fire hydrant or within thirty feet of a stop sign.

sec14-card-sec14-F010.front: How many feet must you stay clear when parking near a fire-station entrance, crosswalk, or intersection?
sec14-card-sec14-F010.memory_hook: Twenty feet from stations, crosswalks, corners
sec14-card-sec14-F010.expected_back: Do not park within twenty feet of a fire-station entrance, crosswalk or intersection.

sec14-card-sec14-F011.front: Within how many feet of a railroad crossing is parking prohibited?
sec14-card-sec14-F011.memory_hook: Stay fifty feet from rail crossings
sec14-card-sec14-F011.expected_back: Do not park within fifty feet of a railroad crossing.

sec14-card-sec14-F012.front: How far away must you park from stopped fire apparatus displaying emergency flashers?
sec14-card-sec14-F012.memory_hook: Park five hundred feet from firetrucks
sec14-card-sec14-F012.expected_back: Do not park within five hundred feet of stopped fire apparatus displaying emergency flashers.

sec14-card-sec14-F013.front: Who bears primary responsibility for preventing a crash when a vehicle leaves a parking space?
sec14-card-sec14-F013.memory_hook: Departing driver holds main crash duty
sec14-card-sec14-F013.expected_back: The driver leaving a parking space has the main responsibility for avoiding a collision.

sec14-card-sec14-F014.front: Why must drivers take extra care when backing up in residential neighborhoods?
sec14-card-sec14-F014.memory_hook: Children hide behind or between cars
sec14-card-sec14-F014.expected_back: Use special care when backing in residential areas because children may be behind or between parked vehicles.

sec14-card-sec14-F015.front: Which three response fleets may use sirens alongside front red or blue emergency lights?
sec14-card-sec14-F015.memory_hook: Police, fire, and ambulances run strobes
sec14-card-sec14-F015.expected_back: Police vehicles, fire vehicles and ambulances may use sirens and front red or blue emergency lights.

sec14-card-sec14-F016.front: Which forward- or side-visible colored lamps are banned on vehicles lacking special authorization?
sec14-card-sec14-F016.memory_hook: No unauthorized front red, side blue
sec14-card-sec14-F016.expected_back: Without authorization, a vehicle is forbidden from showing a forward-visible red lamp or a side-visible blue lamp.

sec14-card-sec14-F017.front: How must you respond to an approaching emergency vehicle flashing red or blue lights, even without a siren?
sec14-card-sec14-F017.memory_hook: Pull right, clear intersections, stop completely
sec14-card-sec14-F017.expected_back: For an approaching authorized emergency vehicle displaying flashing red or blue lights, slow, yield, pull to the right edge clear of intersections and stop until it passes, whether or not its siren sounds.

sec14-card-sec14-F018.front: On a four-lane road, how should you pass a parked responder or tow truck running overhead flashers?
sec14-card-sec14-F018.memory_hook: Move into the farther lane safely
sec14-card-sec14-F018.expected_back: When passing a stationary emergency vehicle or tow truck using overhead flashers on a four-lane road, change to the lane farther away if safe.

sec14-card-sec14-F019.front: How must you pass a stationary emergency vehicle if changing lanes is unsafe or the road has two lanes?
sec14-card-sec14-F019.memory_hook: Slow to reasonable, prudent passing speed
sec14-card-sec14-F019.expected_back: If a lane change around a stationary emergency vehicle is unsafe or the road has only two lanes, pass at a reasonable and prudent reduced speed.

sec14-card-sec14-F020.front: What is the closest distance you may follow behind an emergency-response vehicle?
sec14-card-sec14-F020.memory_hook: Stay back five hundred feet minimum
sec14-card-sec14-F020.expected_back: Do not follow an emergency-response vehicle closer than five hundred feet.

sec14-card-sec14-F021.front: When may you drive across a fire hose, and why does the handbook forbid crossing without permission?
sec14-card-sec14-F021.memory_hook: Never cross fire hoses without permission
sec14-card-sec14-F021.expected_back: Do not drive across a fire hose without a fire-department official's consent; the handbook warns of damage and danger to rescue workers.

sec14-card-sec14-F022.front: What dollar fine and driving-record points apply to illegally driving over a fire hose?
sec14-card-sec14-F022.memory_hook: Hundred-dollar fine plus two record points
sec14-card-sec14-F022.expected_back: The handbook lists a one hundred-dollar fine and two points for the fire-hose violation.

sec14-card-sec14-F023.front: Can Alaska cities add extra rules beyond state law around emergency vehicles?
sec14-card-sec14-F023.memory_hook: Cities may add stricter emergency rules
sec14-card-sec14-F023.expected_back: A city may impose additional requirements around emergency vehicles.

sec14-card-sec14-F024.front: How should you respond when a police officer signals you to pull over?
sec14-card-sec14-F024.memory_hook: Stop promptly in a safe manner
sec14-card-sec14-F024.expected_back: When police signal a stop, stop as soon as practical in a reasonably safe manner.

sec14-card-sec14-F025.front: What immediate disclosure duty applies if police contact you while you carry a concealed deadly weapon?
sec14-card-sec14-F025.memory_hook: Immediately inform officers about concealed weapons
sec14-card-sec14-F025.expected_back: A person contacted by police who has a concealed deadly weapon on the person must immediately tell the officer, according to the manual.

sec14-card-sec14-F026.front: Which three credentials or vehicle documents must you carry and present to an officer upon request?
sec14-card-sec14-F026.memory_hook: License, insurance proof, and current registration
sec14-card-sec14-F026.expected_back: Carry a driver license, proof of insurance and current registration and show them to an officer when requested.

sec14-card-sec14-F027.front: How may proof of auto insurance be presented digitally during a traffic stop?
sec14-card-sec14-F027.memory_hook: Present insurance proof on mobile devices
sec14-card-sec14-F027.expected_back: Proof of insurance may be shown on a mobile device.

sec14-card-sec14-F028.front: Which side must you pull toward for police, even when cruising in a four-lane road's left lane?
sec14-card-sec14-F028.memory_hook: Signal promptly and move right safely
sec14-card-sec14-F028.expected_back: When being pulled over, signal promptly and move right as soon as safe, even when starting from the left lane of a four-lane road.

sec14-card-sec14-F029.front: Which three roadside spots should you avoid choosing when pulling over for police?
sec14-card-sec14-F029.memory_hook: Skip curves, blind hillcrests, and guardrails
sec14-card-sec14-F029.expected_back: Avoid choosing an unsafe police-stop location such as a curve, the far side of a hillcrest or beside a guardrail.

sec14-card-sec14-F030.front: What three safety steps should vehicle occupants follow inside the car during a traffic stop?
sec14-card-sec14-F030.memory_hook: Stay inside, light cabin, hands visible
sec14-card-sec14-F030.expected_back: During a traffic stop, occupants should remain inside, illuminate the cabin at night and keep hands visible.

sec14-card-sec14-F031.front: When should you reach for documents during a stop, and what if a disability affects compliance?
sec14-card-sec14-F031.memory_hook: Retrieve when asked, explain any disability
sec14-card-sec14-F031.expected_back: Wait for the officer's request before retrieving documents, and explain a disability that prevents compliance with instructions.

sec14-card-sec14-F032.front: How should you pull back onto the roadway once a traffic stop concludes?
sec14-card-sec14-F032.memory_hook: Signal and safely reenter live traffic
sec14-card-sec14-F032.expected_back: After a traffic stop, signal and safely reenter traffic unless the officer directs otherwise.

sec14-card-sec14-F033.front: What five-step sequence should you follow immediately after a tire blows out?
sec14-card-sec14-F033.memory_hook: Hold off brakes, steer, slow, exit
sec14-card-sec14-F033.expected_back: After a tire blowout, initially avoid braking, concentrate on steering, slow gradually, brake gently and move entirely off the pavement.

sec14-card-sec14-F034.front: Under what condition does the handbook allow trying to put out a vehicle fire?
sec14-card-sec14-F034.memory_hook: Fight vehicle fires only while safe
sec14-card-sec14-F034.expected_back: For a vehicle fire, the handbook conditions attempts to extinguish it on whether doing so remains safe.

sec14-card-sec14-F035.front: Why must you test your brakes gently after driving through deep water?
sec14-card-sec14-F035.memory_hook: Wet brakes fail or pull sideways
sec14-card-sec14-F035.expected_back: After deep-water driving, test brakes gently because they may fail to hold or pull to one side.

sec14-card-sec14-F036.front: What technique does the handbook recommend for drying out wet brakes?
sec14-card-sec14-F036.memory_hook: Drive slowly, low gear, light brake
sec14-card-sec14-F036.expected_back: The handbook recommends slowly driving in a low gear with light brake application to dry wet brakes.

sec14-card-sec14-F037.front: Which three actions should you take if your accelerator jams open?
sec14-card-sec14-F037.memory_hook: Brake, shift neutral, focus on steering
sec14-card-sec14-F037.expected_back: For a jammed accelerator, the handbook lists using the brakes, shifting to neutral and concentrating on steering.

sec14-card-sec14-F038.front: Where should you park a disabled vehicle, and which lights should you turn on at night?
sec14-card-sec14-F038.memory_hook: Clear roadway completely, run flashers nights
sec14-card-sec14-F038.expected_back: For a disabled vehicle, park entirely outside the traveled roadway if possible and use parking lights or hazard flashers at night.

sec14-card-sec14-F039.front: How should you mark a disabled vehicle, especially when it cannot be moved off the road?
sec14-card-sec14-F039.memory_hook: Place triangles or flares, raise hood
sec14-card-sec14-F039.expected_back: Use warning triangles or flares if available to mark a disabled vehicle, and raise the hood if it cannot be moved from the road.

sec14-card-sec14-F040.front: Which two mechanical controls help slow a vehicle if the main service brakes fail?
sec14-card-sec14-F040.memory_hook: Apply parking brake, downshift lower gear
sec14-card-sec14-F040.expected_back: The manual's brake-failure instructions include applying the parking brake and selecting a lower gear.

sec14-card-sec14-F041.front: What three emergency moves should you make if an oncoming vehicle crosses into your lane?
sec14-card-sec14-F041.memory_hook: Honk, brake sharply, steer toward ditch
sec14-card-sec14-F041.expected_back: If an oncoming vehicle enters your lane, the handbook directs sounding the horn, braking sharply and steering toward a shoulder or ditch.

sec14-card-sec14-F042.front: How should you control speed and steering right after your wheels drop off the pavement edge?
sec14-card-sec14-F042.memory_hook: Ease throttle, grip firmly, tap brakes
sec14-card-sec14-F042.expected_back: If wheels leave the pavement, ease off the accelerator, grip the wheel firmly, brake lightly and intermittently and maintain vehicle control.

sec14-card-sec14-F043.front: When and how should you steer back onto the pavement after dropping onto the shoulder?
sec14-card-sec14-F043.memory_hook: Reenter slowly once nearby traffic clears
sec14-card-sec14-F043.expected_back: Return to pavement slowly only after nearby traffic has cleared.

sec14-card-sec14-F044.front: What transmission and clutch practices are prohibited when driving downhill?
sec14-card-sec14-F044.memory_hook: Never coast downhill neutral or declutched
sec14-card-sec14-F044.expected_back: Do not coast downhill in neutral or with the clutch disengaged.

sec14-card-sec14-F045.front: How much clear visibility is required in each direction before turning around near a hill or curve?
sec14-card-sec14-F045.memory_hook: Five hundred visible feet each direction
sec14-card-sec14-F045.expected_back: Do not turn around near a hill or curve unless at least five hundred feet is visible in each direction.

sec14-card-sec14-F046.front: What is the safest way to turn around in city traffic, and what sign rule applies?
sec14-card-sec14-F046.memory_hook: Circle the block, obey U-turn bans
sec14-card-sec14-F046.expected_back: Driving around the block is the safest city turnaround method; obey signs prohibiting U-turns.

sec14-card-sec14-F047.front: What unsafe door-and-head habit must you avoid when checking behind your vehicle to back up?
sec14-card-sec14-F047.memory_hook: Look back, never lean out doors
sec14-card-sec14-F047.expected_back: Look before backing and avoid opening the door and leaning your head outside to check behind.

sec14-card-sec14-F048.front: To whom must a backing driver yield when reversing onto or near a highway?
sec14-card-sec14-F048.memory_hook: Backing drivers yield to approaching traffic
sec14-card-sec14-F048.expected_back: A backing driver must yield to vehicles approaching on the highway or an intersecting highway.

sec14-card-sec14-F049.front: When, if ever, is backing allowed on a controlled-access highway or its entry and exit ramps?
sec14-card-sec14-F049.memory_hook: Illegal unless police, fire, flagger directs
sec14-card-sec14-F049.expected_back: Backing on a controlled-access highway or its entry or exit ramps is illegal unless directed by police, firefighters or construction flaggers.

sec13-card-sec13-F001.front: Which two driving factors degrade together in rain, snow, and ice, and what suffers?
sec13-card-sec13-F001.expected_back: Weather changes both visibility and tire traction, so rain, snow and ice reduce the ability to stop or change direction quickly.

sec13-card-sec13-F002.front: Why is pavement extra slick during roughly the first half hour of rainfall?
sec13-card-sec13-F002.expected_back: During roughly the first half hour of rain, water mixes with road oil, dirt and tire dust to make paved surfaces especially slippery.

sec13-card-sec13-F003.front: What check must come before gently testing your brakes for available road traction?
sec13-card-sec13-F003.expected_back: Before cautiously checking available traction, first check the rear-view mirror.

sec13-card-sec13-F004.front: Why must streaking or skipping wiper blades and empty washer reservoirs be fixed promptly?
sec13-card-sec13-F004.expected_back: Wipers that streak or skip are hazardous, especially on a rainy night; working wipers and washer fluid are important safety equipment.

sec13-card-sec13-F005.front: Why should you widen following distance behind vehicles on wet or slushy roads?
sec13-card-sec13-F005.expected_back: Leave extra room behind another vehicle to reduce spray on the windshield and headlights.

sec13-card-sec13-F006.front: What quick exterior habit keeps your car visible during and after wet road trips?
sec13-card-sec13-F006.expected_back: Clean vehicle lights often after rainy conditions.

sec13-card-sec13-F007.front: Why should you ease off speed when nearing a long-standing green signal, especially on slick pavement?
sec13-card-sec13-F007.expected_back: Approach a long-standing green signal more slowly so a change to yellow can be handled safely, particularly in bad weather.

sec13-card-sec13-F008.front: Why is adequate tire tread critical when braking on wet pavement?
sec13-card-sec13-F008.expected_back: Use tires with adequate tread because worn tires impair directional control while stopping on a wet surface.

sec13-card-sec13-F009.front: Why does the Alaska handbook advise keeping your gas tank full during cold weather?
sec13-card-sec13-F009.expected_back: The handbook recommends keeping the fuel tank full in cold weather to reduce condensation.

sec13-card-sec13-F010.front: Where should you scan for wildlife, and during which daily light transitions are animals most active?
sec13-card-sec13-F010.expected_back: Scan the road and roadsides carefully for wildlife, especially around dawn and dusk.

sec13-card-sec13-F011.front: What do yellow wildlife-warning signs tell you about a stretch of highway?
sec13-card-sec13-F011.expected_back: Wildlife-warning signs identify locations with frequent animal activity near the road.

sec13-card-sec13-F012.front: How do clean headlights and a clear windshield specifically protect Alaska night drivers?
sec13-card-sec13-F012.expected_back: Clean headlights and a clear windshield help detect moose in low light.

sec13-card-sec13-F013.front: What two adjustments help you spot animals in time when driving rural roads at night?
sec13-card-sec13-F013.expected_back: At night, reduce speed and use high beams when conditions permit.

sec13-card-sec13-F014.front: Why must you slow immediately when a moose or deer stands calmly beside the shoulder?
sec13-card-sec13-F014.expected_back: Slow down near a deer or moose beside the road because it may suddenly enter traffic.

sec13-card-sec13-F015.front: Why must you slow and keep scanning after a single deer or moose finishes crossing?
sec13-card-sec13-F015.expected_back: After seeing one animal cross, slow and watch for others because deer and moose often travel in groups.

sec13-card-sec13-F016.front: How can you warn approaching drivers about wildlife standing near the highway?
sec13-card-sec13-F016.expected_back: A brief hazard-light or headlight signal can warn approaching drivers about animals near the highway.

sec13-card-sec13-F017.front: What human traffic hazard often accompanies roadside moose or bear sightings?
sec13-card-sec13-F017.expected_back: Watch for other drivers stopping or pulling over abruptly to view wildlife.

sec13-card-sec13-F018.front: Why shouldn't you trust deer whistles, extra lights, or roadside reflectors to prevent animal strikes?
sec13-card-sec13-F018.expected_back: Do not rely on deer whistles, added lights or reflectors to keep animals away; cautious driving remains the primary defense.

sec13-card-sec13-F019.front: Why must you brake firmly in your lane instead of swerving if an animal bolts in front of you?
sec13-card-sec13-F019.expected_back: If an animal runs into the path, brake firmly without swerving, because swerving may cause another collision or a fixed-object impact.

sec13-card-sec13-F020.front: Whom must you contact after colliding with a big-game animal in Alaska?
sec13-card-sec13-F020.expected_back: After a big-game collision, contact local police or Alaska State Troopers.

sec13-card-sec13-F021.front: Who legally owns big-game animals injured or killed in Alaska traffic collisions, and whom must the driver notify?
sec13-card-sec13-F021.expected_back: Big-game animals injured or killed in a vehicle collision belong to the state, and the driver must notify a State Trooper or wildlife officer as soon as possible.

sec13-card-sec13-F022.front: Which two habits cut skid risk, especially when temperatures hover around freezing and thawing?
sec13-card-sec13-F022.expected_back: Reduce skid risk by avoiding abrupt changes in speed or direction and watching for slippery conditions during freezing or thawing.

sec13-card-sec13-F023.front: Why do bridges and shaded or sheltered stretches surprise drivers in cold weather?
sec13-card-sec13-F023.expected_back: Bridges and shaded or sheltered areas can become slippery sooner and remain slippery longer than other road surfaces.

sec13-card-sec13-F024.front: What happens if you crank the steering wheel too far while trying to catch a skid?
sec13-card-sec13-F024.expected_back: Overcorrecting during a skid can simply send the skid in another direction.

sec13-card-sec13-F025.front: Where and how should a new driver practice ice stopping and skid recovery before winter traffic?
sec13-card-sec13-F025.expected_back: Practice stopping and skid recovery only at low speed in a safe private area before driving in traffic on ice or packed snow.

sec13-card-sec13-F026.front: How should you check road grip when you suspect hidden ice ahead?
sec13-card-sec13-F026.expected_back: When ice is suspected, make any traction test cautiously after checking the mirror.

sec13-card-sec13-F027.front: When should you start slowing for an upcoming stop on ice or packed snow?
sec13-card-sec13-F027.expected_back: Begin slowing well before the intended stop when driving on ice or packed snow.

sec13-card-sec13-F028.front: Why must you avoid locking your wheels when braking on slick surfaces?
sec13-card-sec13-F028.expected_back: Avoid locking the wheels under braking because rolling wheels are needed for steering control.

sec13-card-sec13-F029.front: How does the Alaska handbook contrast slippery braking without anti-lock brakes versus anti-lock-equipped vehicles?
sec13-card-sec13-F029.expected_back: The handbook discusses gentle brake pumping for slippery surfaces but directs drivers of anti-lock-equipped vehicles to the vehicle manual for the correct method.

sec13-card-sec13-F030.front: How should you react mentally and with the steering wheel if your car begins skidding?
sec13-card-sec13-F030.expected_back: During a skid, stay calm and steer the front wheels toward the direction of the skid.

sec13-card-sec13-F031.front: Which three panic inputs must you avoid while recovering from a skid?
sec13-card-sec13-F031.expected_back: Do not brake abruptly, oversteer or overcorrect while recovering from a skid.

sec13-card-sec13-F032.front: According to the handbook, how do you shed speed safely as steering control returns from a skid?
sec13-card-sec13-F032.expected_back: The manual describes gently applying and releasing the brake as control returns to slow the vehicle safely.

sec13-card-sec13-F033.front: What throttle input does the Alaska skid-recovery note specify for front-wheel-drive or four-wheel-drive vehicles?
sec13-card-sec13-F033.expected_back: The skid-recovery note states that front-wheel-drive or four-wheel-drive vehicles need easy acceleration to pull out of a skid.

sec16-card-sec16-F001.front: Which four water sources can flood roads, bridges, and low-lying areas?
sec16-card-sec16-F001.memory_hook: Rivers, failed dams, snowmelt, heavy rain
sec16-card-sec16-F001.expected_back: Floodwater may result from overflowing rivers, failed dams or levees, snow runoff or heavy rain and may cover roads, bridges and low areas.

sec16-card-sec16-F002.front: How quickly can flash flooding develop during or after intense rainfall?
sec16-card-sec16-F002.memory_hook: Develops unexpectedly within minutes or hours
sec16-card-sec16-F002.expected_back: Flash flooding can develop unexpectedly within minutes or hours of intense rainfall.

sec16-card-sec16-F003.front: What should you do whenever you encounter a flooded roadway ahead?
sec16-card-sec16-F003.memory_hook: Turn around and take another route
sec16-card-sec16-F003.expected_back: Do not drive into a flooded roadway; turn around and use another route.

sec16-card-sec16-F004.front: Why must drivers exercise heightened caution around potential flooding at night?
sec16-card-sec16-F004.memory_hook: Floodwater hides across dark nighttime pavement
sec16-card-sec16-F004.expected_back: Use particular caution at night because floodwater is harder to see.

sec16-card-sec16-F005.front: How little water can reach the underside of most passenger cars and cause stalling or lost control?
sec16-card-sec16-F005.memory_hook: Six inches stalls or floats cars
sec16-card-sec16-F005.expected_back: The handbook warns that six inches of water can reach the bottom of most passenger cars and cause stalling or loss of control.

sec16-card-sec16-F006.front: How deep must moving floodwater get before it sweeps away pickups, SUVs, and passenger cars?
sec16-card-sec16-F006.memory_hook: Two moving feet sweeps away trucks
sec16-card-sec16-F006.expected_back: Two feet of moving water can sweep away most vehicles, including pickup trucks and sport utility vehicles.

sec16-card-sec16-F007.front: Why can seemingly shallow floodwater still trap a vehicle unexpectedly?
sec16-card-sec16-F007.memory_hook: Shallow water hides dips, washed roadbeds
sec16-card-sec16-F007.expected_back: Apparently shallow floodwater may hide a dip or a roadbed washed away underneath.

sec16-card-sec16-F008.front: What should you do if floodwater blocks your path and no alternate route exists?
sec16-card-sec16-F008.memory_hook: Reach higher ground until water drops
sec16-card-sec16-F008.expected_back: If no alternate route is available, move to higher ground and wait for floodwater to fall.

sec16-card-sec16-F009.front: How do gentle acceleration and braking—avoiding jackrabbit starts and hard stops—affect fuel consumption?
sec16-card-sec16-F009.memory_hook: Gentle pedals cut wasted fuel burn
sec16-card-sec16-F009.expected_back: Gentle acceleration and braking and fewer abrupt starts or hard stops can reduce fuel use.

sec16-card-sec16-F010.front: How should you approach an upcoming red traffic light to save fuel and brakes?
sec16-card-sec16-F010.memory_hook: Spot red early, ease off throttle
sec16-card-sec16-F010.expected_back: Anticipate a red light and ease off the accelerator early rather than maintaining power until hard braking is necessary.

sec16-card-sec16-F011.front: Why should you hold an even speed when conditions allow instead of surging and braking?
sec16-card-sec16-F011.memory_hook: Hold steady speed, skip surging pedals
sec16-card-sec16-F011.expected_back: Maintain an even speed when appropriate instead of repeatedly accelerating and braking.

sec16-card-sec16-F012.front: How does the handbook advise warming up an engine instead of prolonged driveway idling?
sec16-card-sec16-F012.expected_back: The handbook recommends warming an engine through driving rather than prolonged idling.

sec16-card-sec16-F013.front: Where does the handbook recommend using cruise control to save fuel?
sec16-card-sec16-F013.memory_hook: Use cruise control on flat highways
sec16-card-sec16-F013.expected_back: Cruise control on flat highways is presented as a fuel-saving practice.

sec16-card-sec16-F014.front: What fuel or emissions issues can an illuminated onboard-diagnostics light signal, and whom should you ask?
sec16-card-sec16-F014.memory_hook: Worse economy, higher emissions, ask dealer
sec16-card-sec16-F014.expected_back: An illuminated onboard-diagnostics light can indicate poorer fuel economy or increased emissions, so ask a dealer for information.

sec16-card-sec16-F015.front: What two benefits come from keeping generous following distance behind other vehicles?
sec16-card-sec16-F015.memory_hook: Protects safety and cuts vehicle wear
sec16-card-sec16-F015.expected_back: Keeping enough following distance from other vehicles protects your safety and prevents wear and tear on your vehicle.

sec16-card-sec16-F016.front: How do you measure the handbook's minimum two-second following gap using a roadside landmark?
sec16-card-sec16-F016.memory_hook: Count two after landmark before reaching
sec16-card-sec16-F016.expected_back: For the stated two-second minimum, start counting when the vehicle ahead reaches a fixed object and remain behind that object until the count ends.

sec16-card-sec16-F017.front: About how long does it take to recognize a hazard and move your foot onto the brake?
sec16-card-sec16-F017.expected_back: The manual estimates roughly three-quarters of a second for recognizing a need to brake and moving a foot to the pedal.

sec16-card-sec16-F018.front: At fifty miles per hour, roughly how far do you travel reacting versus braking to a stop?
sec16-card-sec16-F018.expected_back: At fifty miles per hour, the manual's reaction example includes about fifty-five feet before braking and at least another one hundred sixty feet after braking begins.

sec16-card-sec16-F019.front: Why must you keep your left or resting foot off the brake pedal while cruising?
sec16-card-sec16-F019.memory_hook: Never rest feet on brake pedals
sec16-card-sec16-F019.expected_back: Do not rest a foot on the brake pedal while driving.

sec16-card-sec16-F020.front: What pedal mistake must you avoid in a vehicle equipped with anti-lock brakes?
sec16-card-sec16-F020.expected_back: Do not pump the brake pedal in a vehicle equipped with anti-lock brakes.

sec16-card-sec16-F021.front: When should you reduce speed for a curve or restricted forward sightline?
sec16-card-sec16-F021.memory_hook: Slow down before curves, blind spots
sec16-card-sec16-F021.expected_back: Slow before a curve or any area where the view ahead is restricted.

sec16-card-sec16-F022.front: Why must you widen following separation when driving in rain or snow?
sec16-card-sec16-F022.memory_hook: Wet or icy roads stretch stops
sec16-card-sec16-F022.expected_back: Increase separation from other vehicles in rain or snow because wet or icy pavement lengthens stopping distance.

sec16-card-sec16-F023.front: Which three vehicle adjustments can an available economy mode make to trim fuel burn?
sec16-card-sec16-F023.memory_hook: Smooths throttle, shifts, cuts AC load
sec16-card-sec16-F023.expected_back: An available economy setting can smooth accelerator input, alter shift points and reduce air-conditioning load on the engine.

sec16-card-sec16-F024.front: What two downsides does the handbook note about unnecessary idling?
sec16-card-sec16-F024.memory_hook: Idling wastes fuel, may be banned
sec16-card-sec16-F024.expected_back: Unnecessary idling wastes fuel and may be prohibited.

sec16-card-sec16-F025.front: Beyond what expected stationary duration does the handbook suggest turning off the engine?
sec16-card-sec16-F025.expected_back: The handbook gives a rule of thumb to shut the engine off for a stop expected to exceed thirty to sixty seconds.

sec16-card-sec16-F026.front: Which four travel alternatives can lower your vehicle operating expenses?
sec16-card-sec16-F026.memory_hook: Transit, biking, walking, or shared carpools
sec16-card-sec16-F026.expected_back: Public transportation, bicycling, walking or carpooling can reduce vehicle operating costs.

sec16-card-sec16-F027.front: How can combining errands and central parking reduce time and fuel use?
sec16-card-sec16-F027.memory_hook: Batch errands, park centrally, walk stops
sec16-card-sec16-F027.expected_back: Combining errands can reduce driving time and fuel use; parking centrally and walking between nearby stops can also help.

sec16-card-sec16-F028.front: Which three digital tasks can eliminate unnecessary driving trips altogether?
sec16-card-sec16-F028.memory_hook: Online shopping, banking, and bill pay
sec16-card-sec16-F028.expected_back: Online shopping, banking and bill payment can eliminate trips that do not require leaving home.

sec16-card-sec16-F029.front: What three conditions should you verify on your vehicle's fuel cap?
sec16-card-sec16-F029.memory_hook: Fuel cap present, undamaged, tightly sealed
sec16-card-sec16-F029.expected_back: Make sure the fuel cap is present, undamaged and tightly fitted.

sec16-card-sec16-F030.front: Which three benefits come from keeping tires inflated to proper pressure?
sec16-card-sec16-F030.memory_hook: Boosts safety, tire life, fuel economy
sec16-card-sec16-F030.expected_back: Proper tire pressure improves safety, tire life and fuel use.

sec16-card-sec16-F031.front: What minimum tire tread depth does the Alaska handbook state?
sec16-card-sec16-F031.expected_back: The handbook states a minimum tire tread depth of two thirty-seconds of an inch.

sec16-card-sec16-F032.front: During a penny tread check, what visual clue indicates your tires are worn out?
sec16-card-sec16-F032.memory_hook: Top of Lincoln's head means worn
sec16-card-sec16-F032.expected_back: In the penny tread check, seeing the top of Lincoln's head with the coin inserted into a groove indicates worn-out tires.

sec16-card-sec16-F033.front: Why should tires be rotated regularly as part of routine maintenance?
sec16-card-sec16-F033.memory_hook: Rotate tires regularly for longer life
sec16-card-sec16-F033.expected_back: Rotate tires as part of maintenance to extend useful tire life.

sec16-card-sec16-F034.front: Why should you unload unneeded cargo and take off unused roof racks or carriers?
sec16-card-sec16-F034.memory_hook: Extra weight and roof drag burn
sec16-card-sec16-F034.expected_back: Remove unnecessary cargo and unused roof racks or carriers because extra weight and wind resistance increase fuel use.

sec16-card-sec16-F035.front: Which engine oil viscosity should you choose, and how should oil condition be maintained?
sec16-card-sec16-F035.memory_hook: Manufacturer oil grade, change degraded oil
sec16-card-sec16-F035.expected_back: Use the oil grade recommended by the vehicle manufacturer and change degraded oil regularly.

sec16-card-sec16-F036.front: Which two routine engine-care steps help preserve strong fuel economy?
sec16-card-sec16-F036.memory_hook: Regular tune-ups plus clean air filters
sec16-card-sec16-F036.expected_back: Regular tune-ups and a clean air filter support fuel economy.

sec16-card-sec16-F037.front: What two planning advantages come from keeping records of your driving history and expenses?
sec16-card-sec16-F037.memory_hook: Compare ongoing costs, guide next purchase
sec16-card-sec16-F037.expected_back: Keep records of driving history to compare costs over time and inform future vehicle purchases.

sec16-card-sec16-F038.front: Starting with model-year two thousand thirteen vehicles, what label helps shoppers compare fuel use, cost, and environmental impact?
sec16-card-sec16-F038.memory_hook: Check federal fuel-economy environmental window labels
sec16-card-sec16-F038.expected_back: For model-year two thousand thirteen and newer vehicles, review the federal fuel-economy and environmental label when comparing fuel use, cost and environmental impact.

sec16-card-sec16-F039.front: What market factor can change the dollar savings estimated in the handbook?
sec16-card-sec16-F039.memory_hook: Estimated savings shift with gas prices
sec16-card-sec16-F039.expected_back: The handbook notes that its estimated savings may vary with the price of gasoline.

sec01-card-sec01-F001.question_text: Unless a legal exemption applies, what credential do you need to drive on Alaska streets, highways, or public property?
sec01-card-sec01-F001.teaching_text: Operating on any public road or lot without proper state authorization exposes you to unlicensed-driving citations right away.

sec01-card-sec01-F002.question_text: At what minimum age can a nonresident drive on an out-of-state or foreign license, and when must they get an Alaska license?
sec01-card-sec01-F002.teaching_text: Visitors and new arrivals get roughly three months on a home credential before Alaska requires switching over.

sec01-card-sec01-F003.question_text: Which military family members may drive on a valid home-state license while keeping permanent residence there?
sec01-card-sec01-F003.teaching_text: Test questions love the family distinction because spouses over eighteen share this exemption while other dependents do not.

sec01-card-sec01-F004.question_text: How does Alaska treat someone who is temporarily moving farm machinery along a highway?
sec01-card-sec01-F004.teaching_text: Short agricultural transfers between fields do not require a standard driver license on Alaska highways.

sec01-card-sec01-F005.question_text: When is a federal employee exempt from holding an Alaska driver license?
sec01-card-sec01-F005.teaching_text: The exemption applies strictly to government vehicles driven on official duty, not personal errands in a private car.

sec01-card-sec01-F006.question_text: How does Alaska classify a commercial driver who is domiciled in another state?
sec01-card-sec01-F006.teaching_text: Interstate truck and bus operators keep their home-state credential instead of obtaining a separate Alaska license.

sec01-card-sec01-F007.question_text: Which license class does Alaska issue for everyday passenger vehicles?
sec01-card-sec01-F007.teaching_text: Knowing the standard noncommercial letter keeps you from confusing everyday car privileges with commercial or motorcycle classes.

sec01-card-sec01-F008.question_text: Under a Class D license, up to what engine displacement may a motorcycle or motor scooter have without another endorsement?
sec01-card-sec01-F008.teaching_text: Once a two-wheeler reaches fifty cubic centimeters or more, your passenger car license alone no longer covers it.

sec01-card-sec01-F009.question_text: What category of vehicles does an Alaska IP instruction permit cover?
sec01-card-sec01-F009.teaching_text: This standard learner class lets new drivers practice in everyday noncommercial vehicles under proper adult supervision.

sec01-card-sec01-F010.question_text: Under what exact supervision condition does an IE instruction permit allow driving noncommercial vehicles?
sec01-card-sec01-F010.teaching_text: Unlike a regular learner permit, an IE permit is valid strictly during lessons supervised by a licensed driving instructor.

sec01-card-sec01-F011.question_text: What Social Security requirement applies to an original Alaska license or permit application, and must you show the card?
sec01-card-sec01-F011.teaching_text: DMV verifies your digits electronically against its database, so memorizing an accurate number works without the paper card.

sec01-card-sec01-F012.question_text: What address proof must an original license or permit applicant provide, and what documents count as examples?
sec01-card-sec01-F012.teaching_text: Showing a recent pay stub, bank statement, or utility bill proves where you live before DMV issues a first credential.

sec01-card-sec01-F013.question_text: Besides residence and Social Security details, what documentary proof does an original Alaska application require?
sec01-card-sec01-F013.teaching_text: Every first-time applicant must establish both exact age and United States citizenship or authorized stay.

sec01-card-sec01-F014.question_text: What features make a United States birth certificate acceptable at DMV, and which common keepsake records fail?
sec01-card-sec01-F014.teaching_text: Applicants often get turned away at the counter because souvenir hospital footprints and baptismal papers lack official government certification.

sec01-card-sec01-F015.question_text: When can a court order prove your birth date at DMV, and what court record does not qualify?
sec01-card-sec01-F015.teaching_text: Only a sealed court order listing your full name and birth date works, never a criminal or civil conviction abstract.

sec01-card-sec01-F016.question_text: Whose birth date can military identification establish as a primary DMV document, and whose card falls short?
sec01-card-sec01-F016.teaching_text: Active-duty, reserve, or retired IDs work for the service member, whereas dependent cards cannot stand alone as primary proof.

sec01-card-sec01-F017.question_text: Which United States passport documents prove your birth date at DMV, and what happens if one is expired?
sec01-card-sec01-F017.teaching_text: Once the expiration date passes, a passport book or card loses its status as acceptable birth-date evidence.

sec01-card-sec01-F018.question_text: Can a United States citizen born overseas prove birth date at DMV using a consular birth report?
sec01-card-sec01-F018.teaching_text: Americans born overseas use this official federal consular record in place of a state-issued birth certificate.

sec01-card-sec01-F019.question_text: Under what conditions can a foreign passport serve as identity-related evidence at Alaska DMV?
sec01-card-sec01-F019.teaching_text: Photocopies or expired booklets fail at the counter, and the passport must be paired with matching immigration paperwork.

sec01-card-sec01-F020.question_text: Which immigration and citizenship records does the Alaska manual list as acceptable supporting documents?
sec01-card-sec01-F020.teaching_text: Bringing one of these official federal credentials verifies lawful status alongside your primary identity record.

sec01-card-sec01-F021.question_text: What legal-presence proof is required when renewing an Alaska license, permit, or identification card?
sec01-card-sec01-F021.teaching_text: Legal presence is checked again at renewal time, not just when you apply for your very first card.

sec01-card-sec01-F022.question_text: What must you bring if the name on your birth-date record differs from your other identification?
sec01-card-sec01-F022.teaching_text: Without a certified paper trail bridging old and current names, DMV cannot verify that all documents belong to you.

sec01-card-sec01-F023.question_text: Below what age do applicants need parental consent for an Alaska instruction permit or driver license?
sec01-card-sec01-F023.teaching_text: Every minor applicant needs an authorized adult co-signer until reaching legal adulthood at eighteen.

sec01-card-sec01-F024.question_text: What legal risk does an adult take on by signing parental consent for a minor's driving privilege?
sec01-card-sec01-F024.teaching_text: Co-signing is serious business because crash damages from a teen's negligence or willful misconduct can land on that adult.

sec01-card-sec01-F025.question_text: Who is legally allowed to sign the parental-consent section before a minor receives a permit or license?
sec01-card-sec01-F025.teaching_text: Older siblings, relatives without court guardianship, or family friends cannot authorize a minor's application.

sec01-card-sec01-F026.question_text: Does one parental-consent signature cover future license upgrades, or how does Alaska handle each credential type?
sec01-card-sec01-F026.teaching_text: Moving from an instruction permit to a provisional license requires a fresh consent signature for that specific stage.

sec01-card-sec01-F027.question_text: How can a minor satisfy the consent rule when the parent cannot appear in person at DMV?
sec01-card-sec01-F027.teaching_text: A notary seal proves the absent parent's signature is genuine so DMV can still process the teen's application.

sec01-card-sec01-F028.question_text: Who may withdraw parental consent for a minor driver, and how must that request be verified?
sec01-card-sec01-F028.teaching_text: Only the exact adult who signed initially can pull consent back, using a notarized or DMV-witnessed written request.

sec01-card-sec01-F029.question_text: What action does Alaska DMV take when parental consent is withdrawn for a minor driver?
sec01-card-sec01-F029.teaching_text: Once the co-signer pulls authorization, DMV cancels the teen's permit or license immediately until valid consent returns.

sec01-card-sec01-F030.question_text: What credential does anyone learning to drive need before practicing on a street or highway?
sec01-card-sec01-F030.teaching_text: Practicing on public roadways without a valid learner permit is illegal even if an experienced adult sits beside you.

sec01-card-sec01-F031.question_text: At what minimum age can you get an Alaska instruction permit, and how long does it stay valid?
sec01-card-sec01-F031.teaching_text: Alaska starts supervised practice early at fourteen and gives learners a two-year window before expiration.

sec01-card-sec01-F032.question_text: What minimum age and driving experience must a learner's supervising licensed driver have?
sec01-card-sec01-F032.teaching_text: Your coach must be at least twenty-one and hold a full year of licensed experience in that exact vehicle class.

sec01-card-sec01-F033.question_text: Where must the supervising licensed driver sit while a learner practices in a passenger car?
sec01-card-sec01-F033.teaching_text: Riding in the back seat leaves the supervisor unable to coach closely or take immediate control in an emergency.

sec01-card-sec01-F034.question_text: How long must a sixteen- or seventeen-year-old hold a valid instruction permit before getting a provisional Class D license?
sec01-card-sec01-F034.teaching_text: Rushing straight to a road test at sixteen fails unless your learner permit has been active for six months.

sec01-card-sec01-F035.question_text: How many times may a noncommercial instruction permit be renewed in Alaska?
sec01-card-sec01-F035.teaching_text: Because you only get one renewal, letting a second permit expire forces you to restart the application process.

sec01-card-sec01-F036.question_text: What requirements must an applicant meet to obtain an original Alaska instruction permit?
sec01-card-sec01-F036.teaching_text: Passing both vision and knowledge exams comes before you ever practice legally on public roads.

sec01-card-sec01-F037.question_text: Which approved enrollment programs allow DMV to issue a special instruction permit?
sec01-card-sec01-F037.teaching_text: Structured high-school, community-college, commercial training, and medical rehabilitation courses qualify for specialized learner permits.

sec01-card-sec01-F038.question_text: What fee does the Alaska manual list for an original instruction permit?
sec01-card-sec01-F038.teaching_text: Knowing the exact counter fee prevents mixing up learner permit pricing with standard or federal license rates.

sec01-card-sec01-F039.question_text: After an earlier license of the same class has been expired for how long may someone obtain another permit?
sec01-card-sec01-F039.teaching_text: Once a former license has been dead for five years, drivers can re-enter supervised practice on a fresh permit.

sec01-card-sec01-F040.question_text: What is the minimum age at which Alaska may issue a driver license?
sec01-card-sec01-F040.teaching_text: While instruction permits start at fourteen, solo licensing does not unlock until at least your sixteenth birthday.

sec01-card-sec01-F041.question_text: What two things must a driver do with their driver license for it to be valid behind the wheel?
sec01-card-sec01-F041.teaching_text: Leaving your card at home or forgetting to sign it makes the credential invalid during a traffic stop.

sec01-card-sec01-F042.question_text: When does an under-twenty-one Alaska license expire, and what extra test is required to renew it?
sec01-card-sec01-F042.teaching_text: Waiting past ninety days after turning twenty-one leaves you unlicensed, and renewal requires passing an alcohol-awareness exam.

sec01-card-sec01-F043.question_text: What kinds of license restrictions can physical conditions trigger on an Alaska credential?
sec01-card-sec01-F043.teaching_text: Tailored restrictions let drivers with vision or mobility needs operate safely so long as required gear is used.

sec01-card-sec01-F044.question_text: Can you get an Alaska license while your driving rights are canceled, suspended, or revoked anywhere?
sec01-card-sec01-F044.teaching_text: Moving north never erases a suspension or revocation because interstate records block new licensing until cleared.

sec01-card-sec01-F045.question_text: Before Alaska issues your new license, what might DMV require you to do with another state's card?
sec01-card-sec01-F045.teaching_text: Drivers hold one valid state license at a time, so DMV collects the prior state's card at issuance.

sec01-card-sec01-F046.question_text: How does Alaska licensing treat military dependents compared with a service member's spouse?
sec01-card-sec01-F046.teaching_text: Teen and other non-spouse military dependents cannot borrow the active-duty home-state exemption if they drive in Alaska.

sec01-card-sec01-F047.question_text: Upon conviction, what minimum jail sentence applies for driving while canceled, suspended, revoked, or against a limited license?
sec01-card-sec01-F047.teaching_text: Ignoring a license sanction or breaking work-license limits triggers mandatory jail time starting at ten days.

sec01-card-sec01-F048.question_text: How many certified practice hours does an under-eighteen first-license applicant need, including challenging conditions?
sec01-card-sec01-F048.teaching_text: At least ten of those forty logged hours must build real skill in darkness or rough Alaska weather.

sec01-card-sec01-F049.question_text: Which adults are authorized to certify a young applicant's required forty hours of driving experience?
sec01-card-sec01-F049.teaching_text: Alaska allows an employer alongside a parent or legal guardian to sign off on the minor's practice log.

sec01-card-sec01-F050.question_text: How many months immediately before applying must a provisional-license applicant stay free of traffic-law convictions?
sec01-card-sec01-F050.teaching_text: A single traffic conviction during your learner window resets the six-month clean clock needed for provisional licensing.

sec01-card-sec01-F051.question_text: What six-month clean record is required right before graduating out of a provisional license?
sec01-card-sec01-F051.teaching_text: Any traffic ticket or a second underage-drinking conviction inside the prior six months blocks your upgrade.

sec01-card-sec01-F052.question_text: Which adult passengers allow a provisional driver to carry other riders in the vehicle?
sec01-card-sec01-F052.teaching_text: Having a parent, guardian, or someone at least twenty-one onboard lifts the teen peer-passenger ban.

sec01-card-sec01-F053.question_text: May siblings ride with a provisional driver when no parent or adult is in the car?
sec01-card-sec01-F053.teaching_text: Alaska carves out an everyday family exception so provisional teens can drive brothers and sisters without an adult along.

sec01-card-sec01-F054.question_text: During what overnight hours is a provisional driver generally barred from driving without a qualifying adult?
sec01-card-sec01-F054.teaching_text: Unless accompanied by a parent, guardian, or licensed twenty-one-year-old for that class, late-night solo trips are off-limits.

sec01-card-sec01-F055.question_text: How does the provisional nighttime restriction accommodate a teen's employment?
sec01-card-sec01-F055.teaching_text: Driving to, from, or during work is legal between one and five a.m. only if you skip detours.

sec01-card-sec01-F056.question_text: After six clean months free of driving and substance convictions, what two steps remove provisional restrictions for a minor?
sec01-card-sec01-F056.teaching_text: Restrictions do not vanish automatically for minors after six months without updated parental consent and a fifteen-dollar license fee.

sec01-card-sec01-F057.question_text: What does a driver aged eighteen or older need to get a license without provisional limits or parental consent?
sec01-card-sec01-F057.teaching_text: Legal adults skip parental sign-off and provisional curfews by paying the standard fifteen-dollar issuance fee.

sec01-card-sec01-F058.question_text: Which off-system areas qualify for an exception to provisional passenger and nighttime restrictions?
sec01-card-sec01-F058.teaching_text: Remote communities disconnected from the land highway system or highways carrying four hundred ninety-nine daily vehicles qualify.

sec01-card-sec01-F059.question_text: According to the manual, at what two points do provisional license restrictions cease?
sec01-card-sec01-F059.teaching_text: Curfews and passenger limits end either on your eighteenth birthday or once you complete formal removal at DMV.

sec01-card-sec01-F060.question_text: Before which credential issuances does Alaska apply vision testing?
sec01-card-sec01-F060.teaching_text: Even replacing a lost card or renewing an old one can require verifying that your eyesight meets state standards.

sec01-card-sec01-F061.question_text: What document can substitute for taking the vision test at the DMV counter?
sec01-card-sec01-F061.teaching_text: Bringing a signed medical or optometry certification confirming DMV eyesight compliance lets you bypass the counter screener.

sec01-card-sec01-F062.question_text: What visual acuity standard does Alaska state for driver licensing?
sec01-card-sec01-F062.teaching_text: Meeting twenty-forty acuity ensures you can read highway signs and spot hazards early enough to react.

sec01-card-sec01-F063.question_text: What rule applies if you need glasses or contacts to pass the DMV vision standard?
sec01-card-sec01-F063.teaching_text: Driving without required glasses or contacts violates your license restriction and slows hazard recognition.

sec01-card-sec01-F064.question_text: What happens if an applicant's vision fails to meet the Alaska licensing standard?
sec01-card-sec01-F064.teaching_text: DMV holds back the permit or license until corrective lenses or medical treatment bring acuity up to twenty-forty.

sec01-card-sec01-F065.question_text: Which three groups of applicants must take the Alaska written knowledge test?
sec01-card-sec01-F065.teaching_text: Letting an Alaska license stay expired past twelve months or suffering revocation puts you right back in knowledge testing.

sec01-card-sec01-F066.question_text: What additional written test is required after your twenty-first birthday before an original or renewed driver license?
sec01-card-sec01-F066.teaching_text: Adults obtaining or renewing their first post-twenty-one credential must prove they know Alaska impaired-driving laws.

sec01-card-sec01-F067.question_text: Where do Alaska written-test questions come from, and what three subject areas do they cover?
sec01-card-sec01-F067.teaching_text: Every exam item comes straight from the state manual across road rules, safe habits, and sign recognition.

sec01-card-sec01-F068.question_text: How soon may an applicant retake the Alaska written test after not passing?
sec01-card-sec01-F068.teaching_text: You cannot retest the same afternoon, giving you overnight to review missed manual rules before trying tomorrow.

sec01-card-sec01-F069.question_text: How may an applicant who understands English but struggles with reading take the written test?
sec01-card-sec01-F069.teaching_text: A helper may read prompts aloud, yet every answer choice must come strictly from the applicant alone.

sec01-card-sec01-F070.question_text: What three helpful features does Alaska's online knowledge-test service offer?
sec01-card-sec01-F070.teaching_text: Remote testing supports translated text, spoken playback, and immediate pass-or-fail feedback as soon as you finish.
