sec01-card-sec01-F071.question_text: What must be removed for an Alaska license photo, and how are religious or medical head coverings handled?
sec01-card-sec01-F071.teaching_text: Hats, sunglasses, heavy costume makeup, and face-hiding hair come off, while religious or medical wraps stay above the brow.

sec01-card-sec01-F072.question_text: What fees does the manual list for standard versus federally compliant noncommercial licenses?
sec01-card-sec01-F072.teaching_text: Choosing federal REAL ID compliance doubles the noncommercial license fee compared with a standard state card.

sec01-card-sec01-F073.question_text: In the handbook's fee table, how much does an instruction permit cost for standard versus federally compliant identification?
sec01-card-sec01-F073.teaching_text: Adding federal identification compliance adds twenty dollars on top of the fifteen-dollar standard learner permit fee.

sec01-card-sec01-F074.question_text: How do you replace a lost, stolen, destroyed, or unreadable Alaska license or permit?
sec01-card-sec01-F074.teaching_text: Presenting acceptable identification lets DMV issue a duplicate card so you never drive without a readable credential.

sec01-card-sec01-F075.question_text: How and within how many days must a license or permit holder report a name or address change to DMV?
sec01-card-sec01-F075.teaching_text: Missing the thirty-day written update window can cause critical renewal or suspension notices to go to an old address.

sec01-card-sec01-F076.question_text: Which official records are required to process a name change at Alaska DMV?
sec01-card-sec01-F076.teaching_text: Informal certificates fail because marriage records must be certified copies issued through vital statistics, or backed by court order.

sec01-card-sec01-F077.question_text: What must you provide before Alaska issues a license if another state previously suspended, canceled, or revoked your privileges?
sec01-card-sec01-F077.teaching_text: Verbal assurances never clear an interstate block without official written clearance from the state that sanctioned you.

sec01-card-sec01-F078.question_text: Who may obtain a copy of an Alaska driving record, and what fee does the manual list?
sec01-card-sec01-F078.teaching_text: Privacy rules restrict record copies to you or someone you authorize, accompanied by the ten-dollar record fee.

sec01-card-sec01-F079.question_text: When can an Alaska applicant register a choice for organ and tissue donation?
sec01-card-sec01-F079.teaching_text: Both original licensing and routine renewals give applicants the option to add donor designation right on the card.

sec02-card-sec02-F001.question_text: Who are Alaska's financial-responsibility and mandatory-insurance laws designed to protect?
sec02-card-sec02-F001.teaching_text: Requiring coverage and crash accountability shields innocent drivers, passengers, and pedestrians from unpaid collision losses.

sec02-card-sec02-F002.question_text: Under Alaska financial-responsibility rules, what collision costs fall on the at-fault driver or vehicle owner?
sec02-card-sec02-F002.teaching_text: Causing property damage or bodily injury makes the vehicle owner or operator financially accountable to victims.

sec02-card-sec02-F003.question_text: How many years can Alaska suspend your license if a crash creates a reasonable chance of civil liability?
sec02-card-sec02-F003.teaching_text: Unresolved crash claims can sideline your driving privilege for as long as three years even before a lawsuit finishes.

sec02-card-sec02-F004.question_text: How can a driver end a three-year financial-responsibility suspension before the full period runs out?
sec02-card-sec02-F004.teaching_text: Reaching a documented payment agreement with the other people involved lifts the civil-liability hold early.

sec02-card-sec02-F005.question_text: What insurance coverage must the vehicle owner or driver carry under Alaska's mandatory-insurance law?
sec02-card-sec02-F005.teaching_text: Driving any motor vehicle without active liability coverage violates state law before a crash ever happens.

sec02-card-sec02-F006.question_text: Which two dollar amounts does the manual's insurance paragraph list for bodily-injury-or-death liability coverage?
sec02-card-sec02-F006.teaching_text: Know both exact policy figures because the manual states fifty thousand and one hundred thousand dollars for injury or death.

sec02-card-sec02-F007.question_text: What minimum property-damage liability coverage amount does the Alaska manual list?
sec02-card-sec02-F007.teaching_text: Repairing modern vehicles or roadside structures adds up fast, so policies must carry at least twenty-five thousand dollars.

sec02-card-sec02-F008.question_text: Where must proof of liability insurance be kept when operating a vehicle?
sec02-card-sec02-F008.teaching_text: Having an active policy at home will not save you at a roadside stop if proof is missing from the car.

sec02-card-sec02-F009.question_text: What two roadside consequences can follow failing to show an officer proof of liability insurance?
sec02-card-sec02-F009.teaching_text: Officers do not just write tickets for missing insurance cards; they can tow and impound the car on the spot.

sec02-card-sec02-F010.question_text: Within how many days and after what crash thresholds must you send insurance proof to Alaska DMV?
sec02-card-sec02-F010.teaching_text: Any collision involving injury, death, or property damage above five hundred one dollars starts a strict fifteen-day DMV clock.

sec02-card-sec02-F011.question_text: Does a driver who did not cause a qualifying crash still have to submit insurance proof to DMV?
sec02-card-sec02-F011.teaching_text: Fault never excuses paperwork because blame-free drivers face suspension too if they skip the mandatory DMV filing.

sec02-card-sec02-F012.question_text: Does reporting a crash to police or your insurer satisfy the DMV insurance notification requirement?
sec02-card-sec02-F012.teaching_text: Drivers get suspended by assuming their insurer or investigating officer automatically notified DMV of coverage.

sec02-card-sec02-F013.question_text: Where can a driver get the insurance-certificate form required after a qualifying crash?
sec02-card-sec02-F013.teaching_text: Even if no officer hands you the form at the scene, DMV counters and online downloads leave no excuse.

sec02-card-sec02-F014.question_text: What suspension lengths apply for a first and second occurrence of driving uninsured or missing the fifteen-day proof deadline?
sec02-card-sec02-F014.teaching_text: Even an insured driver who forgets the fifteen-day filing loses privileges for ninety days first and one year second.

sec02-card-sec02-F015.question_text: What should you do with your vehicle immediately after any crash?
sec02-card-sec02-F015.teaching_text: Stopping fulfills your legal duty, and moving drivable cars off the roadway prevents a secondary pileup.

sec02-card-sec02-F016.question_text: How should you warn approaching traffic after a collision, especially at night?
sec02-card-sec02-F016.teaching_text: Placing flares or road signals alerts oncoming headlights without putting your body in front of moving vehicles.

sec02-card-sec02-F017.question_text: How should you assist injured people at a crash scene, and when should you move them?
sec02-card-sec02-F017.teaching_text: Shifting an injured victim needlessly can worsen spinal trauma unless fire, water, or active traffic forces a move.

sec02-card-sec02-F018.question_text: Which two basic care steps does the Alaska manual highlight for an injured crash victim?
sec02-card-sec02-F018.teaching_text: Stopping severe blood loss and preventing shock-related hypothermia stabilize victims while emergency responders travel to the scene.

sec02-card-sec02-F019.question_text: Which six pieces of information must drivers exchange with one another after a collision?
sec02-card-sec02-F019.teaching_text: Collecting full identity, phone, address, license, tag, and insurance-company details protects everyone when claims are filed.

sec02-card-sec02-F020.question_text: Besides other drivers' details, whose identities should you record after a crash?
sec02-card-sec02-F020.teaching_text: Bystanders leave quickly once traffic clears, and neutral witness accounts often settle disputed fault later.

sec02-card-sec02-F021.question_text: Within a municipality, which crashes require calling local police immediately via nine-one-one?
sec02-card-sec02-F021.teaching_text: Inside city limits, any injury or combined property damage reaching two thousand dollars demands an immediate nine-one-one call.

sec02-card-sec02-F022.question_text: Who must you contact immediately for an injury or two-thousand-dollar damage crash outside a municipality?
sec02-card-sec02-F022.teaching_text: Beyond municipal boundaries, Alaska State Troopers handle immediate collision response for serious damage or injuries.

sec02-card-sec02-F023.question_text: How must a driver interact with the officer investigating a collision?
sec02-card-sec02-F023.teaching_text: Answering scene questions accurately helps officers complete official reports that clear up insurance and DMV follow-ups.

sec02-card-sec02-F024.question_text: Within how many days is a DMV crash report required, and what exception removes that requirement?
sec02-card-sec02-F024.teaching_text: When an officer investigates at the scene, their official report covers the ten-day self-report, though insurance proof still applies.

sec02-card-sec02-F025.question_text: What ways can a driver submit a required Alaska DMV crash report?
sec02-card-sec02-F025.teaching_text: Drivers can file online or pick up the paper crash-report form from DMV offices or the state website.

sec02-card-sec02-F026.question_text: What must you do after hitting an unattended parked car or private property?
sec02-card-sec02-F026.teaching_text: Driving off without trying to locate the owner or leaving your name, address, and phone number turns damage into hit-and-run.

sec02-card-sec02-F027.question_text: If you already showed insurance to police at a crash with five hundred one dollars in damage, must you still file with DMV?
sec02-card-sec02-F027.teaching_text: Classic exam trap because showing your insurance card to the officer never replaces sending DMV its fifteen-day certificate.

sec02-card-sec02-F028.question_text: What numeric range of points do Alaska moving-violation convictions carry, and how are values weighted?
sec02-card-sec02-F028.teaching_text: High-hazard offenses carry heavier point totals toward ten so crash-prone drivers hit intervention thresholds faster.

sec02-card-sec02-F029.question_text: Which twelve-month and twenty-four-month point totals mandate suspension or revocation regardless of personal hardship?
sec02-card-sec02-F029.teaching_text: Excuse letters about jobs or family commutes cannot stop mandatory action once you hit twelve or eighteen points.

sec02-card-sec02-F030.question_text: Can a driver get a limited work-purpose license during a points-based suspension or revocation?
sec02-card-sec02-F030.teaching_text: Stacking too many tickets completely parks you because occupational limited licenses are unavailable on point suspensions.

sec02-card-sec02-F031.question_text: At what point accumulation milestone does Alaska send a warning to a driver?
sec02-card-sec02-F031.teaching_text: Hitting half of a suspension threshold triggers an early notice so you can clean up habits before losing privileges.

sec02-card-sec02-F032.question_text: Which two ways can reduce record points, and how often can a defensive-driving course count?
sec02-card-sec02-F032.teaching_text: Staying violation-free earns credit, and an approved defensive-driving class shaves points at most once every twelve months.

sec02-card-sec02-F033.question_text: At what point totals must a provisional-license holder complete a division-approved driver-improvement course?
sec02-card-sec02-F033.teaching_text: Provisional teens face mandatory retraining at half the adult suspension numbers to curb risky habits early.

sec02-card-sec02-F034.question_text: What can repeated violations require a driver to complete to retain driving privileges?
sec02-card-sec02-F034.teaching_text: Ignoring a motor-vehicle hearing officer's interview or action plan puts your remaining driving privilege in jeopardy.

sec03-card-sec03-F001.question_text: Which two outcomes in Alaska or another state add points to your Alaska driving record?
sec03-card-sec03-F001.teaching_text: Paying a ticket through bail forfeiture or getting convicted out of state still posts points straight to Alaska DMV.

sec03-card-sec03-F002.question_text: How many points are assigned for driving while suspended, revoked, or contrary to a limited license?
sec03-card-sec03-F002.teaching_text: One violation behind the wheel during a suspension lands nearly enough points by itself to trigger another sanction.

sec03-card-sec03-F003.question_text: How many driving-record points does Alaska assign for driving under the influence?
sec03-card-sec03-F003.teaching_text: Impaired driving sits at the very top of Alaska's point scale alongside court and administrative revocations.

sec03-card-sec03-F004.question_text: How many points are added to an Alaska record for reckless driving?
sec03-card-sec03-F004.teaching_text: Willful disregard for road safety draws the maximum ten-point hit plus mandatory license revocation.

sec03-card-sec03-F005.question_text: How many points does Alaska assign for refusing a required breath sample?
sec03-card-sec03-F005.teaching_text: Saying no to breath testing never spares your record because refusal carries the exact same ten points as DUI.

sec03-card-sec03-F006.question_text: How many points are assigned for fleeing or attempting to evade a police officer?
sec03-card-sec03-F006.teaching_text: Running from a patrol stop creates extreme pursuit danger and hits your driving record with ten points.

sec03-card-sec03-F007.question_text: How many points does racing or participating in a speed contest put on an Alaska record?
sec03-card-sec03-F007.teaching_text: Turning public roads into a drag strip lands the maximum ten-point penalty on a single conviction.

sec03-card-sec03-F008.question_text: How many points are assigned for negligent homicide involving a motor vehicle?
sec03-card-sec03-F008.teaching_text: Causing a fatal crash through criminal negligence brings maximum record points alongside felony court revocation.

sec03-card-sec03-F009.question_text: How many points does manslaughter involving a motor vehicle add to an Alaska driving record?
sec03-card-sec03-F009.teaching_text: Any fatal felony behind the wheel sits at the ten-point ceiling on Alaska's demerit schedule.

sec03-card-sec03-F010.question_text: How many points are assigned for assault involving a motor vehicle?
sec03-card-sec03-F010.teaching_text: Using or operating a vehicle in an assault conviction posts ten points right onto your driving record.

sec03-card-sec03-F011.question_text: How many points does Alaska assign for leaving the scene of a crash?
sec03-card-sec03-F011.teaching_text: Exam questions test nine versus ten points closely, and leaving a collision scene stands alone at nine.

sec03-card-sec03-F012.question_text: How many points does negligent driving add to an Alaska record?
sec03-card-sec03-F012.teaching_text: Distinguish the three tiers carefully because reckless is ten, negligent is six, and careless behavior is four.

sec03-card-sec03-F013.question_text: How many points are assigned for failing to yield to an authorized emergency vehicle?
sec03-card-sec03-F013.teaching_text: Delaying an ambulance, fire rig, or patrol responder puts lives at risk and triggers an immediate point warning.

sec03-card-sec03-F014.question_text: What point total hits your record if you fail to stop while a school bus loads or unloads?
sec03-card-sec03-F014.teaching_text: Children cross unpredictably around boarding buses, so ignoring bus stop signals puts six points on your record.

sec03-card-sec03-F015.question_text: What point penalty hits a driver who disobeys official traffic controls in parks, crosswalks, playgrounds, or school zones?
sec03-card-sec03-F015.teaching_text: Ignoring signs or signals where children walk and play carries triple the points of a basic moving ticket.

sec03-card-sec03-F016.question_text: How many points does Alaska assign for driving without insurance?
sec03-card-sec03-F016.teaching_text: Skipping mandatory liability coverage hits you with six demerit points on top of suspension and impoundment risks.

sec03-card-sec03-F017.question_text: How many points does careless-driving behavior receive on an Alaska record?
sec03-card-sec03-F017.teaching_text: Keep careless at four points separate from negligent at six and reckless at ten when answering point questions.

sec03-card-sec03-F018.question_text: How many points are assigned for following another vehicle too closely?
sec03-card-sec03-F018.teaching_text: Cutting off your stopping cushion causes rear-end collisions and lands four points per conviction.

sec03-card-sec03-F019.question_text: How many points does a standard failure to stop or yield add to your record?
sec03-card-sec03-F019.teaching_text: Rolling a stop sign or cutting off right-of-way adds four points, while emergency-vehicle yield failures jump to six.

sec03-card-sec03-F020.question_text: How many points are assigned when a minor drives after consuming alcohol?
sec03-card-sec03-F020.teaching_text: For a provisional teen, one six-point hit instantly triggers mandatory driver-improvement retraining alongside alcohol revocation.

sec03-card-sec03-F021.question_text: How many points apply for illegal passing inside a designated traffic safety corridor?
sec03-card-sec03-F021.teaching_text: Safety corridors mark high-severity highway stretches where impatient passing causes head-on crashes and four-point penalties.

sec03-card-sec03-F022.question_text: How many points do unlisted other moving violations receive in the handbook's general category?
sec03-card-sec03-F022.teaching_text: Routine moving citations not singled out for higher risk still chip away at your record two points at a time.

sec03-card-sec03-F023.question_text: What point value applies when an oversize or overweight load breaks its permit's operating-hour limits?
sec03-card-sec03-F023.teaching_text: Moving heavy or wide loads outside permitted hours disrupts traffic flow and carries a distinct three-point penalty.

sec03-card-sec03-F024.question_text: How many points does speeding in a school zone or playground crosswalk assign?
sec03-card-sec03-F024.teaching_text: Even moderate excess speed through a school zone or playground crosswalk jumps straight to six points.

sec03-card-sec03-F025.question_text: How many points are assigned for driving three through nine miles per hour over the speed limit?
sec03-card-sec03-F025.teaching_text: Creeping three to nine miles per hour past the posted sign starts Alaska's speeding ladder at two points.

sec03-card-sec03-F026.question_text: Going ten to nineteen miles per hour past the posted speed limit puts how many points on your record?
sec03-card-sec03-F026.teaching_text: Pushing ten to nineteen over doubles the low-band point hit and lengthens stopping distance dramatically.

sec03-card-sec03-F027.question_text: How many points are assigned for driving twenty miles per hour or more above the limit?
sec03-card-sec03-F027.teaching_text: Two twenty-over speeding tickets in a single year reach twelve points and trigger mandatory suspension.

sec03-card-sec03-F028.question_text: What point bands apply when violating speed restrictions on an oversize or overweight permit?
sec03-card-sec03-F028.teaching_text: Permit speed limits use the exact same three-to-nine, ten-to-nineteen, and twenty-plus point brackets as posted highway signs.

sec03-card-sec03-F029.question_text: What must be done with the physical driver license when privileges are suspended or revoked?
sec03-card-sec03-F029.teaching_text: Keeping a sanctioned plastic card in your wallet is not allowed; the department requires physical surrender.

sec03-card-sec03-F030.question_text: Does reaching the scheduled end date of a suspension or revocation automatically restore your right to drive?
sec03-card-sec03-F030.teaching_text: Driving the morning after your sanction calendar ends is still illegal until formal reinstatement and future coverage are completed.

sec03-card-sec03-F031.question_text: What ongoing insurance requirement follows any suspension, revocation, or license limitation?
sec03-card-sec03-F031.teaching_text: Regaining privileges requires maintaining verified financial responsibility for the future, not just showing an old wallet card.

sec03-card-sec03-F032.question_text: What does an S R twenty-two insurance filing prove to DMV, and what must the insurer report?
sec03-card-sec03-F032.teaching_text: If your policy cancels or lapses early, the insurer notifies DMV directly so your reinstatement does not quietly slide.

sec03-card-sec03-F033.question_text: How does suspension affect driving privileges, and what card step is required once reinstatement rules are met?
sec03-card-sec03-F033.teaching_text: After clearing a temporary suspension, you visit a field office to get a duplicate license rather than starting from scratch.

sec03-card-sec03-F034.question_text: What happens to driving privileges when someone owns or operates an uninsured vehicle involved in a crash?
sec03-card-sec03-F034.teaching_text: Both the uninsured car's owner and its driver face mandatory privilege suspension after a collision.

sec03-card-sec03-F035.question_text: How does Alaska DMV treat accumulating repeated motor-vehicle-law violations?
sec03-card-sec03-F035.teaching_text: Stacking multiple traffic offenses shows ongoing road risk that gives DMV grounds to suspend your license.

sec03-card-sec03-F036.question_text: What license action can follow violating the restrictions printed on your driver license?
sec03-card-sec03-F036.teaching_text: Ignoring corrective-lens, equipment, or provisional codes is treated as a formal ground to suspend your driving privilege.

sec03-card-sec03-F037.question_text: How does revocation differ from suspension when you eventually finish reinstatement requirements?
sec03-card-sec03-F037.teaching_text: Unlike suspension where a duplicate replaces your old license, revocation terminates the credential so you must obtain a new license.

sec03-card-sec03-F038.question_text: If a court convicts you of DUI or chemical-test refusal, what mandatory license action follows?
sec03-card-sec03-F038.teaching_text: Either criminal conviction triggers mandatory revocation rather than a lighter discretionary suspension.

sec03-card-sec03-F039.question_text: What happens to your privileges upon a court conviction for driving while canceled, suspended, or revoked?
sec03-card-sec03-F039.teaching_text: Getting caught driving on a suspended or canceled credential escalates the sanction into full mandatory revocation.

sec03-card-sec03-F040.question_text: What mandatory license action follows a court conviction for reckless driving?
sec03-card-sec03-F040.teaching_text: Beyond adding ten demerit points, a reckless-driving conviction automatically revokes your license.

sec03-card-sec03-F041.question_text: If you are involved in an injury crash and fail to stop and render aid, what follows conviction?
sec03-card-sec03-F041.teaching_text: Abandoning someone hurt in a collision triggers mandatory court-ordered revocation of your driving privilege.

sec03-card-sec03-F042.question_text: Swearing to false motor-vehicle facts under oath brings what license action upon conviction?
sec03-card-sec03-F042.teaching_text: Lying under oath on motor-vehicle paperwork is a serious offense that revokes your license upon conviction.

sec03-card-sec03-F043.question_text: Fleeing unlawfully in a vehicle to escape arrest triggers what license consequence upon conviction?
sec03-card-sec03-F043.teaching_text: Using a car to run from an arresting officer guarantees license revocation once convicted in court.

sec03-card-sec03-F044.question_text: What license action follows conviction for a motor-vehicle felony causing injury or death, like manslaughter or assault?
sec03-card-sec03-F044.teaching_text: Manslaughter, negligent homicide, or vehicular assault convictions all strip driving privileges through mandatory revocation.

sec03-card-sec03-F045.question_text: What action must DMV take administratively when a driver refuses a chemical test after a DUI arrest?
sec03-card-sec03-F045.teaching_text: Administrative revocation starts directly through DMV after a post-arrest refusal without waiting on a criminal trial.

sec03-card-sec03-F046.question_text: For a noncommercial driver arrested for DUI, what breath-test result triggers mandatory administrative revocation?
sec03-card-sec03-F046.teaching_text: Blowing zero point zero eight or higher after arrest forces DMV to revoke noncommercial privileges administratively.

sec03-card-sec03-F047.question_text: How does Alaska classify habitual violations of motor-vehicle laws on the administrative side?
sec03-card-sec03-F047.teaching_text: Chronic disregard for traffic statutes lets DMV revoke driving privileges administratively to protect other road users.

sec03-card-sec03-F048.question_text: What administrative action applies to a driver under twenty-one who operates after consuming alcohol?
sec03-card-sec03-F048.teaching_text: Zero-tolerance rules expose drivers under twenty-one to administrative revocation without needing an adult-tier breath reading.

sec03-card-sec03-F049.question_text: What happens administratively if a driver under twenty-one refuses chemical testing?
sec03-card-sec03-F049.teaching_text: Refusing the chemical test under twenty-one triggers DMV administrative revocation just like testing positive for alcohol.

sec03-card-sec03-F050.question_text: Even away from a car, what DMV action hits someone under twenty-one who uses a false license to get alcohol?
sec03-card-sec03-F050.teaching_text: Misusing a fake or borrowed ID to buy alcohol costs your driving privilege administratively even if nobody drove.

sec03-card-sec03-F051.question_text: How does the outcome of a related court case affect DMV's administrative action against your driving privileges?
sec03-card-sec03-F051.teaching_text: Winning dismissal or acquittal in criminal court does not stop DMV from enforcing its separate administrative action.

sec03-card-sec03-F052.question_text: What financial charge is required to reinstate privileges after a suspension, revocation, or limitation?
sec03-card-sec03-F052.teaching_text: Alongside insurance filings and wait periods, restoring valid status always requires paying DMV's reinstatement fee.

sec04-card-sec04-F001.question_text: Simply by driving a motor vehicle in Alaska, what test have you already legally agreed to take?
sec04-card-sec04-F001.teaching_text: Behind the wheel in Alaska means you have already consented to breath testing that measures alcohol concentration.

sec04-card-sec04-F002.question_text: When may an Alaska officer require you to provide a breath sample for alcohol testing?
sec04-card-sec04-F002.teaching_text: Once lawfully arrested for driving under the influence, providing a breath sample becomes a legal requirement.

sec04-card-sec04-F003.question_text: Which severe crash outcomes allow an officer to require blood or urine tests for alcohol or drugs?
sec04-card-sec04-F003.teaching_text: When a collision kills or seriously injures another person, implied testing expands to blood or urine samples.

sec04-card-sec04-F004.question_text: How seriously does Alaska criminal law classify refusing chemical testing after a lawful arrest?
sec04-card-sec04-F004.teaching_text: Refusing a post-arrest test is a crime in itself that escalates from misdemeanor to felony based on prior offenses.

sec04-card-sec04-F005.question_text: How do Alaska courts treat a driving-under-the-influence charge alongside a chemical-test refusal charge?
sec04-card-sec04-F005.teaching_text: Refusing the breathalyzer does not merge into one case; you can face two distinct charges in court.

sec04-card-sec04-F006.question_text: Can a driver who refuses chemical testing obtain a limited work-purpose license during revocation?
sec04-card-sec04-F006.teaching_text: Refusing a chemical test locks you out of limited work-purpose driving for the entire revocation period.

sec04-card-sec04-F007.question_text: When may an officer require a preliminary roadside breath sample before making a full arrest?
sec04-card-sec04-F007.teaching_text: Following a collision or moving violation, probable cause of alcohol impairment lets the officer require a roadside screen.

sec04-card-sec04-F008.question_text: How does Alaska classify refusing a preliminary roadside breath test?
sec04-card-sec04-F008.teaching_text: Keep the two tests straight on exam day because roadside preliminary refusal is an infraction while post-arrest refusal is criminal.

sec04-card-sec04-F009.question_text: Which six major personal and financial consequences does the handbook link to driving under the influence?
sec04-card-sec04-F009.teaching_text: Beyond losing your license and serving jail time, legal fees, vehicle impoundment, and skyrocketing insurance drain thousands.

sec04-card-sec04-F010.question_text: How many points does a DUI add, and how long does that offense stay on your Alaska driving record?
sec04-card-sec04-F010.teaching_text: Time never wipes an Alaska impaired-driving offense off your driving history once it posts.

sec04-card-sec04-F011.question_text: Which three safe alternatives to driving after drinking does the Alaska manual highlight?
sec04-card-sec04-F011.teaching_text: Planning a sober driver, cab, or transit ride before your first drink eliminates every excuse to get behind the wheel.

sec04-card-sec04-F012.question_text: What revocation periods apply for a first offense versus repeat offenses of using a false license to get alcohol?
sec04-card-sec04-F012.teaching_text: Flashing a fraudulent ID for alcohol costs sixty days of driving the first time and a full year thereafter.

sec04-card-sec04-F013.question_text: Below what age does Alaska prohibit alcohol consumption?
sec04-card-sec04-F013.teaching_text: State law bars alcohol consumption until twenty-one, backing strict zero-tolerance enforcement for young operators.

sec04-card-sec04-F014.question_text: Under age twenty-one, consuming any alcohol can get you cited or arrested for operating which three craft types?
sec04-card-sec04-F014.teaching_text: Alaska's underage zero-tolerance law reaches beyond highways to planes and boats after any measurable drink.

sec04-card-sec04-F015.question_text: For someone under twenty-one, what three driving statuses can DMV revoke after a breath refusal or any alcohol reading?
sec04-card-sec04-F015.teaching_text: Even an unlicensed teen loses future eligibility to obtain an Alaska license after an underage alcohol violation.

sec04-card-sec04-F016.question_text: Does a dismissed citation or not-guilty court verdict stop an under-twenty-one administrative alcohol revocation?
sec04-card-sec04-F016.teaching_text: Because DMV's administrative track runs separately, beating the criminal ticket does not save an underage driver's license.

sec04-card-sec04-F017.question_text: How long is the first administrative revocation for under-twenty-one alcohol operation or test refusal?
sec04-card-sec04-F017.teaching_text: Notice the contrast on test day because underage first revocations start at thirty days while adult DUI starts at ninety.

sec04-card-sec04-F018.question_text: With one previous revocation on record, how long is an under-twenty-one administrative revocation for alcohol operation or refusal?
sec04-card-sec04-F018.teaching_text: A second underage alcohol or refusal incident doubles the administrative loss from thirty days up to sixty.

sec04-card-sec04-F019.question_text: With two previous revocations, how long does the under-twenty-one administrative revocation last?
sec04-card-sec04-F019.teaching_text: Stacking two prior underage actions pushes the administrative revocation period to ninety days.

sec04-card-sec04-F020.question_text: How long is the under-twenty-one administrative revocation when the driver has three or more previous revocations?
sec04-card-sec04-F020.teaching_text: Once an underage driver reaches three prior revocations, the administrative penalty jumps from months to a full year.

sec04-card-sec04-F021.question_text: How is a minor's alcohol-operation or refusal conviction graded, and what court penalties apply?
sec04-card-sec04-F021.teaching_text: Courts classify the minor's offense as an infraction and order community service, up to one thousand dollars, or both.

sec04-card-sec04-F022.question_text: What breath or blood alcohol concentration creates a legal presumption of driving under the influence in Alaska?
sec04-card-sec04-F022.teaching_text: Testing at zero point zero eight or higher establishes legal presumption of impairment even if you feel fine.

sec04-card-sec04-F023.question_text: Following a DUI arrest, which two testing outcomes trigger administrative revocation?
sec04-card-sec04-F023.teaching_text: Refusing the breathalyzer never dodges DMV action because both refusal and zero point zero eight trigger revocation.

sec04-card-sec04-F024.question_text: What happens to a DUI or refusal administrative revocation if the criminal charge is dismissed or ends not guilty?
sec04-card-sec04-F024.teaching_text: DMV's civil license revocation operates under independent rules that survive criminal court dismissals or acquittals.

sec04-card-sec04-F025.question_text: How long does the first administrative revocation last for driving under the influence or chemical refusal?
sec04-card-sec04-F025.teaching_text: An adult first administrative revocation takes you off the road for ninety days before reinstatement is possible.

sec04-card-sec04-F026.question_text: How long is the administrative revocation when you have one prior DUI or refusal conviction?
sec04-card-sec04-F026.teaching_text: A single prior conviction quadruples the ninety-day baseline into a full one-year administrative revocation.

sec04-card-sec04-F027.question_text: How long does administrative revocation last with two prior DUI or refusal convictions?
sec04-card-sec04-F027.teaching_text: Two earlier convictions jump the administrative revocation period from one year straight to three years.

sec04-card-sec04-F028.question_text: What administrative revocation length applies with three or more prior DUI or refusal convictions?
sec04-card-sec04-F028.teaching_text: Three or more prior convictions push administrative license loss to five full years.

sec04-card-sec04-F029.question_text: Convictions from how many preceding years, in Alaska or out of state, count when setting your revocation period?
sec04-card-sec04-F029.teaching_text: Out-of-state DWI, DUI, or refusal convictions inside the past fifteen years stack right onto your Alaska revocation length.

sec04-card-sec04-F030.question_text: How do DMV civil proceedings relate to criminal court proceedings after an alcohol arrest?
sec04-card-sec04-F030.teaching_text: Drivers must handle both deadlines separately because showing up in criminal court never answers a DMV notice.

sec04-card-sec04-F031.question_text: During an Alaska revocation or disqualification, may you drive that vehicle class or apply for a license in another state?
sec04-card-sec04-F031.teaching_text: Crossing state lines to apply for another license during revocation is strictly prohibited alongside driving the affected class.

sec04-card-sec04-F032.question_text: How can a person contest an administrative revocation or disqualification?
sec04-card-sec04-F032.teaching_text: Phone complaints do not preserve appeal rights; contesting a DMV action requires a written administrative-hearing request.

sec04-card-sec04-F033.question_text: Which two written formats may you use to request an Alaska DMV administrative hearing?
sec04-card-sec04-F033.teaching_text: You do not have to hunt down a special form if time is tight because a personal written letter works too.

sec04-card-sec04-F034.question_text: Within how many days of the notice's Date Issued must an administrative hearing normally be requested, and what exception exists?
sec04-card-sec04-F034.teaching_text: Missing the tight seven-day window forfeits your hearing unless physical incapacity triggers the statutory late exception.

sec04-card-sec04-F035.question_text: What does DMV provide once an administrative hearing request is granted?
sec04-card-sec04-F035.teaching_text: The hearing packet spells out the governing statutes, procedural rules, and exact issues you must prepare to address.

sec04-card-sec04-F036.question_text: When does a timely hearing applicant receive a temporary license to drive until the hearing?
sec04-card-sec04-F036.teaching_text: If your underlying license was valid and no court has revoked you, temporary driving continues until the hearing.

sec04-card-sec04-F037.question_text: According to the Alaska manual, which driving-related ability is affected first after drinking alcohol?
sec04-card-sec04-F037.teaching_text: Because self-assessment breaks down before slurred speech or stumbling, impaired drivers talk themselves into thinking they are fine.

sec04-card-sec04-F038.question_text: Is alcohol a stimulant or depressant, and how does it change reflexes, alertness, vision, and judgment?
sec04-card-sec04-F038.teaching_text: Alcohol depresses central nervous functioning rather than sharpening you, cutting alertness, sight, and reaction speed together.

sec04-card-sec04-F039.question_text: What happens to crash risk with each additional drink before getting behind the wheel?
sec04-card-sec04-F039.teaching_text: Collision danger climbs steadily drink by drink rather than waiting until you reach the legal presumption number.

sec04-card-sec04-F040.question_text: How do average blood alcohol readings in young drivers' crashes compare with those of middle-aged or older drivers?
sec04-card-sec04-F040.teaching_text: Combining driving inexperience with even small amounts of alcohol triggers crashes sooner than in older age groups.

sec04-card-sec04-F041.question_text: What matters more for impairment: whether you drink beer, wine, or spirits, or how much alcohol enters your body?
sec04-card-sec04-F041.teaching_text: Switching from liquor to beer never protects you because your bloodstream reacts to total pure alcohol consumed.

sec04-card-sec04-F042.question_text: Which serving sizes of beer, eighty-proof spirits, and wine does the Alaska manual equate in alcohol content?
sec04-card-sec04-F042.teaching_text: Notice Alaska's exact manual numbers because wine is listed at four ounces alongside twelve-ounce beer and one-and-a-half-ounce spirits.

sec04-card-sec04-F043.question_text: Which four factors can change how the same amount of alcohol affects the exact same person on different days?
sec04-card-sec04-F043.teaching_text: Fatigue, stress, medications, or an empty stomach can make one drink hit much harder than it did last week.

sec04-card-sec04-F044.question_text: Do coffee, fresh air, food, or a cold shower sober someone up, and what actually eliminates alcohol?
sec04-card-sec04-F044.teaching_text: Caffeine or cold water merely creates a wide-awake impaired driver while blood alcohol stays unchanged.

sec04-card-sec04-F045.question_text: Which organ processes alcohol in the body, and which two organs eliminate remaining traces?
sec04-card-sec04-F045.teaching_text: Because the liver oxidizes alcohol at a fixed pace and lungs expel vapor, breathalyzers accurately measure impairment.

sec04-card-sec04-F046.question_text: How does combining alcohol with other drugs compare in danger with taking either substance by itself?
sec04-card-sec04-F046.teaching_text: Drug-alcohol interactions amplify sedation and reaction loss far beyond what either substance produces alone.

sec04-card-sec04-F047.question_text: Why is it hard to judge how much someone can drink before driving?
sec04-card-sec04-F047.teaching_text: Shifting body chemistry, stomach contents, and impaired judgment make self-estimating a safe drink limit unreliable.

sec04-card-sec04-F048.question_text: What average burn-off pace does the manual state for one drink and four drinks, and what is its clear recommendation?
sec04-card-sec04-F048.teaching_text: Even though four drinks average roughly four hours, the manual flatly advises anyone who has been drinking not to drive.

sec04-card-sec04-F049.question_text: After a DUI or refusal conviction, which vehicles must have an ignition interlock installed?
sec04-card-sec04-F049.teaching_text: Borrowing a friend's or family member's car without an interlock violates the post-conviction mandate.

sec04-card-sec04-F050.question_text: For at least how many months is an ignition interlock required after a first DUI or refusal conviction?
sec04-card-sec04-F050.teaching_text: Even a first-time offender faces a minimum half-year ignition-interlock requirement on every vehicle driven.

sec04-card-sec04-F051.question_text: In the handbook's interlock table, how many months apply after a second conviction and after a third conviction?
sec04-card-sec04-F051.teaching_text: Each repeat conviction adds another six months to the interlock schedule, moving from twelve to eighteen.

sec04-card-sec04-F052.question_text: How many ignition-interlock months does the table list after a fourth conviction and after a fifth conviction?
sec04-card-sec04-F052.teaching_text: Continuing the six-month step pattern puts fourth convictions at twenty-four months and fifth convictions at thirty.

sec04-card-sec04-F053.question_text: Who is financially responsible for installing and maintaining a required ignition interlock?
sec04-card-sec04-F053.teaching_text: State courts and DMV do not subsidize interlock hardware; every installation and calibration bill falls on the driver.

sec04-card-sec04-F054.question_text: Which two proofs must you submit to reinstate driving privileges after an interlock-qualifying conviction?
sec04-card-sec04-F054.teaching_text: DMV blocks license reinstatement until both your ignition-interlock verification and future financial-responsibility filing are on record.

sec04-card-sec04-F055.question_text: Where does alcohol enter the bloodstream, and what four driving functions does it disrupt?
sec04-card-sec04-F055.teaching_text: Absorbed directly from the stomach, alcohol degrades brain function, reaction speed, vision, and your sense of responsibility.

sec04-card-sec04-F056.question_text: What deceptive mental feeling can alcohol create even while it degrades judgment, hearing, speech, and balance?
sec04-card-sec04-F056.teaching_text: Feeling bold and capable while coordination and senses fail is exactly what lures impaired drivers into fatal mistakes.

sec04-card-sec04-F057.question_text: In the handbook's impairment chart, what effects appear as low as zero point zero two percent?
sec04-card-sec04-F057.teaching_text: Even a tiny zero point zero two reading measurably loosens inhibitions and shifts driver decision-making.

sec04-card-sec04-F058.question_text: What does the impairment chart link to zero point zero six percent versus zero point zero eight percent?
sec04-card-sec04-F058.teaching_text: Reaction and coordination slip at zero point zero six before serious driving deterioration hits at zero point zero eight.

sec04-card-sec04-F059.question_text: In the impairment chart, what changes happen at zero point one zero percent and at zero point one six percent?
sec04-card-sec04-F059.teaching_text: Vision, speech, and balance falter at zero point one zero, and basic walking or standing breaks down by zero point one six.

sec04-card-sec04-F060.question_text: What life-threatening dangers does the handbook's chart associate with zero point four zero percent?
sec04-card-sec04-F060.teaching_text: Reaching zero point four zero brings unconsciousness, potential coma, and immediate medical danger of death.

sec04-card-sec04-F061.question_text: Who should you ask about medication side effects that might interfere with safe driving?
sec04-card-sec04-F061.teaching_text: Checking side effects with your physician ahead of time keeps surprise dizziness or drowsiness off the highway.

sec04-card-sec04-F062.question_text: Can nonprescription cold and allergy medicines affect your ability to drive safely?
sec04-card-sec04-F062.teaching_text: Store-bought sinus and allergy tablets often pack drowsy antihistamines that slow reactions just like prescription sedatives.

sec04-card-sec04-F063.question_text: Which four categories of pills can make driving unsafe when taken in excessive doses?
sec04-card-sec04-F063.teaching_text: Overusing uppers for energy or downers for calm distorts timing, alertness, and steering control.

sec04-card-sec04-F064.question_text: Why does the manual warn specifically against driving after taking illegal drugs?
sec04-card-sec04-F064.teaching_text: Unregulated street substances vary wildly in purity and potency, making sudden incapacitation behind the wheel unpredictable.

sec04-card-sec04-F065.question_text: Does Alaska's controlled-substance DUI ban apply only to illegal street drugs, or what else does it cover?
sec04-card-sec04-F065.teaching_text: Having a pharmacy bottle never excuses impaired driving because controlled substances include legal narcotic and nonnarcotic medications.

sec04-card-sec04-F066.question_text: How do Alaska's penalties for driving under the influence of controlled substances compare with alcohol DUI penalties?
sec04-card-sec04-F066.teaching_text: Drug-impaired convictions trigger the exact same points, revocations, fines, and jail exposure as alcohol DUI.

sec04-card-sec04-F067.question_text: How can prescribed drugs affect alertness, and what happens if you combine them with alcohol?
sec04-card-sec04-F067.teaching_text: Prescriptions alone can dull alertness, and pairing them with alcohol magnifies impairment to potentially deadly extremes.

sec05-card-sec05-F001.question_text: How does wearing a safety belt actually improve your escape chances if a crashed vehicle catches fire or enters water?
sec05-card-sec05-F001.teaching_text: People fear getting trapped by belts, yet staying conscious during impact is what lets you unbuckle and get out.

sec05-card-sec05-F002.question_text: What upper-body impacts can a lap belt alone fail to stop compared with a lap-and-shoulder belt?
sec05-card-sec05-F002.teaching_text: Without a shoulder strap, your upper body jackknifes forward into the wheel, dashboard, or windshield.

sec05-card-sec05-F003.question_text: How does being ejected from a vehicle during a collision affect your survival odds?
sec05-card-sec05-F003.teaching_text: Staying buckled inside the cabin's protective cage saves lives because being thrown out multiplies fatal injuries.

sec05-card-sec05-F004.question_text: Why is holding a child in your arms dangerous during a crash, especially if the adult is unrestrained?
sec05-card-sec05-F004.teaching_text: Crash forces rip a child out of human arms, and an unbelted adult's body weight slams forward onto them.

sec05-card-sec05-F005.question_text: How do inertia-reel seat belts made after nineteen seventy-four behave during normal driving versus sudden braking?
sec05-card-sec05-F005.teaching_text: Feeling slack while leaning forward does not mean the belt is broken because abrupt deceleration locks the reel instantly.

sec05-card-sec05-F006.question_text: Why is a plain vehicle lap belt dangerous for a small child without an appropriate safety seat?
sec05-card-sec05-F006.teaching_text: Adult belt geometry concentrates violent collision load onto a young child's vulnerable hip and abdominal organs.

sec05-card-sec05-F007.question_text: How do child safety seats manage collision forces across a young passenger's body?
sec05-card-sec05-F007.teaching_text: Distributing impact energy over a wider surface shields fragile bones and internal organs during sudden stops.

sec05-card-sec05-F008.question_text: Beyond crash impact protection, how does properly restraining a child help the driver during everyday trips?
sec05-card-sec05-F008.teaching_text: Keeping young passengers buckled securely in place lets you keep your eyes and hands on traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-F009.question_text: What is Alaska's general rule on safety-belt use for motor-vehicle occupants?
sec05-card-sec05-F009.teaching_text: Unless one of the narrow statutory exceptions applies, every person riding in a motor vehicle must buckle up.

sec05-card-sec05-F010.question_text: At what age can an unbelted passenger be cited directly, and for which younger riders is the driver responsible?
sec05-card-sec05-F010.teaching_text: Passengers eighteen and up own their own seat-belt tickets, while the driver answers legally for anyone under sixteen.

sec05-card-sec05-F011.question_text: What must the driver do before transporting any child younger than sixteen?
sec05-card-sec05-F011.teaching_text: Even in a carpool, the person behind the wheel must provide and fasten proper protection before rolling.

sec05-card-sec05-F012.question_text: Which infants and young children must ride in an approved rear-facing child safety seat under Alaska law?
sec05-card-sec05-F012.teaching_text: Turning a baby forward before both age one and twenty pounds violates statute and endangers neck support.

sec05-card-sec05-F013.question_text: What restraint rule applies to a child aged one to under five who weighs at least twenty pounds?
sec05-card-sec05-F013.teaching_text: Toddlers and preschoolers at twenty pounds or more stay in an approved child restraint per manufacturer rules until five.

sec05-card-sec05-F014.question_text: What age, height, and weight bracket requires a child to use a specified booster or approved child-restraint system?
sec05-card-sec05-F014.teaching_text: Children older than four and under eight who are under fifty-seven inches and between twenty and sixty-five pounds need boosters.

sec05-card-sec05-F015.question_text: How must a child older than four be restrained once they exceed the statutory booster height or weight limits?
sec05-card-sec05-F015.teaching_text: Once a child past four tops fifty-seven inches or sixty-five pounds, securing them with a safety belt is required.

sec05-card-sec05-F016.question_text: Who chooses between an approved child restraint and a safety belt for a child aged eight through fifteen still under booster size limits?
sec05-card-sec05-F016.teaching_text: When an eight-to-fifteen-year-old remains under fifty-seven inches or sixty-five pounds, Alaska assigns that fit judgment to the driver.

sec05-card-sec05-F017.question_text: Under what three conditions is an older vehicle exempt from Alaska's seat-belt law?
sec05-card-sec05-F017.teaching_text: Classic cars built before nineteen sixty-five qualify only if manufactured without belts and not registered as custom collectors.

sec05-card-sec05-F018.question_text: When are mail or newspaper delivery drivers exempt from wearing a safety belt?
sec05-card-sec05-F018.teaching_text: Reaching from inside the cab to roadside boxes during paid delivery routes is exempt, unlike commuting home afterward.

sec05-card-sec05-F019.question_text: When are school-bus passengers exempt from Alaska's safety-belt requirement?
sec05-card-sec05-F019.teaching_text: Riders on standard compartmented buses are exempt unless that specific bus is legally required to carry belts.

sec05-card-sec05-F020.question_text: How does Alaska's seat-belt law treat passengers riding in emergency vehicles?
sec05-card-sec05-F020.teaching_text: Medics and responders tending patients in emergency rigs are listed among statutory exceptions to the belt requirement.

sec05-card-sec05-F021.question_text: Which state official may exempt specific people or classes of people from the seat-belt law by regulation?
sec05-card-sec05-F021.teaching_text: Special medical or occupational exemptions granted under regulations come from the Commissioner of Public Safety.

sec05-card-sec05-F022.question_text: What fine and point penalty can a driver face for failing to restrain a passenger younger than sixteen?
sec05-card-sec05-F022.teaching_text: Unlike an adult ticket with zero points, leaving a child unrestrained hits the driver's record with two demerit points.

sec05-card-sec05-F023.question_text: What dollar fine does the Alaska handbook list for an adult's seat-belt violation?
sec05-card-sec05-F023.teaching_text: Compare the two numbers carefully because adult belt violations list a fifteen-dollar fine while child restraint violations reach fifty.

sec05-card-sec05-F024.question_text: How can a court waive the fifteen-dollar adult seat-belt fine?
sec05-card-sec05-F024.teaching_text: Giving fifteen dollars to an approved emergency-medical-services group and submitting your citation copy plus receipt waives the fine.

sec05-card-sec05-F025.question_text: Who trains and educates caregivers on correctly installing and using child seats, boosters, and vehicle restraints?
sec05-card-sec05-F025.teaching_text: Certified technicians help families eliminate loose straps or wrong belt routing before a crash tests the seat.

sec05-card-sec05-F026.question_text: Beyond minimum legal age, how long does pediatric best-practice guidance recommend keeping infants and toddlers rear-facing?
sec05-card-sec05-F026.teaching_text: Riding rear-facing up to the seat maker's top height or weight cradles a toddler's head and spine best.

sec05-card-sec05-F027.question_text: Once a child outgrows their rear-facing seat limit, what does pediatric guidance recommend next and for how long?
sec05-card-sec05-F027.teaching_text: Five-point harnesses spread crash load far better than rushing a young child into a booster early.

sec05-card-sec05-F028.question_text: After outgrowing a forward-facing harness seat, how long does pediatric guidance recommend keeping a child in a booster?
sec05-card-sec05-F028.teaching_text: Boosters lift the child so the vehicle's lap-and-shoulder straps sit across strong hip and collarbone bones.

sec05-card-sec05-F029.question_text: At roughly what height and age range does proper vehicle belt fit usually happen in the manual's best-practice guidance?
sec05-card-sec05-F029.teaching_text: Keep law versus guidance distinct because four feet nine inches is pediatric best practice while fifty-seven inches governs booster law.

sec05-card-sec05-F030.question_text: How should children who are large enough for the vehicle belt wear it for best protection?
sec05-card-sec05-F030.teaching_text: Tucking the shoulder strap behind a child's back invites severe head and chest injuries in a crash.

sec05-card-sec05-F031.question_text: Below what age does the handbook's pediatric best-practice guidance recommend seating children in the rear?
sec05-card-sec05-F031.teaching_text: Back-seat placement keeps kids younger than thirteen away from front-dash impact zones and deploying front airbags.

sec05-card-sec05-F032.question_text: What two basics make car seats and boosters actually protect children in a crash?
sec05-card-sec05-F032.teaching_text: Even an expensive safety seat fails if it does not fit the child's current size or is buckled loosely.

sec05-card-sec05-F033.question_text: What should you do with your phone before shifting into gear and starting a drive?
sec05-card-sec05-F033.teaching_text: Cutting notification pings before moving eliminates the reflex to glance down at a lit screen in traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-F034.question_text: How can a phone's driving-status message reduce pressure to answer calls or texts on the road?
sec05-card-sec05-F034.teaching_text: Letting callers know automatically that you are driving removes social pressure to reply while moving.

sec05-card-sec05-F035.question_text: What should a solo driver do first before placing a necessary phone call?
sec05-card-sec05-F035.teaching_text: Parking in a safe spot off active lanes lets you dial and talk without splitting visual attention.

sec05-card-sec05-F036.question_text: When you have someone riding with you, how should a necessary phone call be handled?
sec05-card-sec05-F036.teaching_text: Handing phone duty to a passenger keeps both your hands on the wheel and your focus ahead.

sec05-card-sec05-F037.question_text: How does the Alaska manual classify texting, browsing the web, or reading email while driving?
sec05-card-sec05-F037.teaching_text: Reading or typing on screens steals seconds of highway sight distance and breaks Alaska law.

sec05-card-sec05-F038.question_text: Whose phone-use rules should you verify before driving across Alaska communities?
sec05-card-sec05-F038.teaching_text: Municipalities can enforce stricter handheld phone ordinances on top of statewide texting prohibitions.

sec05-card-sec05-F039.question_text: When should you review maps and directions, and how should mid-trip route checks happen?
sec05-card-sec05-F039.teaching_text: Studying routes while rolling pulls eyes off traffic, so plan ahead, ask a rider, or pull over safely.

sec05-card-sec05-F040.question_text: What should you do with pets before starting a trip?
sec05-card-sec05-F040.teaching_text: Loose animals can climb into your lap or under brake pedals the moment traffic slows abruptly.

sec05-card-sec05-F041.question_text: How should a driver handle a problem involving children inside the vehicle?
sec05-card-sec05-F041.teaching_text: Twisting around toward the back seat while moving sends your car drifting across lanes in a heartbeat.

sec05-card-sec05-F042.question_text: Which non-phone habits does the manual tell drivers to avoid so eyes and attention stay on the road?
sec05-card-sec05-F042.teaching_text: Smoking, eating, drinking, reading, or playing videos steals visual and manual control just as fast as texting.

sec06-card-sec06-F001.question_text: What three capabilities define having full control of your vehicle?
sec06-card-sec06-F001.teaching_text: True control means steering accurately, managing pace smoothly, and slowing or halting whenever conditions demand.

sec06-card-sec06-F002.question_text: Which three personal states or habits can undermine your ability to control a vehicle safely?
sec06-card-sec06-F002.teaching_text: Driving exhausted, angry, or distracted slows hazard recognition and ruins smooth steering and braking judgment.

sec06-card-sec06-F003.question_text: What legal duty of care applies around walkers, cyclists, wildlife, and other vehicles?
sec06-card-sec06-F003.teaching_text: Technical right-of-way never excuses hitting someone; Alaska law requires due care and slowing or stopping whenever needed.

sec06-card-sec06-F004.question_text: Which roadside users and roadway features call for heightened driver caution?
sec06-card-sec06-F004.teaching_text: Curves, steep downgrades, bridges, rail tracks, intersections, animals, and shoulder walkers shrink your margin for error.

sec06-card-sec06-F005.question_text: What message do roadside red reflectors, red flags, and lit flares send to approaching drivers?
sec06-card-sec06-F005.teaching_text: Spotting red roadside markers or flares ahead warns of stalled vehicles, wide loads, or crash scenes needing immediate care.

sec06-card-sec06-F006.question_text: What kind of roadway hazard is marked by orange flags and orange signs?
sec06-card-sec06-F006.teaching_text: High-visibility orange always signals active or temporary roadwork where lane shifts, equipment, and crews sit close.

sec06-card-sec06-F007.question_text: Where should you look while backing up instead of relying solely on your mirrors?
sec06-card-sec06-F007.teaching_text: Turning to look directly through the back glass while creeping slowly reveals blind zones that flat mirrors miss.

sec06-card-sec06-F008.question_text: Which way do you turn the steering wheel to guide the back of your vehicle while reversing?
sec06-card-sec06-F008.teaching_text: Wanting the tail to go right means turning the top of the wheel right, even as the front nose swings opposite.

sec06-card-sec06-F009.question_text: Who has priority when a driver is backing across a sidewalk or into a street?
sec06-card-sec06-F009.teaching_text: Because rear visibility is restricted, a reversing motorist must yield to all street traffic and sidewalk pedestrians.

sec06-card-sec06-F010.question_text: What top speed does the Alaska handbook recommend when backing up?
sec06-card-sec06-F010.teaching_text: Keeping reverse speed at or under five miles per hour lets you stop within inches if someone steps behind you.

sec06-card-sec06-F011.question_text: What rule governs front-seat passenger counts and cargo placement near the driver?
sec06-card-sec06-F011.teaching_text: Overloading the front row or stacking gear on the dash blocks sightlines and interferes with steering and pedals.

sec06-card-sec06-F012.question_text: What does the Alaska manual state about texting and visual-screen devices while driving?
sec06-card-sec06-F012.teaching_text: Typing messages is illegal behind the wheel, and watching any active video or screen steals eyes off Alaskan roads.

sec06-card-sec06-F013.question_text: Which three real-time factors determine a reasonable and prudent following distance?
sec06-card-sec06-F013.teaching_text: A gap that works on dry summer pavement at thirty turns dangerously tight on icy winter highways.

sec06-card-sec06-F014.question_text: On a rural two-lane Alaska highway, how many trailing vehicles require a slower driver to pull over safely?
sec06-card-sec06-F014.teaching_text: Alaska's famous five-car turnout rule prevents frustrated passing trains along winding two-lane mountain highways.

sec06-card-sec06-F015.question_text: How do you measure the recommended four-second following cushion behind a lead vehicle?
sec06-card-sec06-F015.teaching_text: Starting your count as the car ahead passes a sign or shadow ensures four full seconds before your front bumper arrives.

sec06-card-sec06-F016.question_text: To at least how many seconds should you expand your following gap when towing a trailer or driving on slick roads?
sec06-card-sec06-F016.teaching_text: Extra trailer weight and wet or icy traction stretch braking distance far beyond dry passenger-car stops.

sec06-card-sec06-F017.question_text: How can the four-second counting method protect you when driving after dark?
sec06-card-sec06-F017.teaching_text: If your car reaches the outer edge of your headlight beam in under four seconds, you are outrunning your night sightline.

sec06-card-sec06-F018.question_text: How does Alaska's recommended four-second following cushion compare with the stated legal minimum?
sec06-card-sec06-F018.teaching_text: Exam questions test both numbers, contrasting two seconds as the bare legal floor against four seconds for safe everyday driving.

sec06-card-sec06-F019.question_text: How should your right foot respond when brake lights illuminate ahead?
sec06-card-sec06-F019.teaching_text: Pivoting your foot immediately over the brake pedal shaves precious reaction tenths off your stopping distance.

sec06-card-sec06-F020.question_text: What immediate collision danger is signaled when the space to the vehicle ahead keeps shrinking?
sec06-card-sec06-F020.teaching_text: Even before brake lights flash, a closing gap proves the lead car lifted off the gas or shifted down.

sec06-card-sec06-F021.question_text: How can you tell from far back whether a distant vehicle is rolling or completely stopped?
sec06-card-sec06-F021.teaching_text: Checking whether a distant vehicle moves relative to trees, signs, or guardrails spots a dead stop long before closing in.

sec06-card-sec06-F022.question_text: How does watching for trouble ahead of the car in front of you improve your safety?
sec06-card-sec06-F022.teaching_text: Spotting a merging moose or turning car two vehicles up lets you slow before the lead driver even hits the brakes.

sec06-card-sec06-F023.question_text: How should you maintain and use your brake lights to protect against being rear-ended?
sec06-card-sec06-F023.teaching_text: Wiping road grime off lenses and tapping the pedal lightly early wakes up distracted tailgaters behind you.

sec06-card-sec06-F024.question_text: What rear-visibility upkeep is essential for monitoring traffic behind you in Alaska weather?
sec06-card-sec06-F024.teaching_text: A frosted or snow-packed back window blinds your inside rear-view mirror to fast-closing vehicles on slick roads.

sec06-card-sec06-F025.question_text: Which three maneuvers should you signal early to warn following motorists?
sec06-card-sec06-F025.teaching_text: Early visual cues prevent the driver behind from accelerating right as you begin slowing or shifting lanes.

sec06-card-sec06-F026.question_text: How should you brake when someone follows behind you and a stop lies ahead?
sec06-card-sec06-F026.teaching_text: Stretching out your slowdown gives a close follower extra pavement and seconds to match your deceleration safely.

sec06-card-sec06-F027.question_text: Within what two boundaries should you keep pace with surrounding traffic?
sec06-card-sec06-F027.teaching_text: Blending smoothly with traffic cuts passing conflicts, yet never justifies breaking speed limits or outrunning bad weather.

sec06-card-sec06-F028.question_text: By what factor do impact force and braking distance multiply when speed doubles from 20 to 40 mph?
sec06-card-sec06-F028.teaching_text: Kinetic energy grows with the square of speed, so doubling your pace quadruples both crash violence and stopping distance.

sec06-card-sec06-F029.question_text: By what factor do impact force and braking distance increase when speed triples from 20 to 60 mph?
sec06-card-sec06-F029.teaching_text: Three times the speed squares into nine times the kinetic energy that your brakes or bumpers must absorb.

sec06-card-sec06-F030.question_text: By what factor do impact force and braking distance jump when speed rises from 20 to 80 mph?
sec06-card-sec06-F030.teaching_text: Four times the speed packs sixteen times the stopping distance and destructive crash energy.

sec06-card-sec06-F031.question_text: Which three real-world conditions must govern your chosen driving speed?
sec06-card-sec06-F031.teaching_text: Posted numbers reflect ideal dry daylight, so real road surfaces, traffic volume, and weather dictate safe pace.

sec06-card-sec06-F032.question_text: What is Alaska's maximum speed limit in an unposted alley under favorable conditions?
sec06-card-sec06-F032.teaching_text: Blind garage exits, dumpsters, and narrow walls make 15 miles per hour the top safe ceiling in alleys.

sec06-card-sec06-F033.question_text: What default speed limit applies in an unposted Alaska business district under favorable conditions?
sec06-card-sec06-F033.teaching_text: Note Alaska's 20-mph business-district rule carefully, since many other states set commercial streets at 25.

sec06-card-sec06-F034.question_text: What is the unposted maximum speed limit in an Alaska school zone under favorable conditions?
sec06-card-sec06-F034.teaching_text: Matching business districts at 20 miles per hour protects children crossing around buses and schoolyards.

sec06-card-sec06-F035.question_text: What default maximum speed applies in an unposted Alaska residential neighborhood under favorable conditions?
sec06-card-sec06-F035.teaching_text: Neighborhood streets allow 25 miles per hour under clear conditions unless local signs establish a different limit.

sec06-card-sec06-F036.question_text: What default maximum applies on other unposted Alaska roadways, and what higher limit may selected highways post?
sec06-card-sec06-F036.teaching_text: Keep 55 locked in for unposted open roads while remembering selected major highways post signs up to 65.

sec06-card-sec06-F037.question_text: Which two government authorities have legal power to alter Alaska's default speed limits?
sec06-card-sec06-F037.teaching_text: Municipalities and the state transportation department adjust zone speeds wherever crash data, geometry, or access warrants.

sec06-card-sec06-F038.question_text: Which five factors must a careful and prudent speed account for when conditions turn unfavorable?
sec06-card-sec06-F038.teaching_text: Narrow lanes, glaze ice, blowing snow, heavy traffic, or fog demand dropping well below dry-pavement limits.

sec06-card-sec06-F039.question_text: How does your visible clear distance ahead cap how fast you may safely drive?
sec06-card-sec06-F039.teaching_text: Blind curves, hill crests, darkness, or whiteouts require a pace slow enough to halt before hitting an unseen obstruction.

sec06-card-sec06-F040.question_text: What rule restricts driving far below the normal pace of reasonable traffic?
sec06-card-sec06-F040.teaching_text: Creeping unnecessarily on clear highways triggers sudden braking and risky overtaking maneuvers behind you.

sec06-card-sec06-F041.question_text: How is reckless driving defined in Alaska, and what license penalty follows conviction?
sec06-card-sec06-F041.teaching_text: Showing willful disregard for life or property goes far beyond a simple ticket and triggers mandatory license revocation.

sec06-card-sec06-F042.question_text: Which lane must slower traffic use on a multilane highway when not passing?
sec06-card-sec06-F042.teaching_text: Staying in the right-hand outside lane leaves inside left lanes clear for faster vehicles to pass predictably.

sec06-card-sec06-F043.question_text: What must you do to protect emergency vehicles stopped along the highway shoulder?
sec06-card-sec06-F043.teaching_text: Vacating the lane next to flashing roadside emergency crews shields officers, medics, and firefighters from live traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-F044.question_text: What financial penalty applies to traffic violations committed inside designated Alaska traffic safety corridors?
sec06-card-sec06-F044.teaching_text: High-crash highway stretches carry doubled statutory fines to deter speeding and aggressive passing.

sec06-card-sec06-F045.question_text: For at least how many continuous feet before a turn or lane move must you signal in Alaska?
sec06-card-sec06-F045.teaching_text: Keeping your blinker or arm signal active through the final 100 feet gives cross and rear drivers unmistakable notice.

sec06-card-sec06-F046.question_text: When should you activate your turn signal earlier than the 100-foot legal minimum?
sec06-card-sec06-F046.teaching_text: At 55 mph a car covers 100 feet in barely over one second, so highway speeds and dense traffic warrant earlier warning.

sec06-card-sec06-F047.question_text: What communication duty applies right before stopping or slowing down abruptly?
sec06-card-sec06-F047.teaching_text: Alerting drivers behind you with brake lamps or an arm stop signal prevents chain-reaction rear-end impacts.

sec06-card-sec06-F048.question_text: Which four winter or road substances must you keep cleared off your turn-signal lights?
sec06-card-sec06-F048.teaching_text: Crusted Alaska road grit, glacial dust, snow, or ice can completely block amber and red signal flashes.

sec06-card-sec06-F049.question_text: Under which two visual conditions should you reinforce electric blinkers with hand-and-arm signals?
sec06-card-sec06-F049.teaching_text: Low-angle sun glare washes out bulb flashes, and a line of cars right behind you hides your taillights from vehicles farther back.

sec06-card-sec06-F050.question_text: Why is it critical to make sure your turn signal cancels after finishing a lane change or gentle turn?
sec06-card-sec06-F050.teaching_text: A forgotten flashing blinker tricks side-street drivers into pulling directly across your path expecting you to turn.

sec06-card-sec06-F051.question_text: Do turn-signaling duties apply to bicyclists on the road as well?
sec06-card-sec06-F051.teaching_text: Hand-and-arm turn cues let nearby drivers anticipate a rider's lane move or intersection turn cleanly.

sec07-card-sec07-F001.question_text: Turning left off a two-way road onto a one-way road, what steps apply and which lane receives you?
sec07-card-sec07-F001.teaching_text: After signaling 100 feet and yielding to traffic and walkers, turning into the nearest left lane keeps your arc tight.

sec07-card-sec07-F002.question_text: What cornering error must you avoid as you reach the crosswalk to start a turn?
sec07-card-sec07-F002.teaching_text: Turning early before clearing the near crosswalk slices straight across opposing stop lines and pedestrian zones.

sec07-card-sec07-F003.question_text: Moving from a one-way road onto a two-way road via a left turn, which approach lane and signal distance apply?
sec07-card-sec07-F003.teaching_text: Positioning in the extreme left curb lane of a one-way road prevents cutting across straight traffic on your left.

sec07-card-sec07-F004.question_text: When turning left from a one-way street onto a two-way street, where do you begin turning the wheel?
sec07-card-sec07-F004.teaching_text: Pulling out past the crosswalk into the junction first lines your car up cleanly with the proper side of the two-way street.

sec07-card-sec07-F005.question_text: How must your front wheels be aimed while paused waiting to turn left, and where should you check?
sec07-card-sec07-F005.teaching_text: Pre-cocking your wheels left means a rear-end tap shoves your car head-on into oncoming lanes.

sec07-card-sec07-F006.question_text: What lane habit and yielding duty apply before making any left turn?
sec07-card-sec07-F006.teaching_text: Getting into your left-turn lane early avoids last-second weaves while you wait for oncoming cars and crosswalk users.

sec07-card-sec07-F007.question_text: How should your vehicle's path finish a left turn?
sec07-card-sec07-F007.teaching_text: Neither cutting inside early nor drifting wide at the exit keeps multi-lane intersections predictable for everyone.

sec07-card-sec07-F008.question_text: Where should you scan at intersections to spot one-way street signs early?
sec07-card-sec07-F008.teaching_text: Checking signal poles and stop-sign posts before turning prevents accidentally swinging into wrong-way lanes.

sec07-card-sec07-F009.question_text: How do you turn left from one one-way street onto another intersecting one-way street?
sec07-card-sec07-F009.teaching_text: Curb-to-curb left turns between one-way streets cross zero through-lanes once pedestrians clear.

sec07-card-sec07-F010.question_text: What three steps prepare a safe right turn between two-way streets?
sec07-card-sec07-F010.teaching_text: Merging right early, signaling 100 feet, and checking the right curb prevents cutting off pedestrians or bikes.

sec07-card-sec07-F011.question_text: Why must you leave space and watch closely behind a car turning right ahead of you?
sec07-card-sec07-F011.teaching_text: Looking left for cross traffic while creeping behind a turning car causes rear-end taps when it stops mid-turn for a pedestrian.

sec07-card-sec07-F012.question_text: What specific collision type does timely turn signaling help prevent behind you?
sec07-card-sec07-F012.teaching_text: Signaling before touching the brake tells followers why you are slowing so they drop back early.

sec07-card-sec07-F013.question_text: When may you use a three-point turn to reverse direction?
sec07-card-sec07-F013.teaching_text: When a street is too tight for a U-turn and no signs or sightline hazards forbid it, a three-point turn reverses direction.

sec07-card-sec07-F014.question_text: How do you begin a three-point turn?
sec07-card-sec07-F014.teaching_text: Stopping snug along the right curb maximizes turning radius across the street and lets trailing cars pass first.

sec07-card-sec07-F015.question_text: What must you do after stopping on the right before swinging left across the road in a three-point turn?
sec07-card-sec07-F015.teaching_text: Swinging perpendicular across both lanes exposes your broadside, demanding a left signal and clear road both ways.

sec07-card-sec07-F016.question_text: After pulling across to the far curb during a three-point turnabout, how do you handle the reverse leg?
sec07-card-sec07-F016.teaching_text: Turning the wheel briskly all the way right while backing swings your nose around into the new travel direction.

sec07-card-sec07-F017.question_text: What final check belongs right after backing before you pull forward out of a three-point turn?
sec07-card-sec07-F017.teaching_text: New cars may round a corner while you reverse, so halt cleanly and verify clear lanes before accelerating away.

sec07-card-sec07-F018.question_text: Who holds right-of-way from both directions throughout an entire three-point turn?
sec07-card-sec07-F018.teaching_text: Because your turnaround blocks normal lanes, oncoming cars, cyclists, and walkers hold priority throughout every step.

sec07-card-sec07-F019.question_text: How should you manage your speed and control when approaching and crossing any intersection?
sec07-card-sec07-F019.teaching_text: Intersections concentrate cross traffic and foot crossings, requiring a controlled, reasonable pace ready for surprises.

sec07-card-sec07-F020.question_text: What makes an intersection classify as uncontrolled?
sec07-card-sec07-F020.teaching_text: Spotting the absence of stop signs, yield triangles, or overhead lights warns you to rely on statutory yield rules.

sec07-card-sec07-F021.question_text: Besides cars, what hidden crossing zones must you watch for while slowing at an uncontrolled crossroad?
sec07-card-sec07-F021.teaching_text: Every street corner connects unseen unmarked pedestrian crosswalks even where residential asphalt has zero paint.

sec07-card-sec07-F022.question_text: Does approaching an uncontrolled intersection from the right let you breeze through at full speed?
sec07-card-sec07-F022.teaching_text: Holding directional priority never cancels your duty to slow down and keep full control entering an open crossroad.

sec07-card-sec07-F023.question_text: When two vehicles approach an uncontrolled intersection on conflicting paths, which driver must yield?
sec07-card-sec07-F023.teaching_text: Giving priority to the vehicle on your right settles open-intersection conflicts with one universal rule.

sec07-card-sec07-F024.question_text: What two assumptions must a driver approaching from the right never make at an uncontrolled intersection?
sec07-card-sec07-F024.teaching_text: Another driver may miss the rule, and any car already inside the junction must be allowed to clear safely.

sec07-card-sec07-F025.question_text: How does the Alaska manual rank nonmotorized users versus motor vehicles at uncontrolled intersections?
sec07-card-sec07-F025.teaching_text: Walkers, cyclists, skiers, and other nonmotorized travelers receive priority over motor vehicles through uncontrolled crossroads.

sec07-card-sec07-F026.question_text: Which way does traffic circulate in a roundabout, and who yields at the entrance?
sec07-card-sec07-F026.teaching_text: Waiting for a gap in counterclockwise circulating traffic keeps the circle moving smoothly without signal delays.

sec07-card-sec07-F027.question_text: About what typical design speed range does the Alaska manual give for roundabouts?
sec07-card-sec07-F027.teaching_text: Note Alaska's 15-to-20-mph roundabout design figure for exam questions testing safe approach deceleration.
