sec07-card-sec07-F028.question_text: On which side of the central island do you enter a roundabout once a safe gap opens?
sec07-card-sec07-F028.teaching_text: Curving to the right of the center island feeds every entry cleanly into counterclockwise flow.

sec07-card-sec07-F029.question_text: Where must you watch for and yield to pedestrians and bicyclists at a roundabout?
sec07-card-sec07-F029.teaching_text: Scanning both inside the circle and across marked exit-leg crosswalks prevents hitting walkers as you accelerate out.

sec07-card-sec07-F030.question_text: Once circulating inside a roundabout, should you stop or follow lane-use signs and markings?
sec07-card-sec07-F030.teaching_text: Stopping mid-circle risks immediate rear-end collisions behind you; follow painted lane guides smoothly to your exit.

sec07-card-sec07-F031.question_text: When must you pick your lane for a multilane roundabout?
sec07-card-sec07-F031.teaching_text: Selecting your lane on the approach prevents risky last-second weaving across spiral stripes inside the circle.

sec07-card-sec07-F032.question_text: According to the Alaska handbook, if another entering vehicle reaches a roundabout simultaneously with you, who do you yield to besides circulating traffic?
sec07-card-sec07-F032.teaching_text: Alaska's manual pairs standard circle priority with yielding to a simultaneous entering driver on your right.

sec07-card-sec07-F033.question_text: What is the safe recovery move if you miss your intended exit inside a roundabout?
sec07-card-sec07-F033.teaching_text: Diving sharply across an outer lane to salvage an exit causes sideswipes when another quick lap takes seconds.

sec07-card-sec07-F034.question_text: Which vehicles hold priority when you prepare to enter an intersection?
sec07-card-sec07-F034.teaching_text: Never pull out ahead of cars already clearing the junction or closing fast enough to create a crash hazard.

sec07-card-sec07-F035.question_text: Where must you stop when needed before entering a protected through-route?
sec07-card-sec07-F035.teaching_text: Halting behind unmarked corner crosswalks keeps side-street hoods clear of walkers and cyclists along the main route.

sec07-card-sec07-F036.question_text: When your red light turns green, who still holds priority before you accelerate forward?
sec07-card-sec07-F036.teaching_text: A green bulb permits entry only after pedestrians and turning cars lawfully caught mid-junction finish clearing.

sec07-card-sec07-F037.question_text: What two actions are mandatory before pulling onto a road from an alley, driveway, or building exit?
sec07-card-sec07-F037.teaching_text: Walls and snowbanks hide approaching sidewalk walkers and street traffic until you stop and scan carefully.

sec07-card-sec07-F038.question_text: May you exceed the posted speed limit briefly to pass a slower vehicle, and what checks come first?
sec07-card-sec07-F038.teaching_text: Many drivers mistakenly think passing grants a speed-limit exemption, when Alaska requires staying within the posted maximum.

sec07-card-sec07-F039.question_text: Where are the three proper stopping points at a stop sign depending on markings?
sec07-card-sec07-F039.teaching_text: Halting behind the crosswalk, painted stop bar, or intersecting shoulder line keeps cross-traffic lanes completely unobstructed.

sec07-card-sec07-F040.question_text: How must you treat a flashing red traffic signal?
sec07-card-sec07-F040.teaching_text: Flashing red works just like a stop sign, requiring a full wheel halt and clear cross-traffic before moving.

sec07-card-sec07-F041.question_text: How long must you stay halted at a lowered railroad gate or a flagger's stop paddle?
sec07-card-sec07-F041.teaching_text: Moving before the gate lifts or the flagger drops the stop sign puts you directly into train or work-equipment paths.

sec07-card-sec07-F042.question_text: What basic duty applies whenever a steady red traffic signal faces your lane?
sec07-card-sec07-F042.teaching_text: Steady red assigns the intersection to conflicting cross movements, requiring a full stop before the line.

sec07-card-sec07-F043.question_text: When does a yield sign require coming to a complete stop?
sec07-card-sec07-F043.teaching_text: Slowing suffices when cross lanes are empty, yet stopping becomes mandatory whenever pedestrians or close cars approach.

sec07-card-sec07-F044.question_text: When must drivers approaching or following a school bus stop?
sec07-card-sec07-F044.teaching_text: Flashing red lights and an extended stop arm warn that schoolchildren are actively stepping across live pavement.

sec07-card-sec07-F045.question_text: What does the Alaska manual require when traffic signals at an intersection stop working?
sec07-card-sec07-F045.teaching_text: Power outages leave every direction unprotected, so treating dark signal heads as a mandatory stop prevents high-speed T-bones.

sec07-card-sec07-F046.question_text: Why should you stay well back rather than tailgating right before pulling left to pass?
sec07-card-sec07-F046.teaching_text: Hanging back preserves a wide sightline past the lead bumper while you check mirrors and signal left.

sec07-card-sec07-F047.question_text: May you cross the centerline briefly just to peek around a vehicle ahead for oncoming traffic?
sec07-card-sec07-F047.teaching_text: Nosing across yellow paint to look puts your left front corner directly into fast oncoming traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-F048.question_text: What audible cue does the Alaska handbook instruct a passing driver to give?
sec07-card-sec07-F048.teaching_text: A brief warning tap alerts the lead motorist not to drift left or start passing at the same moment.

sec07-card-sec07-F049.question_text: What three steps finish a left-side pass cleanly once you clear the overtaken car?
sec07-card-sec07-F049.teaching_text: Signaling right, waiting until safely past, and canceling your blinker afterward prevents cutting off the car behind.

sec07-card-sec07-F050.question_text: May you use the right highway shoulder to overtake another vehicle in Alaska?
sec07-card-sec07-F050.teaching_text: Alaska shoulders hold loose gravel, soft edges, parked cars, and cyclists where nobody expects high-speed passing.

sec07-card-sec07-F051.question_text: When is passing prohibited near a hill crest or curve?
sec07-card-sec07-F051.teaching_text: Blind crests and bends hide fast oncoming vehicles until closing time is far too short to abort.

sec07-card-sec07-F052.question_text: Before what pavement marking begins on your side must a pass be completely finished?
sec07-card-sec07-F052.teaching_text: Sliding back right after a solid yellow no-passing stripe starts puts you inside a blind conflict zone.

sec07-card-sec07-F053.question_text: What does Alaska law say about pressing the gas while another driver is overtaking you?
sec07-card-sec07-F053.teaching_text: Blocking a passing car traps both vehicles beside oncoming traffic and violates Alaska statute.

sec07-card-sec07-F054.question_text: What does a solid yellow stripe on your side of the centerline forbid?
sec07-card-sec07-F054.teaching_text: Engineers paint solid yellow on your side wherever curves, hills, or junctions erase safe passing sight distance.

sec07-card-sec07-F055.question_text: Where is passing a school bus with flashing red lights and an extended stop arm prohibited?
sec07-card-sec07-F055.teaching_text: Both directions stop on undivided two-way roads, and all same-side lanes stop on divided roadways.

sec07-card-sec07-F056.question_text: Within what distance before an intersection or railroad crossing is passing illegal?
sec07-card-sec07-F056.teaching_text: Cross-street turners and trains create acute conflict zones within 100 feet of or across junctions and tracks.

sec07-card-sec07-F057.question_text: How far before a posted narrow bridge, viaduct, or tunnel is passing prohibited?
sec07-card-sec07-F057.teaching_text: Pinched bridge decks, viaducts, and tunnels eliminate shoulder escape space, barring passing for 100 feet beforehand.

sec07-card-sec07-F058.question_text: What is the proper use of a shared center turning lane, and may you use it to pass?
sec07-card-sec07-F058.teaching_text: Using a two-way left-turn lane as a passing chute sets up head-on collisions with opposing left-turners.

sec07-card-sec07-F059.question_text: Does passing an End No Passing Zone sign or returning to dashed yellow guarantee it is safe to pass?
sec07-card-sec07-F059.teaching_text: Road geometry has opened up, yet real-time oncoming cars, weather, or speed still require your independent check.

sec08-card-sec08-F001.question_text: Which three primary jobs do highway traffic signs perform for drivers?
sec08-card-sec08-F001.teaching_text: Every roadside panel fits one of three core missions by warning of hazards, guiding navigation, or stating traffic law.

sec08-card-sec08-F002.question_text: Which three habits must every driver practice around roadway signs?
sec08-card-sec08-F002.teaching_text: Knowing each symbol by shape and color lets you spot instructions blocks early and comply smoothly.

sec08-card-sec08-F003.question_text: What color combinations generally appear on regulatory signs, and what is their legal force?
sec08-card-sec08-F003.teaching_text: White regulatory panels carry binding legal rules rather than optional suggestions, backing violations with citations.

sec08-card-sec08-F004.question_text: What colors appear on a standard stop sign, and where must your car halt?
sec08-card-sec08-F004.teaching_text: Stopping completely at the painted line or before the crosswalk and intersection keeps pedestrian lanes open.

sec08-card-sec08-F005.question_text: Once your wheels stop completely at a stop sign, what must you do before pulling forward?
sec08-card-sec08-F005.teaching_text: A legal stop is only half the rule; cross-street vehicles and pedestrians hold priority before you enter.

sec08-card-sec08-F006.question_text: What actions does a red-and-white downward triangle yield sign require?
sec08-card-sec08-F006.teaching_text: Decelerating early lets you scan both approaches and stop cleanly whenever pedestrians or cross cars conflict.

sec08-card-sec08-F007.question_text: Where is a red-and-white Do Not Enter sign placed, and what does it forbid?
sec08-card-sec08-F007.teaching_text: Facing drivers who approach a one-way street or exit ramp backward, it forbids proceeding past the post.

sec08-card-sec08-F008.question_text: What red rectangular sign with white letters may appear farther down a prohibited entry path?
sec08-card-sec08-F008.teaching_text: If a distracted driver misses Do Not Enter at the corner, Wrong Way panels farther along demand immediate safe recovery.

sec08-card-sec08-F009.question_text: What do black-on-yellow warning signs alert you to, and what response do they usually call for?
sec08-card-sec08-F009.teaching_text: Yellow diamonds flag curves, merges, or slick bridges ahead so you ease off the gas early.

sec08-card-sec08-F010.question_text: What colors appear on highway guide signs, and what four types of navigation info do they give?
sec08-card-sec08-F010.teaching_text: Green highway boards display destinations, route numbers, place names, and mileage early enough for calm lane changes.

sec08-card-sec08-F011.question_text: What do black-on-orange signs mark, and how should your driving adjust?
sec08-card-sec08-F011.teaching_text: Orange signals temporary construction or maintenance zones where narrowed lanes and workers require adjusted speed.

sec08-card-sec08-F012.question_text: How many sides does a school warning sign have, and how must you react upon seeing one?
sec08-card-sec08-F012.teaching_text: House-shaped five-sided school signs warn of school grounds or crossings ahead so you slow and cover the brake.

sec08-card-sec08-F013.question_text: What motorist amenities can white-on-blue roadside service signs point out in Alaska?
sec08-card-sec08-F013.teaching_text: Along remote Alaska highways, blue panels mark vital fuel, phones, food, lodging, campgrounds, rest stops, and litter barrels.

sec08-card-sec08-F014.question_text: What universal meaning does a red circle with a diagonal red slash carry?
sec08-card-sec08-F014.teaching_text: Crossing any black turn arrow, U-turn, or vehicle icon with a red diagonal bar instantly bans that action.

sec08-card-sec08-F015.question_text: May a driver travel faster than a posted speed-limit sign?
sec08-card-sec08-F015.teaching_text: Posted speed panels establish the legal top ceiling under favorable conditions and may never be exceeded.

sec08-card-sec08-F016.question_text: What must you do at an intersection displaying a No Right Turn on Red sign when cross traffic looks completely empty?
sec08-card-sec08-F016.teaching_text: Posted red-turn bans protect blind corners or heavy pedestrian phases even when the lane looks wide open.

sec08-card-sec08-F017.question_text: For what sole purpose may you enter a center lane marked exclusively for left turns?
sec08-card-sec08-F017.teaching_text: Driving straight or passing inside a dedicated center left-turn lane risks head-on crashes with opposing turners.

sec08-card-sec08-F018.question_text: On which side of a Keep Right regulatory sign must you steer your vehicle?
sec08-card-sec08-F018.teaching_text: Keep Right panels sit on divider noses to keep cars from straying left into oncoming lanes.

sec08-card-sec08-F019.question_text: Where does a posted No Parking sign forbid leaving your car?
sec08-card-sec08-F019.teaching_text: Arrows and wording on no-parking plaques define the exact curb stretch or side kept clear for flow or snowplows.

sec08-card-sec08-F020.question_text: What may you do along a curb posted No Stopping, Standing, or Parking?
sec08-card-sec08-F020.teaching_text: Even pausing briefly with the engine running to drop off a friend violates a full no-stopping restriction.

sec08-card-sec08-F021.question_text: What movement is required once you occupy a lane marked for a mandatory left turn?
sec08-card-sec08-F021.teaching_text: Continuing straight out of a mandatory turn-only lane cuts straight across neighboring turners or narrow shoulders.

sec08-card-sec08-F022.question_text: What travel rule does a black-and-white One Way arrow sign establish?
sec08-card-sec08-F022.teaching_text: All lanes on a one-way roadway move solely toward the pointed arrow, barring opposite-direction turns.

sec08-card-sec08-F023.question_text: What must the operator of a heavy vehicle do when its weight exceeds a posted weight-limit sign?
sec08-card-sec08-F023.teaching_text: Bridge decks and thawing spring roads suffer structural collapse or rutting under loads heavier than posted limits.

sec08-card-sec08-F024.question_text: What maneuver may a lane-narrowing regulatory or warning instruction direct right-lane drivers to make?
sec08-card-sec08-F024.teaching_text: When the right lane drops ahead, matching speed and merging left early avoids squeezing onto gravel shoulders.

sec08-card-sec08-F025.question_text: What precaution may be required when approaching a single-lane one-way bridge in Alaska?
sec08-card-sec08-F025.teaching_text: Single-lane backcountry bridges fit only one direction at a time, requiring a stop whenever an oncoming vehicle is crossing.

sec08-card-sec08-F026.question_text: Which side must you keep to on a divided highway and when meeting opposing traffic on a two-way road?
sec08-card-sec08-F026.teaching_text: Divided Highway and Two-Way Traffic warnings remind you after medians start or end to stay right of opposing lanes.

sec08-card-sec08-F027.question_text: How should you respond to a Slippery When Wet warning sign during rain or frost?
sec08-card-sec08-F027.teaching_text: Shaded bridges and polished asphalt lose grip rapidly under frost or rain, making gentle steering and lower speed critical.

sec08-card-sec08-F028.question_text: What does a yellow Traffic Signal Ahead symbol sign prepare you for?
sec08-card-sec08-F028.teaching_text: Curves, hills, or sun glare can hide an upcoming intersection light until stopping room is tight at highway speed.

sec08-card-sec08-F029.question_text: What traffic movement does a right-side Merging Traffic warning sign alert you to?
sec08-card-sec08-F029.teaching_text: Scanning the right ramp early lets you adjust speed or shift left so merging cars blend smoothly.

sec08-card-sec08-F030.question_text: What must a tall camper, box truck, or load do if it exceeds a Low Clearance warning height?
sec08-card-sec08-F030.teaching_text: Wedging a tall roof or cargo rack under a low bridge shears structures and showers debris onto traffic behind.

sec08-card-sec08-F031.question_text: Which animals does the Alaska handbook highlight on wildlife-crossing warnings, and how can they enter the road?
sec08-card-sec08-F031.teaching_text: Deer and caribou bolt out of brush ditches without warning, especially near dawn and dusk.

sec08-card-sec08-F032.question_text: How should you adjust pace when entering a highway ramp with a posted ramp speed?
sec08-card-sec08-F032.teaching_text: Highway cruising numbs speed sense, and tight exit loops roll top-heavy SUVs if entered too fast.

sec08-card-sec08-F033.question_text: What speed adjustment is called for by a curve or winding-road warning paired with an advisory plaque?
sec08-card-sec08-F033.teaching_text: Brake down to the yellow advisory speed on the straight approach before turning the wheel into the bend.

sec08-card-sec08-F034.question_text: What driver awareness does a posted Bike Route sign call for?
sec08-card-sec08-F034.teaching_text: Designated bike corridors concentrate riders along shoulders and intersections, requiring extra mirror and passing care.

sec08-card-sec08-F035.question_text: What do Road Closed and Detour signs instruct motorists to do?
sec08-card-sec08-F035.teaching_text: Driving past closure barricades puts you into washed-out culverts, open trenches, or active paving crews.

sec08-card-sec08-F036.question_text: What action must an orange Flagger Ahead warning sign immediately prepare you for?
sec08-card-sec08-F036.teaching_text: Single-lane alternating work zones often halt traffic around blind bends right past the advance flagger sign.

sec08-card-sec08-F037.question_text: How far ahead can an advance construction-area warning sign alert you to roadwork?
sec08-card-sec08-F037.teaching_text: Five hundred feet gives you just a few highway seconds to lift off the gas and scan for cones.

sec08-card-sec08-F038.question_text: Where must you watch for highway workers when passing roadwork signs?
sec08-card-sec08-F038.teaching_text: Surveyors and maintenance crews work both directly on asphalt lanes and along narrow gravel shoulders.

sec08-card-sec08-F039.question_text: Who may legally park in a stall marked reserved for disability plates or placards?
sec08-card-sec08-F039.teaching_text: Accessible stalls keep wide ramp and aisle clearance open exclusively for authorized disability credentials.

sec08-card-sec08-F040.question_text: What two jobs do orange barricades, panels, cones, tubes, and drums perform in a work zone?
sec08-card-sec08-F040.teaching_text: Channelizing markers outline temporary lane edges clearly past drop-offs, trenches, and heavy paving gear.

sec08-card-sec08-F041.question_text: What extra visibility feature is often mounted on work-zone channelizing devices at night?
sec08-card-sec08-F041.teaching_text: Top-mounted beacons help drivers read curved cone tapers in dark rain or blowing snow.

sec08-card-sec08-F042.question_text: When do flashing or sequencing work-zone arrow panels operate, and what do they indicate?
sec08-card-sec08-F042.teaching_text: Bright sequential arrows cut through both midday glare and midnight darkness to signal an upcoming lane merge.

sec08-card-sec08-F043.question_text: Which three traffic-control actions may a work-zone flagger direct drivers to take?
sec08-card-sec08-F043.teaching_text: Flaggers coordinate single-lane alternating flow around haul trucks and pavers, carrying full legal authority.

sec08-card-sec08-F044.question_text: What high-visibility color do flaggers typically wear, and which two tools do they use to direct you?
sec08-card-sec08-F044.teaching_text: Spotting fluorescent orange vests paired with stop-and-slow paddles or red flags tells you who controls the lane.

sec10-card-sec10-F001.question_text: Where must you bring your vehicle to a stop at a steady circular red light?
sec10-card-sec10-F001.teaching_text: Stopping short of painted lines or the corner entry keeps pedestrian paths and cross lanes clear.

sec10-card-sec10-F002.question_text: Under what three conditions may you turn right at a steady circular red light?
sec10-card-sec10-F002.teaching_text: Rolling a red turn or ignoring a posted ban risks hitting crosswalk walkers and fast cross-traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-F003.question_text: What does a steady circular yellow light warn, and when must you stop for it?
sec10-card-sec10-F003.teaching_text: Treating yellow as a speed-up cue risks entering on red unless you are already too close to stop safely.

sec10-card-sec10-F004.question_text: How should you drive if the signal turns yellow right as you enter the intersection?
sec10-card-sec10-F004.teaching_text: Slamming brakes inside the box invites rear-end hits, so clear through alertly instead.

sec10-card-sec10-F005.question_text: When does a steady circular green signal allow you to make a legal movement?
sec10-card-sec10-F005.teaching_text: Green never overrides gridlocked cross traffic or a posted sign barring a turn.

sec10-card-sec10-F006.question_text: Who still gets right-of-way even after your circular signal turns green?
sec10-card-sec10-F006.teaching_text: Launching on fresh green without letting lingering walkers and cars clear causes preventable intersection crashes.

sec10-card-sec10-F007.question_text: Who holds priority when you turn left on a steady circular green signal?
sec10-card-sec10-F007.teaching_text: A plain green ball gives no protected left phase, so straight-moving opposing cars go first.

sec10-card-sec10-F008.question_text: What does a steady red arrow prohibit, and where must you stop?
sec10-card-sec10-F008.teaching_text: Stopping behind the crosswalk, stop line, or corner keeps your nose out of conflicting lanes.

sec10-card-sec10-F009.question_text: In Alaska, when may you finally turn in a direction controlled by a steady red arrow?
sec10-card-sec10-F009.teaching_text: Unlike a circular red, Alaska's handbook bars turning on a steady red arrow until the arrow changes.

sec10-card-sec10-F010.question_text: What does a steady yellow arrow warn, and how should you respond?
sec10-card-sec10-F010.teaching_text: Protected or permissive turn time is ending, so stop unless already committed inside or too close.

sec10-card-sec10-F011.question_text: What does a green arrow permit, and what duty still applies?
sec10-card-sec10-F011.teaching_text: Even protected green arrows require alertness for walkers or cars lawfully inside the intersection.

sec10-card-sec10-F012.question_text: What sequence is required at a flashing circular red signal?
sec10-card-sec10-F012.teaching_text: Flashing circular red acts like a stop sign, demanding a full halt and all-way scan first.

sec10-card-sec10-F013.question_text: Why is a flashing red beacon sometimes mounted with a stop sign?
sec10-card-sec10-F013.teaching_text: Extra flashing red light draws driver eyes early at rural, high-speed, or crash-prone stops.

sec10-card-sec10-F014.question_text: What must you do before moving in the direction of a flashing red arrow?
sec10-card-sec10-F014.teaching_text: Treat a flashing red arrow as a stop-then-yield control for its pointed lane.

sec10-card-sec10-F015.question_text: How should you respond to a flashing circular yellow traffic signal?
sec10-card-sec10-F015.teaching_text: Easing speed lets you spot walkers or cross cars already occupying the hazard intersection.

sec10-card-sec10-F016.question_text: Who must you yield to before turning on a flashing yellow arrow?
sec10-card-sec10-F016.teaching_text: Flashing yellow arrows allow turns only during safe gaps after opposing traffic and crosswalks clear.

sec10-card-sec10-F017.question_text: What must you do first when all signal bulbs for your direction are dark and nobody is directing traffic?
sec10-card-sec10-F017.teaching_text: Blowing straight through a power outage causes high-speed broadsides with cross-street drivers.

sec10-card-sec10-F018.question_text: After stopping at an unlit signalized intersection, how do you determine priority and proceed?
sec10-card-sec10-F018.teaching_text: Following uncontrolled-corner right-hand yield rules keeps drivers from launching into each other during blackouts.

sec10-card-sec10-F019.question_text: Whom should you notify as soon as possible after encountering an inoperative traffic signal?
sec10-card-sec10-F019.teaching_text: Promptly alerting police speeds up flagger dispatch and repair before a crash occurs.

sec10-card-sec10-F020.question_text: Whose traffic directions override posted signs and operating traffic signals?
sec10-card-sec10-F020.teaching_text: Live responders see crash scenes, fire hoses, or work-zone hazards invisible to automated signal timers.

sec10-card-sec10-F021.question_text: How does a solid orange raised hand or don't-walk display rule curb walkers versus mid-street walkers?
sec10-card-sec10-F021.teaching_text: Stepping off the curb on a steady hand puts walkers straight into green cross-traffic phases.

sec10-card-sec10-F022.question_text: How does a flashing orange raised hand without a countdown govern crosswalk entry and completion?
sec10-card-sec10-F022.teaching_text: Clearance time covers walkers already in the stripes, not late curb step-offs.

sec10-card-sec10-F023.question_text: What does a pedestrian countdown timer show, and what happens when it hits zero?
sec10-card-sec10-F023.teaching_text: Zero marks the end of pedestrian clearance as the hand turns solid and numbers go dark.

sec10-card-sec10-F024.question_text: What rule applies during a flashing orange don't-walk display?
sec10-card-sec10-F024.teaching_text: Flashing orange warns curb pedestrians to wait while giving people in the street time to clear.

sec10-card-sec10-F025.question_text: What does a walk signal or steady white walking-person symbol permit?
sec10-card-sec10-F025.teaching_text: Even with a white walk symbol, staying alert inside crosswalk lines prevents conflicts with turning cars.

sec10-card-sec10-F026.question_text: Which overhead displays and pavement stripes identify a reversible traffic lane?
sec10-card-sec10-F026.teaching_text: Double dashed yellow sidelines plus overhead lane signals mark lanes whose direction flips by time of day.

sec10-card-sec10-F027.question_text: When may you enter a reversible lane, and what if its overhead lane-control signals are dark?
sec10-card-sec10-F027.teaching_text: Entering an unlit reversible lane risks meeting oncoming commuters head-on without active direction control.

sec10-card-sec10-F028.question_text: Why must you stay out of a lane showing a steady red cross overhead?
sec10-card-sec10-F028.teaching_text: Driving underneath a red cross puts your vehicle directly into oncoming rush-hour flow.

sec10-card-sec10-F029.question_text: What action is required when a steady yellow cross illuminates over your reversible lane?
sec10-card-sec10-F029.teaching_text: Yellow cross signals an imminent direction switch, giving you brief time to merge out safely.

sec10-card-sec10-F030.question_text: What does a steady green downward arrow above a lane indicate?
sec10-card-sec10-F030.teaching_text: A green downward arrow confirms the lane beneath is open for your travel direction.

sec10-card-sec10-F031.question_text: Who else may enter a two-way left-turn lane, and how must you use it?
sec10-card-sec10-F031.teaching_text: Because oncoming left-turners share the same center strip, watch ahead closely and yield while turning.

sec10-card-sec10-F032.question_text: How does a one-way left-turn-only lane differ from a two-way center lane, and who still gets priority?
sec10-card-sec10-F032.teaching_text: Opposing cars cannot enter your dedicated pocket, yet oncoming straight traffic and walkers still hold right-of-way.

sec11-card-sec11-F001.question_text: What three functions do pavement markings serve, and what legal weight do they carry?
sec11-card-sec11-F001.teaching_text: Treating painted road lines as mere suggestions brings the exact same ticket risk as running signs.

sec11-card-sec11-F002.question_text: How do yellow pavement lines differ from white pavement lines in separating traffic?
sec11-card-sec11-F002.teaching_text: Glancing at stripe color tells you instantly whether neighboring lanes flow with you or head-on.

sec11-card-sec11-F003.question_text: How do dashed lines, solid white lines, and solid yellow lines compare in restrictiveness?
sec11-card-sec11-F003.teaching_text: Reading line continuity alongside color shows whether crossing is open, discouraged, or flatly barred.

sec11-card-sec11-F004.question_text: Is ordinary driving on the roadway shoulder allowed under Alaska pavement-marking rules?
sec11-card-sec11-F004.teaching_text: Using shoulders as extra travel or passing lanes strikes stopped breakdowns, pedestrians, and cyclists.

sec11-card-sec11-F005.question_text: What pavement symbol and roadside controls mark preferential bus or carpool lanes?
sec11-card-sec11-F005.teaching_text: Painted white diamonds paired with regulatory signs reserve high-occupancy lanes during posted hours.

sec11-card-sec11-F006.question_text: Which stripe color marks the left edge of a divided highway or one-way street?
sec11-card-sec11-F006.teaching_text: Keeping yellow on your left and white on your right confirms you are traveling the lawful way.

sec11-card-sec11-F007.question_text: What is a shared two-way left-turn center lane reserved for, and which three uses are barred?
sec11-card-sec11-F007.teaching_text: Through driving, accelerating, or passing inside a shared center turn lane causes head-on collisions.

sec11-card-sec11-F008.question_text: How does a reversible center lane operate during different times, and what must accompany it?
sec11-card-sec11-F008.teaching_text: Posted time signs or overhead lane signals prevent opposing rush-hour streams from entering together.

sec11-card-sec11-F009.question_text: What do dashed yellow centerline markings indicate on a two-lane, two-way road?
sec11-card-sec11-F009.teaching_text: Broken yellow paint marks zones with adequate sight distance once oncoming traffic is clear.

sec11-card-sec11-F010.question_text: What movement do solid yellow centerlines prohibit, and what crossing movement remains legal?
sec11-card-sec11-F010.teaching_text: DMV tests love checking whether drivers know solid yellow bars overtaking while allowing safe driveway turns.

sec11-card-sec11-F011.question_text: Which side of a divided roadway is marked by a single solid yellow edge line?
sec11-card-sec11-F011.teaching_text: Seeing solid yellow on your right instead of your left warns immediately of wrong-way entry.

sec11-card-sec11-F012.question_text: What do dashed white lane lines tell drivers traveling in the same direction?
sec11-card-sec11-F012.teaching_text: Broken white stripes separate standard multi-lane traffic where safe, signaled lane shifts are open.

sec11-card-sec11-F013.question_text: What does a solid white line between lanes indicate about lane use and changing lanes?
sec11-card-sec11-F013.teaching_text: Solid white channelizes turn pockets or bike buffers where weaving across invites side-swipe crashes.

sec11-card-sec11-F014.question_text: What roadside boundary can a solid white line mark, and what rule governs leaving the lane?
sec11-card-sec11-F014.teaching_text: Right-edge white paint guides night and fog tracking until pulling off the road is safe.

sec11-card-sec11-F015.question_text: What requirement applies once you occupy a lane marked with a directional pavement arrow?
sec11-card-sec11-F015.teaching_text: Driving straight from a turn-arrow lane cuts directly across adjacent turning or curbing traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-F016.question_text: How must you react to lane stencils warning of an upcoming school, rail track, or stop?
sec11-card-sec11-F016.teaching_text: Large lane stencils give advance notice before children, trains, or hidden stop lines appear.

sec11-card-sec11-F017.question_text: Which three roadway features are marked using white transverse lines painted across pavement?
sec11-card-sec11-F017.teaching_text: Crosswise white paint defines stopping thresholds, pedestrian corridors, and legal parking bays.

sec11-card-sec11-F018.question_text: What exact boundary does a white stop line set for an approaching vehicle?
sec11-card-sec11-F018.teaching_text: Creeping past the stop bar intrudes on crosswalks and wide truck turning paths.

sec11-card-sec11-F019.question_text: How must you position your vehicle where parking stalls are painted on pavement?
sec11-card-sec11-F019.teaching_text: Straddling stall stripes blocks adjacent spaces and crowds travel or fire lanes.

sec11-card-sec11-F020.question_text: Does a pedestrian lose intersection right-of-way when no crosswalk lines are painted?
sec11-card-sec11-F020.teaching_text: Crosswalk priority exists at every legal corner regardless of whether white stripes are painted.

sec11-card-sec11-F021.question_text: Who must yield when vehicles and pedestrians meet at marked crossings or intersections?
sec11-card-sec11-F021.teaching_text: Inching forward to pressure pedestrians back onto the curb violates right-of-way law.

sec11-card-sec11-F022.question_text: May you overtake on either side when a car halts at a crosswalk for walkers?
sec11-card-sec11-F022.teaching_text: The stopped car screens the crossing pedestrian from view until your bumper enters the crosswalk.

sec11-card-sec11-F023.question_text: What is the safe move after reaching a corner inside the wrong lane for your turn?
sec11-card-sec11-F023.teaching_text: Forcing a last-second turn or halting traffic to swap lanes causes intersection side-swipes.

sec11-card-sec11-F024.question_text: What must you check for before reversing direction with a U-turn?
sec11-card-sec11-F024.teaching_text: Busy corners and tight medians often post regulatory signs barring U-turns for rushing drivers.

sec11-card-sec11-F025.question_text: How should you approach a railroad crossbuck or advance railroad warning sign?
sec11-card-sec11-F025.teaching_text: Passive rural crossings lack gates or bells, so every crossbuck demands active train scanning.

sec11-card-sec11-F026.question_text: Where must you wait when heavy traffic backs up just past a railroad crossing?
sec11-card-sec11-F026.teaching_text: Entering without full room on the far side can trap your car across live rails.

sec11-card-sec11-F027.question_text: Why shouldn't you accelerate across multi-track rails the instant a train's caboose clears?
sec11-card-sec11-F027.teaching_text: A departing train can hide a second fast locomotive approaching from the opposite direction.

sec11-card-sec11-F028.question_text: May you zigzag around lowered railroad crossing gates if no train seems close?
sec11-card-sec11-F028.teaching_text: Trains look slower than their true speed, so wait until crossing arms rise completely.

sec11-card-sec11-F029.question_text: Why must you never try to race an approaching train to a crossing?
sec11-card-sec11-F029.teaching_text: Large locomotives create an optical illusion of low speed and cannot swerve or stop quickly.

sec11-card-sec11-F030.question_text: How should you handle gears in a manual-transmission car when crossing railroad tracks?
sec11-card-sec11-F030.teaching_text: Missing a gear or stalling the clutch midway leaves your car stranded across steel rails.

sec11-card-sec11-F031.question_text: Why should you leave extra buffer behind buses or certain heavy trucks approaching railroad tracks?
sec11-card-sec11-F031.teaching_text: School buses and hazmat tankers must stop at crossings even when warning lights stay dark.

sec11-card-sec11-F032.question_text: Under what strict conditions is overtaking another vehicle near a railroad crossing allowed?
sec11-card-sec11-F032.teaching_text: Most rail approaches ban passing outright, and blind track sightlines turn overtaking lethal.

sec11-card-sec11-F033.question_text: Within what train distance does the Alaska handbook tell you to prepare to stop, even at unmarked crossings?
sec11-card-sec11-F033.teaching_text: A freight train fifteen hundred feet out closes on an unmarked crossing in mere seconds.

sec11-card-sec11-F034.question_text: What is your immediate first priority if your car stalls on railroad tracks and warning lights start flashing?
sec11-card-sec11-F034.teaching_text: No vehicle or cargo is worth losing lives when an approaching train triggers crossing bells.

sec11-card-sec11-F035.question_text: Which direction must you run after evacuating a car stuck on tracks, and when do you dial nine-one-one?
sec11-card-sec11-F035.teaching_text: Running away from tracks toward the oncoming train dodges flying wreckage flung forward on impact.

sec11-card-sec11-F036.question_text: How soon after railroad warning lights activate can a train strike the crossing?
sec11-card-sec11-F036.teaching_text: Twenty seconds leaves zero margin to restart an engine or gather belongings before impact.

sec11-card-sec11-F037.question_text: What must you do if your car stalls on tracks before lights flash or at an unlit crossing?
sec11-card-sec11-F037.teaching_text: Getting everyone clear first and alerting both dispatchers gives rail crews a chance to halt trains.

sec11-card-sec11-F038.question_text: Which four details should you state when reporting a vehicle stuck on railroad tracks?
sec11-card-sec11-F038.teaching_text: Giving the exact crossing identifier and clearly stating tracks are blocked triggers immediate train stops.

sec11-card-sec11-F039.question_text: What color is the railroad emergency-notification sign, and where is it posted?
sec11-card-sec11-F039.teaching_text: Knowing to check the crossbuck post for the blue plaque saves critical seconds during a stall.

sec11-card-sec11-F040.question_text: Whom does the crossing's emergency-notification phone number reach?
sec11-card-sec11-F040.teaching_text: Direct rail dispatch contact radios engineers far faster than relaying solely through local offices.

sec11-card-sec11-F041.question_text: What does the transportation-department number printed below the railroad dispatch phone identify?
sec11-card-sec11-F041.teaching_text: Unique crossing codes eliminate guesswork on rural stretches where landmarks look identical.

sec11-card-sec11-F042.question_text: Which four hazards should you report using the railroad emergency-notification system?
sec11-card-sec11-F042.teaching_text: Reporting stuck gates, stalled cars, or track hazards prevents derailments and crossing tragedies.
sec11-card-sec11-F042.must_match_memory_hook: Broken gates, blocked tracks, trespassers, hazards

visual_sync.text_span: Broken gates, blocked tracks, trespassers, hazards

sec11-card-sec11-F043.question_text: How do the emergency phone and location ID on the blue crossing sign work together?
sec11-card-sec11-F043.teaching_text: Pairing direct dispatch contact with a unique site ID sends emergency and rail staff straight there.

sec12-card-sec12-F001.question_text: Why does nighttime driving carry a higher fatal-crash rate per mile than daytime travel?
sec12-card-sec12-F001.teaching_text: Seeing far less width and distance at night cuts your time to spot hazards ahead.

sec12-card-sec12-F002.question_text: What does the term glare recovery mean in night driving?
sec12-card-sec12-F002.teaching_text: For several seconds after bright oncoming beams pass, your pupils stay constricted in temporary blindness.

sec12-card-sec12-F003.question_text: How does glare recovery differ across drivers, and which groups often find it harder?
sec12-card-sec12-F003.teaching_text: Aging eyes and certain medical conditions lengthen recovery seconds after bright oncoming headlights pass.

sec12-card-sec12-F004.question_text: What maintenance on lights and glass is essential before driving at night?
sec12-card-sec12-F004.teaching_text: Road film scatters oncoming light across dirty glass while crusted lenses starve your forward beam.

sec12-card-sec12-F005.question_text: What two visual mistakes must you avoid against oncoming headlights at night?
sec12-card-sec12-F005.teaching_text: Staring straight into bright lamps bleaches night vision, while dark lenses hide unlit roadside hazards.

sec12-card-sec12-F006.question_text: How can tinted windshields or front side windows affect night driving, and what rule governs them?
sec12-card-sec12-F006.teaching_text: Dark front film dims faint pedestrians after sunset, so glass must meet legal tint limits.

sec12-card-sec12-F007.question_text: Why is off-road-only auxiliary lighting banned on public roadways?
sec12-card-sec12-F007.teaching_text: Unshielded trail light bars scatter blinding glare directly into oncoming commuters' eyes on public roads.

sec12-card-sec12-F008.question_text: How does alcohol affect driving sharpness, and what precaution applies to medications?
sec12-card-sec12-F008.teaching_text: Even small amounts slow reactions and dim vision, while prescriptions can add hidden drowsiness.

sec12-card-sec12-F009.question_text: Which two lighting items does the Alaska handbook recommend carrying in your vehicle?
sec12-card-sec12-F009.teaching_text: Having a working flashlight and roadside flares protects you if your electrical system dies at night.

sec12-card-sec12-F010.question_text: Between what sunset and sunrise times must your headlights be turned on?
sec12-card-sec12-F010.teaching_text: Half an hour after sunset until half an hour before sunrise marks Alaska's mandatory night-beam window.

sec12-card-sec12-F011.question_text: At what visibility distance must you switch headlights on during daytime fog, rain, snow, smoke, or dust?
sec12-card-sec12-F011.teaching_text: Gray spray, smoke, or blowing snow hides unlit cars well inside a thousand feet.

sec12-card-sec12-F012.question_text: At least how many feet before meeting an oncoming vehicle must you dim high beams?
sec12-card-sec12-F012.teaching_text: Dropping to low beams at five hundred feet prevents blinding the driver approaching your lane.

sec12-card-sec12-F013.question_text: At least how many feet behind a vehicle ahead must you switch from high beams to low beams?
sec12-card-sec12-F013.teaching_text: High beams inside three hundred feet bounce blinding glare off the lead driver's mirrors.

sec12-card-sec12-F014.question_text: When is it legal to drive using parking lights alone?
sec12-card-sec12-F014.teaching_text: Parking lamps mark stationary cars only and never substitute for headlights day or night.

sec12-card-sec12-F015.question_text: How does switching headlights on at dusk or in poor daytime weather help safety?
sec12-card-sec12-F015.teaching_text: Even when you still see pavement fine at dusk, lit headlamps help oncoming drivers spot your car.

sec12-card-sec12-F016.question_text: Which headlight beam setting should you use in rain, fog, snow, or dust?
sec12-card-sec12-F016.teaching_text: High beams reflect straight off airborne droplets, flakes, and dust into a blinding white wall.

sec12-card-sec12-F017.question_text: Among which four reference points should you shift quick glances when meeting oncoming headlights at night?
sec12-card-sec12-F017.teaching_text: Cycling quick glances keeps your car centered and tracks hazards without staring into bright beams.

sec12-card-sec12-F018.question_text: Because sustained high-speed driving builds engine heat, which four under-hood items need frequent checks?
sec12-card-sec12-F018.teaching_text: Catching low coolant, worn hoses, or a loose belt early prevents remote Alaska highway breakdowns.

sec12-card-sec12-F019.question_text: Why must your tires be rated and maintained for high-speed highway travel?
sec12-card-sec12-F019.teaching_text: Weak, underinflated, or worn casings overheat at highway speed and risk sudden blowout loss of control.

sec12-card-sec12-F020.question_text: What lights should you activate when broken down, and what nighttime crash risk demands special alertness?
sec12-card-sec12-F020.teaching_text: Drowsy night drivers can lock onto taillights and drift onto shoulders into stopped breakdowns.

sec12-card-sec12-F021.question_text: Where should you position a disabled vehicle whenever possible?
sec12-card-sec12-F021.teaching_text: Rolling every tire clear of active lanes eliminates high-speed strikes from passing traffic.

sec12-card-sec12-F022.question_text: How can you visually signal vehicle trouble to passing motorists or troopers?
sec12-card-sec12-F022.teaching_text: Popping the hood or tying white cloth on the left handle or antenna signals distress clearly.

sec12-card-sec12-F023.question_text: How quickly must a disabled vehicle be removed from the roadside?
sec12-card-sec12-F023.teaching_text: Abandoned roadside cars remain collision hazards and interfere with snowplows and highway crews.

sec12-card-sec12-F024.question_text: What must you do as soon as you feel drowsy behind the wheel?
sec12-card-sec12-F024.teaching_text: Willpower cannot stop microsleeps once fatigue sets in, so pull off somewhere safe to rest.

sec12-card-sec12-F025.question_text: How should you move your eyes to prevent highway staring on long drives?
sec12-card-sec12-F025.teaching_text: Alternating side scans with near-and-far focus keeps your visual brain alert and engaged.

sec12-card-sec12-F026.question_text: What cabin temperature habit and mileage break interval does the Alaska handbook recommend?
sec12-card-sec12-F026.teaching_text: Warm cabin air breeds drowsiness, while stepping outside every hundred miles restores fresh alertness.

sec12-card-sec12-F027.question_text: When must you drive slower than the posted maximum speed limit?
sec12-card-sec12-F027.teaching_text: Posted numbers assume ideal dry pavement, never glare ice, heavy rain, or congested packs.

sec12-card-sec12-F028.question_text: On Alaska roads covered by the slow-vehicle pull-over rule, how many trailing cars trigger a mandatory safe turnout?
sec12-card-sec12-F028.teaching_text: Letting five or more queued vehicles pass at the first safe turnout prevents risky two-lane overtaking.

sec12-card-sec12-F029.question_text: How does driving at higher highway speeds affect tires and fuel consumption?
sec12-card-sec12-F029.teaching_text: Aerodynamic drag and tread friction climb steeply at high speed, draining gas and tire life.

sec12-card-sec12-F030.question_text: What danger comes from prolonged travel along monotonous highway stretches?
sec12-card-sec12-F030.teaching_text: Unchanging scenery lulls drivers into highway hypnosis, slowing reactions when a hazard suddenly appears.

sec12-card-sec12-F031.question_text: What two visual checks must precede every lane change?
sec12-card-sec12-F031.teaching_text: Mirrors alone miss vehicles riding beside your rear quarter until you glance over your shoulder.

sec12-card-sec12-F032.question_text: Why shouldn't you linger alongside another vehicle's rear fenders?
sec12-card-sec12-F032.teaching_text: Cruising in someone's rear-quarter blind pocket invites a side-swipe if they drift or merge.

sec12-card-sec12-F033.question_text: What minimum following-time cushion does the Alaska handbook recommend on high-speed roads?
sec12-card-sec12-F033.teaching_text: Fast highway velocities multiply stopping distance, requiring four full seconds to avoid pileups.

sec12-card-sec12-F034.question_text: What mental trap develops when following the same group of vehicles for a long time?
sec12-card-sec12-F034.teaching_text: Getting too comfortable behind familiar taillights delays braking when the lead car slams stops.

sec12-card-sec12-F035.question_text: Which lane rule governs slower vehicles, and what is forbidden while being overtaken?
sec12-card-sec12-F035.teaching_text: Speeding up while someone passes strands the overtaking car in conflicting lanes.

sec12-card-sec12-F036.question_text: Which two steering errors must you avoid when passing at highway speed?
sec12-card-sec12-F036.teaching_text: Sharp swerves upset high-speed tire grip, and cutting back early clips the overtaken bumper.

sec12-card-sec12-F037.question_text: Why might sounding your horn right beside a large truck fail to alert its driver?
sec12-card-sec12-F037.teaching_text: Heavy diesel cab roar and trailer length create acoustic dead zones where car horns vanish.

sec12-card-sec12-F038.question_text: What full five-part sequence makes a highway lane change safe?
sec12-card-sec12-F038.teaching_text: Rechecking after signaling and steering gradually prevents colliding with another car entering the gap.

sec12-card-sec12-F039.question_text: How should you use a freeway entrance acceleration lane before merging?
sec12-card-sec12-F039.teaching_text: Matching mainline flow on the ramp lets you slot smoothly into gaps without forcing brake slams.

sec12-card-sec12-F040.question_text: Who holds right-of-way at a freeway merge, and what must you account for if forced to stop?
sec12-card-sec12-F040.teaching_text: Mainline traffic holds priority, while sudden ramp stops require watching trailing mergers in mirrors.

sec12-card-sec12-F041.question_text: When exiting an expressway, when should you begin slowing down?
sec12-card-sec12-F041.teaching_text: Braking early inside fast through lanes triggers chain-reaction rear-end crashes behind you.

sec12-card-sec12-F042.question_text: What is the only safe option if you miss your intended freeway exit?
sec12-card-sec12-F042.teaching_text: Backing along a high-speed freeway shoulder or ramp invites lethal head-on or rear-end impacts.

sec12-card-sec12-F043.question_text: Why must you keep moving forward even after accidentally taking the wrong freeway exit?
sec12-card-sec12-F043.teaching_text: Drivers exiting right behind you at highway speed expect continuous flow down the ramp.

sec12-card-sec12-F044.question_text: When is stopping or parking allowed anywhere along freeway pavement, shoulders, or right-of-way?
sec12-card-sec12-F044.teaching_text: Routine map checks or phone stops on freeway shoulders expose occupants to seventy-mile-per-hour drift.

sec12-card-sec12-F045.question_text: Which turns are legal on a highway or controlled-access freeway?
sec12-card-sec12-F045.teaching_text: Cutting across unpaved medians or police-only crossovers puts slow cars squarely into fast lanes.

sec12-card-sec12-F046.question_text: Do headlight-dimming laws still apply when driving on a divided highway?
sec12-card-sec12-F046.teaching_text: High beams still dazzle oncoming eyes across medians, so divided highways carry full dimming rules.

sec15-card-sec15-F001.question_text: What license-plate and tab setup must noncommercial registered vehicles display in Alaska?
sec15-card-sec15-F001.teaching_text: Driving with expired month or year stickers on your rear plate invites an immediate equipment stop.
sec15-card-sec15-F001.must_match_memory_hook: One rear plate, current month-year tabs

visual_sync.text_span: One rear plate, current month-year tabs

sec15-card-sec15-F002.question_text: What general standard applies to required vehicle equipment and passenger seating positions?
sec15-card-sec15-F002.teaching_text: Having parts bolted on is not enough if lamps sit misaimed or seats lack working belts.
sec15-card-sec15-F002.must_match_memory_hook: Working adjusted gear, belts every seat

visual_sync.text_span: Working adjusted gear, belts every seat

sec15-card-sec15-F003.question_text: How many headlights does a motor vehicle need, and where must they be mounted?
sec15-card-sec15-F003.teaching_text: Driving on one working headlamp makes oncoming traffic mistake your car's width for a motorcycle.
sec15-card-sec15-F003.must_match_memory_hook: Two headlights mounted opposite front sides

visual_sync.text_span: Two headlights mounted opposite front sides

sec15-card-sec15-F004.question_text: How many working taillights and foot-activated brake lights are required on the rear of a vehicle?
sec15-card-sec15-F004.teaching_text: Trailing motorists rely on paired red lamps and foot-brake glow to judge nighttime closing speed.
sec15-card-sec15-F004.must_match_memory_hook: Two red taillights, two brake lights

visual_sync.text_span: Two red taillights, two brake lights

sec15-card-sec15-F005.question_text: When equipped with a rear plate light, what color and readability distance must it meet?
sec15-card-sec15-F005.teaching_text: Colored novelty bulbs or dim plate lamps violate Alaska's fifty-foot white illumination standard.
sec15-card-sec15-F005.must_match_memory_hook: White light readable from fifty feet

visual_sync.text_span: White light readable from fifty feet

sec15-card-sec15-F006.question_text: What equipment standard applies to directional turn signals on a vehicle?
sec15-card-sec15-F006.teaching_text: Burned-out blinkers leave cross traffic guessing your next move at winter intersections and lane changes.
sec15-card-sec15-F006.must_match_memory_hook: Turn signals installed and working properly

visual_sync.text_span: Turn signals installed and working properly

sec15-card-sec15-F007.question_text: Within how many feet must a passenger car's foot brake stop from twenty miles per hour?
sec15-card-sec15-F007.teaching_text: Memorize twenty-five feet from twenty miles per hour because equipment questions love pairing both numbers.
sec15-card-sec15-F007.must_match_memory_hook: Stop within twenty-five feet from twenty

visual_sync.text_span: Stop within twenty-five feet from twenty

sec15-card-sec15-F008.question_text: What performance standard must the emergency or parking brake satisfy?
sec15-card-sec15-F008.teaching_text: A stretched cable that lets your parked car creep downhill fails basic mechanical safety rules.
sec15-card-sec15-F008.must_match_memory_hook: Hold the vehicle stationary on grades

visual_sync.text_span: Hold the vehicle stationary on grades

sec15-card-sec15-F009.question_text: What glass and visibility requirements apply to windshields and original or replacement windows?
sec15-card-sec15-F009.teaching_text: Tempered or laminated safety glass resists jagged shattering while keeping driver sightlines clear.
sec15-card-sec15-F009.must_match_memory_hook: Required windshield, safety glass, clear vision

visual_sync.text_span: Required windshield, safety glass, clear vision

sec15-card-sec15-F010.question_text: What rule governs aftermarket or factory window tint on Alaska vehicles?
sec15-card-sec15-F010.teaching_text: Excessively dark tint blocks nighttime side visibility and violates state light-transmission limits.
sec15-card-sec15-F010.must_match_memory_hook: Window tint must meet legal limits

visual_sync.text_span: Window tint must meet legal limits

sec15-card-sec15-F011.question_text: Which two systems are required to keep rain, snow, and frost off the windshield?
sec15-card-sec15-F011.teaching_text: Alaska storms ice over glass rapidly, making both exterior wipers and interior defrosters mandatory.
sec15-card-sec15-F011.must_match_memory_hook: Working windshield wipers plus a defroster

visual_sync.text_span: Working windshield wipers plus a defroster

sec15-card-sec15-F012.question_text: From how far away must a horn be heard normally, and what sounds are forbidden?
sec15-card-sec15-F012.teaching_text: Your horn must warn traffic two hundred feet ahead without mimicking sirens, whistles, or startling blasts.
sec15-card-sec15-F012.must_match_memory_hook: Two hundred feet, no whistles, blasts

visual_sync.text_span: Two hundred feet, no whistles, blasts

sec15-card-sec15-F013.question_text: Which mirror combination satisfies Alaska's standard rear-viewing requirement?
sec15-card-sec15-F013.teaching_text: Every driver needs a left exterior mirror paired with at least one inside or right-side mirror.
sec15-card-sec15-F013.must_match_memory_hook: Left mirror plus inside or right

visual_sync.text_span: Left mirror plus inside or right

sec15-card-sec15-F014.question_text: Which mirrors are required whenever cargo, trailers, or bodywork obstruct the rear-window view?
sec15-card-sec15-F014.teaching_text: Once cargo blocks the center mirror, right-side traffic disappears without a working right-side exterior mirror.
sec15-card-sec15-F014.must_match_memory_hook: Blocked rear window requires both sides

visual_sync.text_span: Blocked rear window requires both sides

sec15-card-sec15-F015.question_text: What must fenders, mud flaps, or body design accomplish behind the wheels?
sec15-card-sec15-F015.teaching_text: Uncovered tires fling blinding slush and gravel straight onto windshields directly behind you.
sec15-card-sec15-F015.must_match_memory_hook: Fenders or flaps cut wheel spray

visual_sync.text_span: Fenders or flaps cut wheel spray

sec15-card-sec15-F016.question_text: May lamps labeled strictly for off-road operation be used as roadway lighting?
sec15-card-sec15-F016.teaching_text: Unshielded off-road light bars lack highway beam cutoffs and blind oncoming drivers instantly.
sec15-card-sec15-F016.must_match_memory_hook: Never run off-road lamps on highways

visual_sync.text_span: Never run off-road lamps on highways

sec15-card-sec15-F017.question_text: When should a driver sound the vehicle's horn?
sec15-card-sec15-F017.teaching_text: Honking out of impatience startles nearby pedestrians and dilutes genuine collision warnings.
sec15-card-sec15-F017.must_match_memory_hook: Sound horn only for safe operation

visual_sync.text_span: Sound horn only for safe operation

sec15-card-sec15-F018.question_text: What exhaust component must stay in continuous working order, and why?
sec15-card-sec15-F018.teaching_text: Rusted-out or missing mufflers create illegal noise and can leak exhaust fumes underneath the cabin.
sec15-card-sec15-F018.must_match_memory_hook: Working muffler prevents excessive exhaust noise

visual_sync.text_span: Working muffler prevents excessive exhaust noise

sec15-card-sec15-F019.question_text: Are muffler cutouts, bypasses, or similar devices legal to use on a highway?
sec15-card-sec15-F019.teaching_text: Routing exhaust around the muffler defeats noise suppression and violates Alaska highway equipment law.
sec15-card-sec15-F019.must_match_memory_hook: No muffler cutouts or highway bypasses

visual_sync.text_span: No muffler cutouts or highway bypasses

sec15-card-sec15-F020.question_text: Which mechanical, lighting, and snow-clearing tools are suggested as emergency vehicle equipment?
sec15-card-sec15-F020.teaching_text: Packing jumper cables, flares, winter wipers, chains, and scrapers keeps minor winter stalls manageable.
sec15-card-sec15-F020.must_match_memory_hook: Cables, light, flares, traction, snow tools

visual_sync.text_span: Cables, light, flares, traction, snow tools

sec15-card-sec15-F021.question_text: Which seven personal survival and dig-out items belong in the recommended Alaska emergency kit?
sec15-card-sec15-F021.teaching_text: Subzero delays far from town turn life-threatening without warm layers, boots, blankets, food, and dig-out gear.
sec15-card-sec15-F021.must_match_memory_hook: First aid, warmth, sand, shovel, food

visual_sync.text_span: First aid, warmth, sand, shovel, food

sec15-card-sec15-F022.question_text: Which three traits make carbon monoxide in vehicle exhaust especially dangerous?
sec15-card-sec15-F022.teaching_text: Because you can neither see nor smell carbon monoxide, cabin leaks incapacitate occupants without warning.
sec15-card-sec15-F022.must_match_memory_hook: Poisonous, colorless, and completely odorless gas

visual_sync.text_span: Poisonous, colorless, and completely odorless gas

sec15-card-sec15-F023.question_text: Which four physical symptoms can signal carbon-monoxide poisoning?
sec15-card-sec15-F023.teaching_text: Treating sudden cabin headaches, dizziness, or nausea as mere motion sickness risks fatal unconsciousness.
sec15-card-sec15-F023.must_match_memory_hook: Headache, dizziness, nausea, and sudden vomiting

visual_sync.text_span: Headache, dizziness, nausea, and sudden vomiting

sec15-card-sec15-F024.question_text: What two precautions prevent carbon-monoxide exposure inside a vehicle?
sec15-card-sec15-F024.teaching_text: Fixing exhaust leaks and cracking vents for fresh outside airflow keep cabin air breathable.
sec15-card-sec15-F024.must_match_memory_hook: Sound exhaust plus fresh-air cabin circulation

visual_sync.text_span: Sound exhaust plus fresh-air cabin circulation

sec15-card-sec15-F025.question_text: What is the rule on warming or running an engine inside an enclosed garage?
sec15-card-sec15-F025.teaching_text: Concentrated exhaust fills a closed garage within minutes and seeps into attached living spaces.
sec15-card-sec15-F025.must_match_memory_hook: Never run engines inside enclosed garages

visual_sync.text_span: Never run engines inside enclosed garages

sec15-card-sec15-F026.question_text: Why does the handbook warn against sitting parked with windows shut while running heat or air conditioning?
sec15-card-sec15-F026.teaching_text: Stationary tailpipe fumes can pool beneath the chassis and get drawn through cabin climate vents.
sec15-card-sec15-F026.must_match_memory_hook: Avoid closed-window idling with climate on

visual_sync.text_span: Avoid closed-window idling with climate on

sec15-card-sec15-F027.question_text: What immediate emergency step should you take for someone exposed to carbon monoxide?
sec15-card-sec15-F027.teaching_text: Getting the person out of the contaminated cabin into clean outside air immediately halts further inhalation.
sec15-card-sec15-F027.must_match_memory_hook: Move exposed victims into fresh air

visual_sync.text_span: Move exposed victims into fresh air

sec15-card-sec15-F028.question_text: How do large trucks and buses compare with passenger cars when accelerating, slowing, or stopping?
sec15-card-sec15-F028.teaching_text: Massive weight stretches both acceleration onto highways and braking distance toward red lights.
sec15-card-sec15-F028.must_match_memory_hook: Big rigs need extra time, space

visual_sync.text_span: Big rigs need extra time, space

sec15-card-sec15-F029.question_text: What three handling and visibility limitations apply to large vehicles?
sec15-card-sec15-F029.teaching_text: Expecting nimble car-like swerves or tight corner turns around buses and semis sets up collisions.
sec15-card-sec15-F029.must_match_memory_hook: Huge blind spots, wide turns, stiff

visual_sync.text_span: Huge blind spots, wide turns, stiff

sec15-card-sec15-F030.question_text: Where are the blind spots that make up a truck's or bus's no-zone?
sec15-card-sec15-F030.teaching_text: Drivers often watch only side flanks and forget huge blind pockets directly ahead and behind.
sec15-card-sec15-F030.must_match_memory_hook: No-zones surround front, rear, both sides

visual_sync.text_span: No-zones surround front, rear, both sides

sec15-card-sec15-F031.question_text: How can you tell instantly whether a truck or bus driver can see your vehicle?
sec15-card-sec15-F031.teaching_text: Losing sight of the driver's face in those tall side mirrors proves you sit hidden inside a blind spot.
sec15-card-sec15-F031.must_match_memory_hook: Cannot see driver's mirror, stay unseen

visual_sync.text_span: Cannot see driver's mirror, stay unseen

sec15-card-sec15-F032.question_text: Why must you never dart into the open space a truck leaves ahead of its front bumper?
sec15-card-sec15-F032.teaching_text: That open gap is survival braking room, not an invitation to cut in and brake.
sec15-card-sec15-F032.must_match_memory_hook: Never steal a truck's stopping cushion

visual_sync.text_span: Never steal a truck's stopping cushion

sec15-card-sec15-F033.question_text: At fifty-five miles per hour, how does a car's stopping distance compare with a large truck's?
sec15-card-sec15-F033.teaching_text: A semi needs roughly triple a passenger car's stopping room at highway cruising speed.

sec15-card-sec15-F034.question_text: When is it safe to merge back ahead of a truck you just passed, and how should you hold speed?
sec15-card-sec15-F034.teaching_text: Wait until the entire front grille fills your rearview mirror, then keep pace without sudden braking.
sec15-card-sec15-F034.must_match_memory_hook: Full cab in mirror, hold speed

visual_sync.text_span: Full cab in mirror, hold speed

sec15-card-sec15-F035.question_text: What three forward hazards get hidden when you follow a large truck too closely?
sec15-card-sec15-F035.teaching_text: Riding right behind tall trailer doors blinds you to stalled cars or road debris until impact.
sec15-card-sec15-F035.must_match_memory_hook: Hides traffic shifts, debris, crashes ahead

sec15-card-sec15-F036.question_text: How should your following distance behind a large truck compare with following a passenger car?
sec15-card-sec15-F036.teaching_text: Backing off opens wide sightlines past the trailer and keeps you out of rear blind zones.
sec15-card-sec15-F036.must_match_memory_hook: Leave wider space behind large trucks

visual_sync.text_span: Leave wider space behind large trucks

sec15-card-sec15-F037.question_text: How can a truck's rear bumper differ dangerously from a passenger car's bumper in a collision?
sec15-card-sec15-F037.teaching_text: High, rigid trailer frames do not match car bumper heights or crumple softly during rear-end impacts.

sec15-card-sec15-F038.question_text: Why might a truck swing left first, and what mistake must you never make beside the curb?

sec15-card-sec15-F039.question_text: How should you respond when a large truck signals a turn or maneuver?
sec15-card-sec15-F039.teaching_text: Giving turning trucks generous maneuvering space keeps your car clear of sweeping trailers and blind zones.

sec17-card-sec17-F001.question_text: Which five vehicle items should you inspect at least once a month for safety maintenance?

sec17-card-sec17-F002.question_text: How do you perform the penny tread test, and what result shows the tires need replacement?

sec17-card-sec17-F003.question_text: How should you measure tire pressure, and where is the target pressure printed?
sec17-card-sec17-F003.teaching_text: Eyeballing modern radial sidewalls misses dangerous underinflation that only a pressure gauge and door-jamb sticker catch.

sec17-card-sec17-F004.question_text: At what tire temperature should pressure be checked, and what if the reading is too high?
sec17-card-sec17-F004.teaching_text: Driving heats internal air and inflates readings, while overinflated cold tires lose grip and ride harshly.

sec17-card-sec17-F005.question_text: What two-person method does the handbook describe for checking brake lights?

sec17-card-sec17-F006.question_text: Which two parts commonly cause a dead brake light, and what if you cannot fix it yourself?

sec17-card-sec17-F007.question_text: How often does the handbook advise replacing wiper blades across hot, cold, sunny, or dry climates?
sec17-card-sec17-F007.teaching_text: Brittle rubber streaks sleet and glare across windshields, especially where dry dust wears blades twice as fast.

sec17-card-sec17-F008.question_text: What simple cleaning step helps keep windshield wiper blades wiping cleanly?

sec17-card-sec17-F009.teaching_text: Skipping the wipe-and-reinsert step reads splashed crankcase oil instead of the true sump oil line.

sec17-card-sec17-F010.question_text: When should you add engine oil, and where do you find the right oil-change schedule?

sec17-card-sec17-F011.question_text: How do you inspect and top off engine coolant safely?
sec17-card-sec17-F011.teaching_text: Pure water freezes in Alaska winters, so always top the reservoir with the manual's coolant-and-water blend.

sec17-card-sec17-F012.question_text: Why must you never open a radiator cap while the engine is hot?

sec17-card-sec17-F013.question_text: What two roadside problems can result from hauling an uncovered or unsecured load?

sec17-card-sec17-F015.question_text: What maximum dollar fine and jail term can apply to littering in Alaska?
sec17-card-sec17-F015.teaching_text: Dropping trash or loose cargo carries criminal-scale exposure reaching one thousand dollars and ninety days.

sec17-card-sec17-F016.question_text: Besides fines and jail, what cleanup duty may a court order for a littering offender?

sec18-card-sec18-F001.question_text: How does the Alaska handbook classify driving, and what does that place on every motorist?
